1//! Parser for Cassandra 5.0 V5CompressedLegacy decompressed blocks
2//!
3//! This format uses **u8 length prefixes** (NOT VInt) for partition keys and strings,
4//! and simplified encoding optimized for compression. This differs from the newer
5//! V5_0NewBig and V5_0Bti formats which use pure VInt encoding.
6//!
7//! ## Partition Key Size Constraints
8//!
9//! **Apache Cassandra Specification**: Partition keys can be up to 64KB (65536 bytes).
10//! **V5CompressedLegacy Format Limitation**: Uses u8 for key length field, limiting keys to 255 bytes max.
11//!
12//! This means V5CompressedLegacy format cannot represent partition keys larger than 255 bytes,
13//! even though Cassandra allows keys up to 64KB. Tables with larger keys would use a different format.
14//!
15//! Based on format research in docs/V5_COMPRESSED_LEGACY_FORMAT_SPEC.md
16//!
17//! ## Format Structure
18//!
19//! ```text
20//! Decompressed Block:
21//! ├─ [0x00] Partition flags (u8)
22//! ├─ [0x01] Partition key length (u8, NOT VInt)
23//! ├─ [0x02..] Raw partition key bytes
24//! ├─ [+0] Partition deletion time (i32 big-endian)
25//! ├─ [+4] Unknown 8-byte field
26//! ├─ [+8] Row data begins
27//! │  ├─ Row header (flags, timestamp, row_size)
28//! │  ├─ Cells:
29//! │  │  ├─ Type tag or flags (u8)
30//! │  │  ├─ Column name length (u8)
31//! │  │  ├─ Column name bytes
32//! │  │  ├─ Value length (varies)
33//! │  │  └─ Value bytes
34//! │  └─ Trailing 4-byte field (NOT included in row_size)
35//! └─ [Next partition or end of block]
36//! ```
37

53/// Maximum reasonable size for frozen collections to prevent DoS from corrupted data.
54/// Cassandra collections are limited by max_collection_size_in_mb (default 64MB) and
55/// column_value_size_warn_threshold (default 64KB warning), but we use a conservative
56/// element count limit to prevent memory exhaustion from malicious/corrupted data.
57const MAX_FROZEN_COLLECTION_SIZE: u64 = 100_000;
58
59/// Maximum cell path/value length in bytes to prevent overflow on corrupted data.
60/// Issue #225: Linux CI fails with SIGABRT due to unsafe `as usize` casts on large values.
61/// Cassandra's column_value_size_warn_threshold defaults to 64KB; we use 64MB as generous limit.
62const MAX_CELL_VALUE_LENGTH: u64 = 64 * 1024 * 1024;
63
64/// Maximum number of fields allowed in a UDT to prevent memory exhaustion.
65/// This is a safety limit; real-world UDTs rarely exceed 100 fields.
66const MAX_UDT_FIELD_COUNT: usize = 1000;
67
68/// Maximum nesting depth for type definitions to prevent stack overflow.
69/// This covers recursive UDTs and deeply nested collections (e.g., list<list<list<...>>>).
70const MAX_TYPE_NESTING_DEPTH: usize = 10;

72/// Return type for `parse_row_data_with_offset`:
73/// (cells, cell_metadata, row_header, next_offset, is_static, complex_col_meta)
74///
75/// `cell_metadata` maps column name → `CellWriteMetadata` for every live cell
76/// parsed in this row.  It is `Some(map)` only when `want_cell_metadata == true`
77/// was passed to the function; otherwise it is `None` and zero allocations are
78/// incurred on the normal read hot-path.  Used to surface per-cell timestamps /
79/// TTLs for `WRITETIME(col)` / `TTL(col)` queries (issue #693).
80///
81/// `complex_col_meta` maps column name → `ComplexColumnMeta` for every
82/// non-frozen collection column parsed in this row (Issue #700, DS4).  It is
83/// always `Some` when `want_cell_metadata == true` and the row contains
84/// collection columns; always `None` when `want_cell_metadata == false`.
85type ParsedRow = (
86    HashMap<String, Value>,
87    Option<HashMap<String, CellWriteMetadata>>,
88    Option<RowHeader>,
89    usize,
90    bool,
91    Option<HashMap<String, ComplexColumnMeta>>,
92);
93
94/// Return type for [`V5CompressedLegacy::parse_block_with_cell_metadata`].
95///
96/// Each element is `(table_id, row_key, value_map, cell_metadata_map)`.
97type ParsedBlockWithMeta = Vec<(TableId, RowKey, Value, HashMap<String, CellWriteMetadata>)>;

99/// Per-column complex-element capture for the compaction read path (epic #899).
100///
101/// Maps a complex (non-frozen collection / UDT) column name to its optional
102/// complex deletion `(markedForDeleteAt µs, localDeletionTime s)` plus the
103/// per-element cells in on-disk order. Populated by `parse_row_data_with_offset`
104/// only when the caller passes a `Some(&mut _)` collector (the compaction path);
105/// `None` on every user-facing read path.
106type CompactionComplexColumns = HashMap<
107    String,
108    (
109        Option<(i64, i32)>,
110        Vec<crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::ComplexElement>,
111        // The whole-collection collapsed `Value` (epic #899 Phase A neutrality:
112        // the merge OUTPUT path replays this byte-identically to pre-Phase-A).
113        Value,
114    ),
115>;
116
117/// Outcome of [`V5CompressedLegacyParser::parse_one_partition_with_timestamps`].
118///
119/// The sliding-window compaction-read driver (issue #827) feeds the parser a
120/// `data` slice that grows as decompressed chunks are appended and shrinks as
121/// confirmed partitions are drained. Because a single partition can straddle a
122/// compression-chunk boundary, the bounded parser must distinguish "I parsed a
123/// complete partition" from "I ran out of buffer mid-partition and need more
124/// bytes" — conflating the two would silently drop trailing partitions.
125#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
126pub enum ParseStep {
127    /// A full partition was parsed; `usize` bytes of `data` were consumed and
128    /// can be drained from the front of the sliding window.
129    Emitted(usize),
130    /// `data` appears truncated mid-partition. The caller should append the
131    /// next decompressed chunk and retry. Only returned when `!at_final_chunk`.
132    NeedMore,
133    /// Genuine end of partitions in `data` (no more bytes to consume).
134    Done,
135}

137/// Row header data extracted from V5CompressedLegacy row
138#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
139struct RowHeader {
140    /// Row-level timestamp (after delta decoding from min_timestamp)
141    timestamp: Option<i64>,
142    /// Row-level TTL (after delta decoding from min_ttl)
143    ttl: Option<i32>,
144    /// Liveness local deletion time in SECONDS: absolute epoch-second expiry for a
145    /// TTL-bearing INSERT row (the `pk_liveness.ttl()` clock, from `HAS_TTL`).
146    /// This is the `expires_at` for the row liveness — distinct from
147    /// `local_deletion_time` which is the GC-grace clock for row tombstones.
148    /// `None` when `HAS_TTL` was not set.
149    /// Only read by the delta-scan emit path (`parse_block_emit_delta`); allow it
150    /// to be unused when that feature is off so non-delta builds compile under
151    /// `-D warnings`.
152    #[cfg_attr(not(feature = "delta-scan"), allow(dead_code))]
153    liveness_expires_at_seconds: Option<i32>,
154    /// Row-level local deletion time in SECONDS (after delta decoding from
155    /// min_local_deletion_time). This is the GC-grace clock, NOT the reconciliation
156    /// timestamp; do not use it for last-write-wins comparisons.
157    local_deletion_time: Option<i32>,
158    /// Row-level `markedForDeleteAt` reconciliation timestamp in MICROSECONDS
159    /// (absolute = min_timestamp + delta). For a row tombstone this is the
160    /// authoritative deletion timestamp used by the compaction merger for
161    /// timestamp-based last-write-wins shadowing (Issue #505). `None` when the
162    /// row has no HAS_DELETION flag.
163    marked_for_delete_at: Option<i64>,
164    /// Number of bytes consumed by the header
165    header_size: usize,
166    /// Length of the row_size VInt in bytes (needed for offset calculation)
167    /// row_size is measured from AFTER this VInt is consumed
168    row_size_vint_len: usize,
169    /// Bitmask of missing columns from Cassandra's Columns.Serializer format.
170    /// bit=1 means column missing, bit=0 means column present.
171    /// None when HAS_ALL_COLUMNS flag is set.
172    missing_columns_bitmap: Option<u64>,
173}
174
175impl RowHeader {
176    /// Whether this row header describes a row tombstone (HAS_DELETION was set).
177    ///
178    /// Detected via `local_deletion_time` being present, which is only set when the
179    /// HAS_DELETION (0x10) flag was decoded (Issue #505).
180    fn is_row_tombstone(&self) -> bool {
181        self.local_deletion_time.is_some()
182    }
183
184    /// Build the `Value::Tombstone(RowTombstone)` for this header.
185    ///
186    /// The reconciliation `deletion_time` is `marked_for_delete_at` (the
187    /// `markedForDeleteAt` field, MICROSECONDS — same clock as HAS_TIMESTAMP), NOT
188    /// the row write `timestamp` and NOT `local_deletion_time` (seconds, GC clock).
189    /// For a pure row tombstone HAS_TIMESTAMP is absent, so using the write
190    /// timestamp would yield epoch 0 and lose every merge comparison (Issue #505).
191    ///
192    /// Falls back to `local_deletion_time` promoted to microseconds only if
193    /// `marked_for_delete_at` is somehow absent while a deletion was recorded
194    /// (should not happen given HAS_DELETION always writes both VInts), keeping the
195    /// merger's LWW ordering meaningful rather than defaulting to 0.
196    fn row_tombstone(&self) -> Value {
197        let deletion_time = self.row_tombstone_deletion_time();
198        Value::Tombstone(TombstoneInfo {
199            deletion_time,
200            tombstone_type: TombstoneType::RowTombstone,
201            // Carry the on-disk `localDeletionTime` (GC clock, seconds) so the
202            // compaction merge→rewrite path can preserve it (#873). Absent for a
203            // non-tombstone header, hence the `0` fallback.
204            local_deletion_time: self.local_deletion_time.unwrap_or(0) as i64,
205            ttl: None,
206            range_start: None,
207            range_end: None,
208        })
209    }
210
211    /// Authoritative reconciliation timestamp (microseconds) for a row tombstone.
212    fn row_tombstone_deletion_time(&self) -> i64 {
213        match self.marked_for_delete_at {
214            Some(ts) => ts,
215            // Defensive fallback: promote the seconds-based local deletion time to
216            // microseconds so ordering remains non-zero and monotonic.
217            None => self
218                .local_deletion_time
219                .map(|s| (s as i64).saturating_mul(1_000_000))
220                .unwrap_or(0),
221        }
222    }
223}
224
225/// Result of parsing a single complex cell (an element of a list/set, or a
226/// key/value entry of a map).  See [`V5CompressedLegacyParser::parse_complex_cell_value`].
227///
228/// `is_deleted` carries the authoritative IS_DELETED (0x01) cell flag so that
229/// collection parsers can distinguish element-level tombstones from live
230/// elements that merely have an empty value (Issue #493).
231struct ComplexCellParse {
232    /// Decoded cell value, or `None` if the cell was deleted or had an empty value.
233    value: Option<Value>,
234    /// Raw cell-path bytes (the element value for sets, the key for maps).
235    path_bytes: Vec<u8>,
236    /// Whether the cell carries the IS_DELETED (0x01) flag (an element tombstone).
237    is_deleted: bool,
238    /// Whether the cell carries the HAS_EMPTY_VALUE (0x04) flag (an on-disk
239    /// empty-value cell — e.g. a SET member whose identity lives entirely in the
240    /// cell_path). Surfaced so the compaction writer can reproduce the SAME
241    /// on-disk emptiness byte-for-byte rather than re-deriving it from the
242    /// decoded value (epic #899, Phase C: a SET element's decoded member is the
243    /// path bytes, NOT a cell value).
244    has_empty_value: bool,
245    /// Offset immediately following the parsed cell.
246    next_offset: usize,
247    /// Per-element writetime decoded from the cell's own timestamp field, in µs since
248    /// Unix epoch (absolute, after delta decoding from min_timestamp).  `None` when the
249    /// element inherited the row-level timestamp (USE_ROW_TIMESTAMP flag 0x08).
250    ///
251    /// Used by `parse_complex_column_inner` to compute the max element writetime
252    /// for a collection column (Issue #700, DS4).
253    element_writetime: Option<i64>,
254    /// Per-element TTL in seconds when the cell is expiring (`IS_EXPIRING`
255    /// 0x02 set and not `USE_ROW_TTL`). `None` otherwise. Surfaced for the
256    /// per-element compaction contract (epic #899).
257    element_ttl: Option<u32>,
258    /// Per-element `localDeletionTime` in SECONDS for an expiring / deleted
259    /// element. Far-future values in `[2^31, 2^32)` are kept as the wrapping
260    /// `as u32 as i32` representation (epic #899 invariant). `None` when the
261    /// element carries no local deletion time.
262    element_local_deletion_time: Option<i32>,
263}
264
265/// Extra metadata produced by `parse_complex_column_inner` for delta-scan callers
266/// (Issue #700, DS4: non-frozen collection v1 semantics).
267///
268/// Returned alongside the `Value` and new offset so the emit path can set the correct
269/// `replaced` flag and `writetime` on the resulting `CellDelta`.
270///
271/// Fields are read by `parse_block_emit_delta` which is `#[cfg(feature = "delta-scan")]`;
272/// without that feature the struct is built but not consumed, hence the allow.
273#[allow(dead_code)]
274#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
275pub(crate) struct ComplexColumnMeta {
276    /// `true` when the collection generation carries a collection-level tombstone
277    /// (`s = {...}` overwrite), meaning the consumer must **replace** rather than
278    /// merge the prior collection state.
279    pub has_collection_tombstone: bool,
280    /// Maximum element writetime seen across all cells in this collection, in µs
281    /// since Unix epoch.  `0` when no element had its own explicit timestamp
282    /// (all inherited the row timestamp).
283    pub max_element_writetime: i64,
284    /// Number of element-level tombstones detected (`is_deleted` flag) in this
285    /// collection cell (Issue #493 territory).  v1 does not represent them; callers
286    /// must count and warn.
287    pub element_tombstone_count: u64,
288    /// Real complex deletion `(markedForDeleteAt µs, localDeletionTime s)` for
289    /// this column, or `None` for the `LIVE` sentinel (epic #899). Used by the
290    /// compaction read path to populate `ComplexColumn.complex_deletion`.
291    /// Always `None` on the user-facing read path (where the field is unused).
292    pub complex_deletion: Option<(i64, i32)>,
293}

295// Row header flag constants
296const ROW_HAS_TIMESTAMP: u8 = 0x04;
297const ROW_HAS_TTL: u8 = 0x08;
298const ROW_HAS_DELETION: u8 = 0x10;
299const ROW_HAS_ALL_COLUMNS: u8 = 0x20;
300const ROW_HAS_COMPLEX_DELETION: u8 = 0x40; // Issue #221: Row contains complex column with deletion info
301const ROW_HAS_EXTENDED_FLAGS: u8 = 0x80;
302
303/// Issue #932: does the decoded cell map hold any NON-primary-key data cell?
304///
305/// Primary-key (partition + clustering) columns are surfaced into the cell map
306/// as pseudo-cells (#229) so the read-back path can recover the clustering
307/// identity; they are NOT row data. A row carrying `HAS_DELETION` is a PURE row
308/// tombstone only when no such data cell survives — otherwise the row deletion
309/// COEXISTS with surviving (strictly-newer) cells and the row displays as live.
310fn row_has_non_key_cell(cells: &HashMap<String, Value>, schema: &TableSchema) -> bool {
311    cells.keys().any(|name| {
312        !schema.partition_keys.iter().any(|k| &k.name == name)
313            && !schema.clustering_keys.iter().any(|c| &c.name == name)
314    })
315}
316
317// Unfiltered marker constants (from Cassandra UnfilteredSerializer.java lines 102-109)
318// Issue #229: These markers were being misinterpreted as row data, causing parsing failures
319const END_OF_PARTITION: u8 = 0x01; // Signal end of partition - nothing follows this flag byte
320const IS_MARKER: u8 = 0x02; // Range tombstone marker (not a data row)
321
322// Extended flags constants (from Cassandra UnfilteredSerializer.java lines 114-122)
323// These are in the SECOND byte when ROW_HAS_EXTENDED_FLAGS (0x80) is set
324const EXTENDED_IS_STATIC: u8 = 0x01; // Static row - has NO clustering prefix
325
326// NOTE: V5CompressedLegacy format has NO trailing field after row data.
327// The next partition/row starts immediately after row_size bytes.
328// (Previous ROW_TRAILING_FIELD_SIZE constant was removed as part of Issue #237 fix)
329
330/// Parser for V5CompressedLegacy format decompressed blocks
331pub struct V5CompressedLegacyParser {
332    keyspace: String,
333    table_name: String,
334    /// Minimum timestamp from Statistics.db for delta decoding
335    min_timestamp: i64,
336    /// Minimum local deletion time from Statistics.db for delta decoding
337    min_local_deletion_time: i64,
338    /// Minimum TTL from Statistics.db for delta decoding
339    min_ttl: Option<i64>,
340    /// Optional UDT registry for resolving short UDT type names (Issue #238)
341    udt_registry: Option<UdtRegistry>,
342    /// Version-feature gates derived from the SSTable filename.
343    ///
344    /// Threaded here from `SSTableReader::version_gates` (VG1 plumbing).
345    /// Decision points that WILL be gated in VG3 are annotated with
346    /// `// VG3:` comments throughout this file.  Until VG3, behavior is
347    /// identical to the existing `nb`-compatible path regardless of the gate
348    /// values stored here.
349    version_gates: std::sync::Arc<VersionGates>,
350}
351
352impl V5CompressedLegacyParser {
353    /// Create a new V5CompressedLegacy parser
354    ///
355    /// # Arguments
356    /// * `keyspace` - Keyspace name
357    /// * `table_name` - Table name
358    /// * `min_timestamp` - Minimum timestamp for delta decoding (from Statistics.db)
359    /// * `min_local_deletion_time` - Minimum local deletion time for delta decoding (from Statistics.db)
360    /// * `min_ttl` - Minimum TTL for delta decoding (from Statistics.db)
361    pub fn new(
362        keyspace: String,
363        table_name: String,
364        min_timestamp: i64,
365        min_local_deletion_time: i64,
366        min_ttl: Option<i64>,
367    ) -> Self {
368        // Default to nb-compatible BIG gates when not supplied by the caller.
369        // Use the infallible nb_fallback() constructor (no expect/unwrap in lib code).
370        let version_gates = std::sync::Arc::new(VersionGates::Big(BigVersionGates::nb_fallback()));
371        Self {
372            keyspace,
373            table_name,
374            min_timestamp,
375            min_local_deletion_time,
376            min_ttl,
377            udt_registry: None,
378            version_gates,
379        }
380    }
381
382    /// Set the version gates for version-sensitive parsing decisions (VG1 plumbing).
383    ///
384    /// Call this after `new()` with the `Arc<VersionGates>` from `SSTableReader`.
385    /// Until VG3 lands, passing gates here has no effect on parsing behaviour —
386    /// the gate values are stored for future use only.
387    pub fn with_version_gates(mut self, gates: std::sync::Arc<VersionGates>) -> Self {
388        self.version_gates = gates;
389        self
390    }
391
392    /// Set the UDT registry for resolving short UDT type names in frozen collections (Issue #238)
393    pub fn with_udt_registry(mut self, registry: UdtRegistry) -> Self {
394        self.udt_registry = Some(registry);
395        self
396    }
397
398    /// Return `true` when the version gates indicate `hasUIntDeletionTime` (oa / da).
399    ///
400    /// Authority: BigFormat.java:409 — `hasUintDeletionTime = version.compareTo("oa") >= 0`
401    #[inline]
402    fn has_uint_deletion_time(&self) -> bool {
403        match self.version_gates.as_ref() {
404            VersionGates::Big(g) => g.has_uint_deletion_time,
405            VersionGates::Bti(g) => g.has_uint_deletion_time,
406        }
407    }
408
409    /// Try to parse partition header at offset WITHOUT consuming it.
410    ///
411    /// This performs a full parse attempt to determine if the bytes at offset
412    /// represent a valid partition header. This is the NO-HEURISTICS approach:
413    /// we actually try to parse the structure instead of guessing based on byte patterns.
414    ///
415    /// # Arguments
416    /// * `data` - Binary data buffer
417    /// * `offset` - Offset to check
418    ///
419    /// # Returns
420    /// * `true` if a valid partition header can be parsed at this offset
421    /// * `false` if parsing fails (likely a row header or invalid data)
422    ///
423    /// # Visibility
424    /// Exposed for integration testing to validate partition boundary detection
425    #[doc(hidden)]
426    pub fn peek_is_partition_header(&self, data: &[u8], offset: usize) -> bool {
427        // Issue #229 FIX: Check for END_OF_PARTITION marker FIRST
428        //
429        // The END_OF_PARTITION marker (0x01) can be misinterpreted as a valid partition
430        // header because parse_partition_header doesn't validate flags semantically.
431        // We must explicitly reject END_OF_PARTITION (0x01) and IS_MARKER (0x02) here.
432        if offset < data.len() {
433            let flags = data[offset];
434            if Self::is_end_of_partition(flags) || Self::is_range_tombstone_marker(flags) {
435                return false; // These are markers, not partition headers
436            }
437        }
438
439        // Try to actually parse the partition header
440        self.parse_partition_header(data, offset).is_ok()
441    }
442
443    /// Parse decompressed block into (TableId, RowKey, Value) entries
444    ///
445    /// # Arguments
446    /// * `data` - Decompressed block bytes
447    /// * `schema` - Optional table schema for type-aware parsing
448    /// * `reader` - Reference to SSTableReader for value parsing
449    ///
450    /// # Returns
451    /// * `Ok(Vec<(TableId, RowKey, Value)>)` - Parsed entries
452    /// * `Err(Error)` - Parse error with context
453    pub fn parse_block(
454        &self,
455        data: &[u8],
456        schema: Option<&TableSchema>,
457        reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
458    ) -> Result<Vec<(TableId, RowKey, Value)>> {
459        let mut results = Vec::new();
460        self.parse_block_emit(data, schema, reader, |entry| {
461            results.push(entry);
462            Ok(std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(()))
463        })?;
464        Ok(results)
465    }
466
467    /// Parse a block and return both row values and per-cell write metadata.
468    ///
469    /// Identical to [`parse_block`] but the returned vector carries a fourth element:
470    /// the per-cell `CellWriteMetadata` map (column name → metadata). Used by the
471    /// executor when `ProjectionFlags::include_cell_metadata` is set (i.e. when the
472    /// query contains `WRITETIME(col)` or `TTL(col)` expressions).
473    pub fn parse_block_with_cell_metadata(
474        &self,
475        data: &[u8],
476        schema: Option<&TableSchema>,
477        reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
478    ) -> Result<ParsedBlockWithMeta> {
479        let mut results = Vec::new();
480        self.parse_block_emit_with_metadata(data, schema, reader, |entry| {
481            results.push(entry);
482            Ok(std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(()))
483        })?;
484        Ok(results)
485    }
486
487    /// Internal streaming variant of `parse_block_with_cell_metadata`.
488    fn parse_block_emit_with_metadata<F>(
489        &self,
490        data: &[u8],
491        schema: Option<&TableSchema>,
492        reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
493        mut emit: F,
494    ) -> Result<()>
495    where
496        F: FnMut(
497            (TableId, RowKey, Value, HashMap<String, CellWriteMetadata>),
498        ) -> Result<std::ops::ControlFlow<()>>,
499    {
500        if data.is_empty() {
501            return Ok(());
502        }
503
504        let schema = schema.ok_or_else(|| {
505            Error::schema(format!(
506                "V5CompressedLegacy format requires schema for {}.{} (cells lack column names in binary data)",
507                self.keyspace, self.table_name
508            ))
509        })?;
510
511        let mut offset = 0;
512        let mut partition_index = 0;
513
514        while offset < data.len() {
515            // Parse partition header: returns (RowKey, next_data_offset)
516            let (partition_key, next_data_offset) = match self.parse_partition_header(data, offset)
517            {
518                Ok(ph) => ph,
519                Err(_) => break,
520            };
521
522            let table_id = TableId(format!("{}.{}", self.keyspace, self.table_name));
523            offset = next_data_offset;
524            partition_index += 1;
525
526            let mut static_cells: HashMap<String, Value> = HashMap::new();
527            let mut static_cell_meta: HashMap<String, CellWriteMetadata> = HashMap::new();
528            let mut row_count = 0;
529
530            loop {
531                if offset < data.len() && Self::is_end_of_partition(data[offset]) {
532                    offset += 1;
533                    break;
534                }
535
536                if offset < data.len() && Self::is_range_tombstone_marker(data[offset]) {
537                    match self.skip_range_tombstone_marker(data, offset, schema) {
538                        Ok(next_offset) => {
539                            offset = next_offset;
540                            continue;
541                        }
542                        Err(_) => break,
543                    }
544                }
545
546                match self.parse_row_data_with_offset(data, offset, Some(schema), reader, true) {
547                    Ok((
548                        mut cells,
549                        row_cell_meta_opt,
550                        row_header_opt,
551                        next_offset,
552                        is_static,
553                        _complex_meta,
554                    )) => {
555                        let mut row_cell_meta = row_cell_meta_opt.unwrap_or_default();
556                        offset = next_offset;
557                        row_count += 1;
558
559                        if is_static {
560                            static_cells = cells;
561                            static_cell_meta = row_cell_meta;
562                        } else {
563                            // Merge static cells / metadata into clustering row
564                            for (k, v) in &static_cells {
565                                cells.entry(k.clone()).or_insert_with(|| v.clone());
566                            }
567                            for (k, v) in &static_cell_meta {
568                                row_cell_meta.entry(k.clone()).or_insert_with(|| v.clone());
569                            }
570
571                            let row_tombstone =
572                                row_header_opt.as_ref().filter(|h| h.is_row_tombstone());
573
574                            // Issue #932: a HAS_DELETION row may ALSO carry surviving
575                            // cells (written strictly after the row deletion). For the
576                            // user-facing scan those cells — all newer than the
577                            // deletion — display as a live row; the deletion shadows
578                            // only already-absent older cells, so it has no display
579                            // effect here. Emit a pure `Tombstone` ONLY when no
580                            // non-primary-key cell survives.
581                            let has_data_cell = row_has_non_key_cell(&cells, schema);
582                            let row_value = if row_tombstone.is_some() && !has_data_cell {
583                                row_tombstone
584                                    .map(|h| h.row_tombstone())
585                                    .unwrap_or(Value::Null)
586                            } else if cells.is_empty() {
587                                Value::Null
588                            } else {
589                                let mut map_entries: Vec<(Value, Value)> = cells
590                                    .into_iter()
591                                    .map(|(name, value)| (Value::Text(name), value))
592                                    .collect();
593                                map_entries.sort_by(|a, b| {
594                                    let a_key = if let Value::Text(s) = &a.0 {
595                                        s.as_str()
596                                    } else {
597                                        ""
598                                    };
599                                    let b_key = if let Value::Text(s) = &b.0 {
600                                        s.as_str()
601                                    } else {
602                                        ""
603                                    };
604                                    a_key.cmp(b_key)
605                                });
606                                Value::Map(map_entries)
607                            };
608
609                            match emit((
610                                table_id.clone(),
611                                partition_key.clone(),
612                                row_value,
613                                row_cell_meta,
614                            ))? {
615                                std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(()) => {}
616                                std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(()) => return Ok(()),
617                            }
618                        }
619
620                        if offset >= data.len() {
621                            break;
622                        }
623
624                        if self.peek_is_partition_header(data, offset) {
625                            log::debug!(
626                                "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition {} detected at offset {} after {} rows",
627                                partition_index + 1, offset, row_count
628                            );
629                            break;
630                        }
631                    }
632                    Err(e) => {
633                        log::debug!(
634                            "V5CompressedLegacy: Row parse error in partition {} at offset {}: {}",
635                            partition_index,
636                            offset,
637                            e
638                        );
639                        break;
640                    }
641                }
642            }
643        }
644
645        Ok(())
646    }
647
648    /// Delta-scan variant of [`parse_block_emit_with_metadata`] (Epic #696, Issue #698).
649    ///
650    /// Identical in parsing strategy to [`parse_block_emit_with_metadata`] but emits
651    /// **static rows separately** instead of merging them into the first clustering row.
652    /// The emit closure receives five values per row:
653    ///
654    /// ```text
655    /// (partition_key, cells, cell_meta, row_liveness_ts, is_static)
656    /// ```
657    ///
658    /// - `cells`            — column-name → decoded `Value` (including clustering cols).
659    /// - `cell_meta`        — column-name → `CellWriteMetadata` (writetime + TTL).
660    /// - `row_liveness_ts`  — `Some(ts_µs)` when the row was created with `INSERT` and
661    ///   carries a primary-key liveness timestamp (`HAS_TIMESTAMP` flag).  `None` for
662    ///   `UPDATE`-only rows (no pk liveness).
663    /// - `is_static`        — `true` for static-column rows (emit as `StaticUpsert`).
664    ///
665    /// Row tombstones (rows with `HAS_DELETION`) are emitted with a non-empty `cell_meta`
666    /// and an empty `cells` map; callers must detect them via a missing row-liveness
667    /// timestamp combined with `row_header_is_deletion = true` in `cell_meta`.
668    ///
669    /// Note: Range tombstone markers are *skipped* in this version — they are emitted as
670    /// errors by the delta-scan caller per Issue #699 scope boundaries.
671    // ComplexColumnMeta is intentionally restricted to the reader module; the
672    // closure bound here is not part of the public API surface.
673    #[allow(private_bounds)]
674    #[cfg(feature = "delta-scan")]
675    pub fn parse_block_emit_delta<F>(
676        &self,
677        data: &[u8],
678        schema: Option<&TableSchema>,
679        reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
680        mut emit: F,
681    ) -> Result<()>
682    where
683        F: FnMut(
684            (
685                RowKey,
686                HashMap<String, Value>,
687                HashMap<String, CellWriteMetadata>,
688                Option<i64>, // row-level liveness timestamp (HAS_TIMESTAMP), µs
689                bool,        // is_static
690                bool,        // is_row_tombstone
691                Option<i64>, // marked_for_delete_at (row tombstone deletion time, or None)
692                // --- Issue #699 tombstone extensions ---
693                Option<(Vec<Value>, bool, Vec<Value>, bool, i64)>, // range tombstone info: (start_values, start_inclusive, end_values, end_inclusive, deleted_at)
694                bool,                                              // is_partition_tombstone
695                // --- Issue #700 DS4 collection extensions ---
696                HashMap<String, ComplexColumnMeta>, // per-column complex collection metadata
697                // --- Issue #702 TTL liveness expiry ---
698                Option<i64>, // liveness expires_at in microseconds (from HAS_TTL ldt, epoch-s * 1_000_000)
699            ),
700        ) -> Result<std::ops::ControlFlow<()>>,
701    {
702        if data.is_empty() {
703            return Ok(());
704        }
705
706        let schema = schema.ok_or_else(|| {
707            Error::schema(format!(
708                "V5CompressedLegacy delta-scan requires schema for {}.{} (cells lack column names in binary data)",
709                self.keyspace, self.table_name
710            ))
711        })?;
712
713        let mut offset = 0;
714        let mut partition_index = 0;
715
716        while offset < data.len() {
717            let (partition_key, next_data_offset, partition_deletion) = self
718                .parse_partition_header_full(data, offset)
719                .map_err(|e| {
720                    Error::corruption(format!(
721                        "delta-scan: partition-header parse error at offset {} in {}.{}: {}",
722                        offset, self.keyspace, self.table_name, e
723                    ))
724                })?;
725
726            offset = next_data_offset;
727            partition_index += 1;
728            let mut row_count = 0;
729
730            // ----------------------------------------------------------------
731            // Issue #699: emit PartitionDelete if the partition header carried
732            // a tombstone (markedForDeleteAt != LIVE sentinel).
733            // ----------------------------------------------------------------
734            if let Some(deleted_at) = partition_deletion {
735                match emit((
736                    partition_key.clone(),
737                    HashMap::new(),
738                    HashMap::new(),
739                    None,
740                    false,
741                    false,
742                    Some(deleted_at),
743                    None,
744                    true,           // is_partition_tombstone
745                    HashMap::new(), // no collection metadata for tombstones
746                    None,           // no liveness TTL expiry for tombstones
747                ))? {
748                    std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(()) => {}
749                    std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(()) => return Ok(()),
750                }
751            }
752
753            // Buffer for in-flight range tombstone start bound.
754            //
755            // A range tombstone in Cassandra SSTable format is represented as a pair of
756            // adjacent "range tombstone markers":
757            //   INCL_START_BOUND (kind 1) or EXCL_START_BOUND (kind 7)  ← start
758            //   INCL_END_BOUND   (kind 6) or EXCL_END_BOUND   (kind 0)  ← end
759            //
760            // Or as a single "boundary" marker (kind 2 or 5) that encodes both the end
761            // of the previous range and the start of the next range simultaneously (used
762            // when two ranges share a clustering-key boundary point).
763            //
764            // We buffer the start bound here and emit a RangeDelete when the end arrives.
765            //
766            // Tuple: (start_values, start_inclusive, deleted_at)
767            let mut pending_range_start: Option<(Vec<Value>, bool, i64)> = None;
768
769            loop {
770                if offset < data.len() && Self::is_end_of_partition(data[offset]) {
771                    offset += 1;
772                    break;
773                }
774
775                if offset < data.len() && Self::is_range_tombstone_marker(data[offset]) {
776                    // Issue #699: Decode the range tombstone marker and emit RangeDelete.
777                    let (
778                        bound_values,
779                        bound_kind,
780                        deleted_at_primary,
781                        deleted_at_secondary,
782                        next_offset,
783                    ) = self
784                        .parse_range_tombstone_marker_full(data, offset, schema)
785                        .map_err(|e| {
786                            Error::corruption(format!(
787                                "delta-scan: range-tombstone-marker parse error in partition {} \
788                                     at offset {} in {}.{}: {}",
789                                partition_index, offset, self.keyspace, self.table_name, e
790                            ))
791                        })?;
792                    offset = next_offset;
793
794                    // Decode bound kind into start/end semantics.
795                    //
796                    // ClusteringPrefix.Kind ordinals (ClusteringBoundOrBoundary.java):
797                    //   0 = EXCL_END_BOUND              → end,   exclusive  (<  ck)
798                    //   1 = INCL_START_BOUND             → start, inclusive  (>= ck)
799                    //   2 = EXCL_END_INCL_START_BOUNDARY → end excl + start incl (2 del times)
800                    //   5 = INCL_END_EXCL_START_BOUNDARY → end incl + start excl (2 del times)
801                    //   6 = INCL_END_BOUND               → end,   inclusive  (<= ck)
802                    //   7 = EXCL_START_BOUND             → start, exclusive  (>  ck)
803                    match bound_kind {
804                        1 | 7 => {
805                            // Simple start bound: buffer and wait for the matching end.
806                            let is_inclusive = bound_kind == 1; // 1=INCL_START, 7=EXCL_START
807                            pending_range_start =
808                                Some((bound_values, is_inclusive, deleted_at_primary));
809                        }
810                        0 | 6 => {
811                            // Simple end bound: pair with buffered start and emit RangeDelete.
812                            let is_end_inclusive = bound_kind == 6; // 6=INCL_END, 0=EXCL_END
813                            let (start_values, start_inclusive, _start_del) =
814                                pending_range_start.take().unwrap_or_else(|| {
815                                    // End bound with no preceding start bound — treat as
816                                    // open (unbounded) start.  Hard-error policy: we faithfully
817                                    // represent this as an open bound rather than dropping it.
818                                    (Vec::new(), false, deleted_at_primary)
819                                });
820                            // Cassandra puts the authoritative markedForDeleteAt on both
821                            // bounds of a simple range (they are the same value); use the
822                            // end bound's primary deletion time.
823                            let range_info = Some((
824                                start_values,
825                                start_inclusive,
826                                bound_values,
827                                is_end_inclusive,
828                                deleted_at_primary,
829                            ));
830                            match emit((
831                                partition_key.clone(),
832                                HashMap::new(),
833                                HashMap::new(),
834                                None,
835                                false,
836                                false,
837                                Some(deleted_at_primary),
838                                range_info,
839                                false,          // is_partition_tombstone
840                                HashMap::new(), // no collection metadata for tombstones
841                                None,           // no liveness TTL expiry for tombstones
842                            ))? {
843                                std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(()) => {}
844                                std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(()) => return Ok(()),
845                            }
846                        }
847                        2 => {
848                            // EXCL_END_INCL_START_BOUNDARY (kind 2):
849                            //   primary   = end of the previous range, exclusive
850                            //   secondary = start of the new range, inclusive
851                            //
852                            // Close the pending range (if any) first.
853                            if let Some((start_values, start_inclusive, _)) =
854                                pending_range_start.take()
855                            {
856                                let range_info = Some((
857                                    start_values,
858                                    start_inclusive,
859                                    bound_values.clone(),
860                                    false, // EXCL_END
861                                    deleted_at_primary,
862                                ));
863                                match emit((
864                                    partition_key.clone(),
865                                    HashMap::new(),
866                                    HashMap::new(),
867                                    None,
868                                    false,
869                                    false,
870                                    Some(deleted_at_primary),
871                                    range_info,
872                                    false,
873                                    HashMap::new(), // no collection metadata for tombstones
874                                    None,           // no liveness TTL expiry for tombstones
875                                ))? {
876                                    std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(()) => {}
877                                    std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(()) => return Ok(()),
878                                }
879                            }
880                            // Open new range starting at bound_values (inclusive).
881                            let new_del_at = deleted_at_secondary.unwrap_or(deleted_at_primary);
882                            pending_range_start = Some((bound_values, true, new_del_at));
883                        }
884                        5 => {
885                            // INCL_END_EXCL_START_BOUNDARY (kind 5):
886                            //   primary   = end of the previous range, inclusive
887                            //   secondary = start of the new range, exclusive
888                            if let Some((start_values, start_inclusive, _)) =
889                                pending_range_start.take()
890                            {
891                                let range_info = Some((
892                                    start_values,
893                                    start_inclusive,
894                                    bound_values.clone(),
895                                    true, // INCL_END
896                                    deleted_at_primary,
897                                ));
898                                match emit((
899                                    partition_key.clone(),
900                                    HashMap::new(),
901                                    HashMap::new(),
902                                    None,
903                                    false,
904                                    false,
905                                    Some(deleted_at_primary),
906                                    range_info,
907                                    false,
908                                    HashMap::new(), // no collection metadata for tombstones
909                                    None,           // no liveness TTL expiry for tombstones
910                                ))? {
911                                    std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(()) => {}
912                                    std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(()) => return Ok(()),
913                                }
914                            }
915                            // Open new range starting at bound_values (exclusive).
916                            let new_del_at = deleted_at_secondary.unwrap_or(deleted_at_primary);
917                            pending_range_start = Some((bound_values, false, new_del_at));
918                        }
919                        unknown => {
920                            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
921                                "delta-scan: unknown range tombstone bound kind {} at offset {} \
922                                 in {}.{} (partition key {:?}) — cannot represent faithfully \
923                                 (no-heuristics mandate, issue #28)",
924                                unknown, offset, self.keyspace, self.table_name, partition_key.0
925                            )));
926                        }
927                    }
928
929                    continue;
930                }
931
932                match self.parse_row_data_with_offset(data, offset, Some(schema), reader, true) {
933                    Ok((
934                        cells,
935                        row_cell_meta_opt,
936                        row_header_opt,
937                        next_offset,
938                        is_static,
939                        complex_meta,
940                    )) => {
941                        let cell_meta = row_cell_meta_opt.unwrap_or_default();
942                        // DS4 (Issue #700): pass ComplexColumnMeta to the emit closure so the
943                        // delta-scan caller can set `replaced` and surface element tombstone counts.
944                        let col_meta_map = complex_meta.unwrap_or_default();
945                        offset = next_offset;
946                        row_count += 1;
947
948                        let (
949                            row_liveness_ts,
950                            is_row_tombstone,
951                            marked_for_delete_at,
952                            liveness_expires_at_micros,
953                        ) = if let Some(ref h) = row_header_opt {
954                            // Convert epoch-seconds liveness expiry to epoch-microseconds
955                            // (Issue #702: delta-scan CellMeta.expires_at).
956                            let liveness_exp = h
957                                .liveness_expires_at_seconds
958                                .map(|s| (s as i64).saturating_mul(1_000_000));
959                            (
960                                h.timestamp,
961                                h.is_row_tombstone(),
962                                h.marked_for_delete_at,
963                                liveness_exp,
964                            )
965                        } else {
966                            (None, false, None, None)
967                        };
968
969                        match emit((
970                            partition_key.clone(),
971                            cells,
972                            cell_meta,
973                            row_liveness_ts,
974                            is_static,
975                            is_row_tombstone,
976                            marked_for_delete_at,
977                            None,                       // range_info (not a range tombstone)
978                            false,                      // is_partition_tombstone
979                            col_meta_map,               // DS4 collection metadata
980                            liveness_expires_at_micros, // Issue #702: TTL liveness expiry
981                        ))? {
982                            std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(()) => {}
983                            std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(()) => return Ok(()),
984                        }
985
986                        if offset >= data.len() {
987                            break;
988                        }
989
990                        if self.peek_is_partition_header(data, offset) {
991                            log::debug!(
992                                "V5CompressedLegacy delta-scan: Partition {} detected at offset {} after {} rows",
993                                partition_index + 1, offset, row_count
994                            );
995                            break;
996                        }
997                    }
998                    Err(e) => {
999                        return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
1000                            "delta-scan: row parse error in partition {} at offset {} in {}.{}: {}",
1001                            partition_index, offset, self.keyspace, self.table_name, e
1002                        )));
1003                    }
1004                }
1005            }
1006
1007            let _ = row_count; // acknowledged for logging purposes
1008
1009            // Finding 3: dangling-range guard.
1010            // A well-formed SSTable always pairs every start marker with a matching
1011            // end marker (or a boundary marker that closes the range) before the
1012            // end-of-partition byte.  If we reach here with `pending_range_start`
1013            // still set, the SSTable is corrupt — the range was opened but never
1014            // closed.  Silently discarding it would violate the no-heuristics mandate
1015            // (issue #28); return a corruption error naming the partition.
1016            if let Some((start_vals, start_incl, start_del_at)) = pending_range_start {
1017                return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
1018                    "delta-scan: partition {} in {}.{} (key {:?}) has an unclosed range \
1019                     tombstone start bound (values={:?}, inclusive={}, deleted_at={}) with \
1020                     no matching end marker — corrupt SSTable (no-heuristics mandate, issue #28)",
1021                    partition_index,
1022                    self.keyspace,
1023                    self.table_name,
1024                    partition_key.0,
1025                    start_vals,
1026                    start_incl,
1027                    start_del_at,
1028                )));
1029            }
1030        }
1031
1032        Ok(())
1033    }
1034
1035    /// Streaming variant of [`parse_block`]: invokes `emit` for each parsed
1036    /// `(TableId, RowKey, Value)` entry instead of collecting them into a `Vec`,
1037    /// so callers can forward rows into a bounded channel without materializing
1038    /// the whole block at once (issue #790). Returning `ControlFlow::Break` from
1039    /// `emit` stops parsing early — used when the streaming consumer is dropped.
1040    pub fn parse_block_emit<F>(
1041        &self,
1042        data: &[u8],
1043        schema: Option<&TableSchema>,
1044        reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
1045        mut emit: F,
1046    ) -> Result<()>
1047    where
1048        F: FnMut((TableId, RowKey, Value)) -> Result<std::ops::ControlFlow<()>>,
1049    {
1050        if data.is_empty() {
1051            return Ok(());
1052        }
1053
1054        // V5CompressedLegacy format stores cells WITHOUT column names,
1055        // relying on schema to interpret the binary data. Schema is REQUIRED.
1056        let schema = schema.ok_or_else(|| {
1057            Error::schema(format!(
1058                "V5CompressedLegacy format requires schema for {}.{} (cells lack column names in binary data)",
1059                self.keyspace, self.table_name
1060            ))
1061        })?;
1062
1063        log::debug!(
1064            "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsing block for {}.{} ({} bytes)",
1065            self.keyspace,
1066            self.table_name,
1067            data.len()
1068        );
1069        log::debug!(
1070            "V5CompressedLegacy: Schema has {} columns",
1071            schema.columns.len()
1072        );
1073        for (i, col) in schema.columns.iter().enumerate() {
1074            log::debug!("  Column {}: {} ({})", i, col.name, col.data_type);
1075        }
1076        log::debug!(
1077            "V5CompressedLegacy: First 64 bytes of data: {}",
1078            hex::encode(&data[..std::cmp::min(64, data.len())])
1079        );
1080        debug!(
1081            "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsing block for {}.{} ({} bytes)",
1082            self.keyspace,
1083            self.table_name,
1084            data.len()
1085        );
1086
1087        let mut emitted: usize = 0;
1088        let mut offset = 0;
1089        let table_id = TableId::new(format!("{}.{}", self.keyspace, self.table_name));
1090
1091        // Cassandra partition key size limits (used in header validation)
1092        // - CASSANDRA_MAX_KEY_SIZE: 64KB limit per Apache Cassandra specification
1093        // - FORMAT_MAX_KEY_SIZE: u8 max value - V5CompressedLegacy format limitation
1094        const CASSANDRA_MAX_KEY_SIZE: usize = 65536; // 64KB per Cassandra spec
1095        const FORMAT_MAX_KEY_SIZE: usize = 255; // u8 max value - format limitation
1096
1097        // Parse ALL partitions in block (Issue #2 fix: previously only parsed one partition)
1098        let mut partition_index = 0;
1099        let mut skipped_partitions = 0;
1100        while offset < data.len() {
1101            log::debug!(
1102                "V5CompressedLegacy: === PARTITION {} at offset {} (block size: {}) ===",
1103                partition_index,
1104                offset,
1105                data.len()
1106            );
1107
1108            // CRITICAL FIX (Issue #164): Validate partition header format before attempting parse
1109            //
1110            // Most compressed blocks contain EXACTLY ONE partition. After parsing the first
1111            // partition's row data and trailing VInt, we should NOT assume there's another
1112            // partition just because offset < data.len().
1113            //
1114            // Partition header format validation:
1115            // - Byte 0: Flags (typically 0x00, sometimes has partition-level flags)
1116            // - Byte 1: Partition key length (u8, typically 16 for UUID)
1117            // - Bytes 2+: Partition key data
1118            //
1119            // If we don't see a valid partition header structure, we've reached the end
1120            // of partitions in this block (remaining bytes are likely padding or metadata).
1121            if offset >= data.len() {
1122                break; // End of block
1123            }
1124
1125            // Check if this looks like a partition header (flags byte + reasonable key length)
1126            // Partition keys can be up to 64KB per Cassandra spec (composite keys, text, etc.)
1127            if offset + 2 > data.len() {
1128                log::debug!(
1129                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Not enough bytes for partition header at offset {} (need 2, have {}), stopping",
1130                    offset,
1131                    data.len() - offset
1132                );
1133                break;
1134            }
1135
1136            let flags = data[offset];
1137            let key_len = data[offset + 1] as usize;
1138
1139            // Validate partition header:
1140            // - Key length must be non-zero and within format's limit (u8 max = 255 bytes)
1141            //   Note: Cassandra spec allows 64KB keys, but V5CompressedLegacy format uses u8 length
1142            // - Must have enough bytes for the header (size depends on format version)
1143            //
1144            // VG3: oa format (hasUIntDeletionTime) uses a compact DeletionTime:
1145            //   LIVE = 1 byte; DELETED = 12 bytes.  The minimum is therefore 1 byte.
1146            // nb format always uses 12 bytes (4 + 8).
1147            // NOTE: No heuristic validation of flags (Issue #258, #28 no-heuristics mandate)
1148            let deletion_time_min = if self.has_uint_deletion_time() { 1 } else { 12 };
1149            let header_min_size = 1 + 1 + key_len + deletion_time_min;
1150            if key_len == 0
1151                || key_len > FORMAT_MAX_KEY_SIZE.min(CASSANDRA_MAX_KEY_SIZE)
1152                || offset + header_min_size > data.len()
1153            {
1154                log::warn!(
1155                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Skipping malformed partition header at offset {} \
1156                     (flags=0x{:02x}, key_len={}, need {} bytes, have {}, partition={}): header validation failed",
1157                    offset,
1158                    flags,
1159                    key_len,
1160                    header_min_size,
1161                    data.len() - offset,
1162                    partition_index
1163                );
1164                // Try to skip to next potential partition boundary
1165                skipped_partitions += 1;
1166                offset += 1; // Minimal forward progress to avoid infinite loop
1167                continue; // Skip this partition, try next
1168            }
1169
1170            // Try to parse partition header
1171            match self.parse_partition_header(data, offset) {
1172                Ok((partition_key, new_offset)) => {
1173                    let header_size = new_offset - offset;
1174                    offset = new_offset;
1175
1176                    log::debug!(
1177                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition {} - Parsed partition key: {} bytes (header consumed {} bytes, now at offset {})",
1178                        partition_index,
1179                        partition_key.0.len(),
1180                        header_size,
1181                        offset
1182                    );
1183                    log::debug!(
1184                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition {} - Row data starts at offset {}, remaining: {} bytes",
1185                        partition_index,
1186                        offset,
1187                        data.len() - offset
1188                    );
1189                    log::debug!(
1190                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition {} - Row data hex (first 128 bytes): {}",
1191                        partition_index,
1192                        hex::encode(&data[offset..std::cmp::min(offset + 128, data.len())])
1193                    );
1194
1195                    debug!(
1196                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsed partition key: {} bytes, now at offset {}",
1197                        partition_key.0.len(),
1198                        offset
1199                    );
1200
1201                    // Parse ALL rows in this partition (Issue #166 fix: multi-row partition support)
1202                    //
1203                    // V5CompressedLegacy partitions can contain multiple rows with different clustering keys.
1204                    // We use structural parsing (peek_is_partition_header) to detect partition boundaries,
1205                    // not flag value heuristics (Issue #258, #28 no-heuristics mandate).
1206                    // We parse rows in a loop until we encounter:
1207                    // - End of block (offset >= data.len())
1208                    // - END_OF_PARTITION marker (flags == 0x01, Issue #229 fix)
1209                    // - Next partition header (detected via peek_is_partition_header)
1210                    // - Parse error (invalid row data)
1211
1212                    // Issue #480 FIX: Static cell handling
1213                    //
1214                    // Cassandra static rows are stored once per partition (before clustering rows).
1215                    // They should NOT be emitted as separate result entries — instead their column
1216                    // values must be merged into each clustering row that follows in the partition.
1217                    //
1218                    // We accumulate static cells here and inject them into every clustering row.
1219                    let mut static_cells: HashMap<String, Value> = HashMap::new();
1220                    let mut row_count = 0;
1221                    loop {
1222                        // Issue #229 FIX: Check for END_OF_PARTITION marker BEFORE attempting row parse
1223                        //
1224                        // Per Cassandra's UnfilteredSerializer.java (lines 102, 730-732):
1225                        // When END_OF_PARTITION (0x01) is set in the flags byte, nothing follows.
1226                        // The partition is complete and we should move to the next partition.
1227                        if offset < data.len() && Self::is_end_of_partition(data[offset]) {
1228                            log::debug!(
1229                                "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition {} complete via END_OF_PARTITION marker at offset {} ({} rows parsed)",
1230                                partition_index, offset, row_count
1231                            );
1232                            offset += 1; // Skip the END_OF_PARTITION marker byte
1233                            break; // Move to next partition
1234                        }
1235
1236                        // Issue #229 FIX: Check for range tombstone marker
1237                        //
1238                        // Per Cassandra's UnfilteredSerializer.java (lines 103, 735-738):
1239                        // When IS_MARKER (0x02) is set, this is a range tombstone boundary, not a row.
1240                        // We skip these markers for now (full implementation would parse deletion ranges).
1241                        if offset < data.len() && Self::is_range_tombstone_marker(data[offset]) {
1242                            log::debug!(
1243                                "V5CompressedLegacy: Range tombstone marker at offset {} (partition {}), skipping",
1244                                offset, partition_index
1245                            );
1246                            // Skip the marker - for now, just advance past it
1247                            // A full implementation would parse ClusteringBoundOrBoundary and deletion times
1248                            match self.skip_range_tombstone_marker(data, offset, schema) {
1249                                Ok(next_offset) => {
1250                                    offset = next_offset;
1251                                    continue; // Continue to next row/marker
1252                                }
1253                                Err(e) => {
1254                                    log::debug!(
1255                                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to skip range tombstone marker at offset {}: {}",
1256                                        offset, e
1257                                    );
1258                                    break; // Can't parse marker, end partition
1259                                }
1260                            }
1261                        }
1262
1263                        match self.parse_row_data_with_offset(
1264                            data,
1265                            offset,
1266                            Some(schema),
1267                            reader,
1268                            false,
1269                        ) {
1270                            Ok((
1271                                mut cells,
1272                                _row_cell_meta,
1273                                row_header_opt,
1274                                next_offset,
1275                                is_static,
1276                                _complex_meta,
1277                            )) => {
1278                                // Update offset to point to the next row or partition
1279                                offset = next_offset;
1280                                row_count += 1;
1281
1282                                log::debug!(
1283                                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition {} Row {} - Parsed {} cells, now at offset {} (is_static={})",
1284                                    partition_index,
1285                                    row_count,
1286                                    cells.len(),
1287                                    offset,
1288                                    is_static
1289                                );
1290
1291                                if let Some(ref header) = row_header_opt {
1292                                    log::debug!(
1293                                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Row {} metadata - timestamp={:?}, ttl={:?}, deletion={:?}",
1294                                        row_count,
1295                                        header.timestamp, header.ttl, header.local_deletion_time
1296                                    );
1297                                }
1298
1299                                debug!(
1300                                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsed {} cells from row {} (is_static={})",
1301                                    cells.len(),
1302                                    row_count,
1303                                    is_static
1304                                );
1305
1306                                // Issue #480 FIX: Static row handling
1307                                //
1308                                // Static rows are stored once per partition and contain values for
1309                                // STATIC columns (e.g. `static_data TEXT STATIC`). They must NOT
1310                                // be emitted as standalone result rows. Instead, store the static
1311                                // column values and merge them into each subsequent clustering row.
1312                                if is_static {
1313                                    log::debug!(
1314                                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition {} - Storing {} static cells for merging into clustering rows",
1315                                        partition_index,
1316                                        cells.len()
1317                                    );
1318                                    static_cells = cells;
1319                                    // Do NOT push to results — static rows are not result rows
1320                                    // Continue to next row/marker in partition
1321                                } else {
1322                                    // Merge static cells into this clustering row (Issue #480)
1323                                    for (k, v) in &static_cells {
1324                                        cells.entry(k.clone()).or_insert_with(|| v.clone());
1325                                    }
1326
1327                                    // Convert cells HashMap to Value::Map (required by SelectExecutor)
1328                                    //
1329                                    // Issue #505: Row tombstones are detected via HAS_DELETION in the
1330                                    // row header.  When present, emit a proper `Value::Tombstone`
1331                                    // carrying the authoritative `markedForDeleteAt` (microseconds) so
1332                                    // the compaction merger can apply tombstone-shadowing semantics
1333                                    // rather than treating the absent cells as a live empty row.
1334                                    let row_tombstone =
1335                                        row_header_opt.as_ref().filter(|h| h.is_row_tombstone());
1336
1337                                    // Issue #932: a HAS_DELETION row carrying
1338                                    // surviving (strictly-newer) cells displays as a
1339                                    // live row for the user-facing scan — the
1340                                    // deletion shadows only already-absent older
1341                                    // cells. Emit a pure Tombstone only when no
1342                                    // non-primary-key cell survives.
1343                                    let has_data_cell = row_has_non_key_cell(&cells, schema);
1344                                    let row_value = if row_tombstone.is_some() && !has_data_cell {
1345                                        if let Some(h) = row_tombstone {
1346                                            log::debug!(
1347                                                "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition {} Row {} - emitting Tombstone(deletion_time={})",
1348                                                partition_index, row_count, h.row_tombstone_deletion_time()
1349                                            );
1350                                            h.row_tombstone()
1351                                        } else {
1352                                            Value::Null
1353                                        }
1354                                    } else if cells.is_empty() {
1355                                        warn!(
1356                                            "V5CompressedLegacy: No cells extracted for {}.{} partition {} row {} (partition key: {} bytes)",
1357                                            self.keyspace,
1358                                            self.table_name,
1359                                            partition_index,
1360                                            row_count,
1361                                            partition_key.0.len()
1362                                        );
1363                                        Value::Null
1364                                    } else {
1365                                        // Convert HashMap<String, Value> to Vec<(Value, Value)> for Value::Map.
1366                                        //
1367                                        // Sort alphabetically by column name to guarantee a deterministic
1368                                        // ordering across independent parse calls.  HashMap iteration order
1369                                        // is randomized per-instance in Rust, so two separate calls to
1370                                        // stitch_and_parse_all_chunks (e.g. get() then scan()) would
1371                                        // otherwise produce Vec orderings that compare as unequal even
1372                                        // though they hold the same data.
1373                                        //
1374                                        // Alphabetical is not schema column order, but the query layer
1375                                        // (executor.rs:storage_data_to_query_row) accesses columns by name
1376                                        // (not position), so this ordering does not affect query correctness
1377                                        // or sstabledump parity.
1378                                        //
1379                                        // NON-BLOCKING-3 (Issue #516/517): A future improvement could use
1380                                        // serialization-header order (reader.header.columns) rather than
1381                                        // alphabetical, matching Cassandra's on-disk column order exactly.
1382                                        // That would require threading the column order through ParsedRow
1383                                        // to this call site.
1384                                        let mut map_entries: Vec<(Value, Value)> = cells
1385                                            .into_iter()
1386                                            .map(|(name, value)| (Value::Text(name), value))
1387                                            .collect();
1388                                        map_entries.sort_by(|a, b| {
1389                                            let a_key = if let Value::Text(s) = &a.0 {
1390                                                s.as_str()
1391                                            } else {
1392                                                ""
1393                                            };
1394                                            let b_key = if let Value::Text(s) = &b.0 {
1395                                                s.as_str()
1396                                            } else {
1397                                                ""
1398                                            };
1399                                            a_key.cmp(b_key)
1400                                        });
1401                                        Value::Map(map_entries)
1402                                    };
1403
1404                                    match emit((
1405                                        table_id.clone(),
1406                                        partition_key.clone(),
1407                                        row_value,
1408                                    ))? {
1409                                        std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(()) => emitted += 1,
1410                                        // Consumer dropped (streaming receiver gone): stop parsing.
1411                                        std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(()) => return Ok(()),
1412                                    }
1413                                }
1414
1415                                // Check if we're at the end of the partition
1416                                if offset >= data.len() {
1417                                    debug!(
1418                                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition {} complete: {} rows parsed (end of block)",
1419                                        partition_index, row_count
1420                                    );
1421                                    break; // End of block
1422                                }
1423
1424                                // CRITICAL FIX (Issue #166): NO HEURISTICS - Try-parse approach
1425                                //
1426                                // Instead of guessing based on byte patterns (e.g., checking if flags <= 0x20
1427                                // or validating key_len ranges), we ACTUALLY TRY TO PARSE the next structure.
1428                                //
1429                                // Why heuristics fail:
1430                                // - Row with small value (e.g., boolean=0x0A) can look like key_len
1431                                // - Row flags=0x00 or 0x20 pass "<= 0x20" checks meant for partitions
1432                                // - Any byte-pattern guessing will eventually fail on edge cases
1433                                //
1434                                // The only reliable approach: try to parse as partition header.
1435                                // If that succeeds, it's a partition. If it fails, continue with rows.
1436                                if self.peek_is_partition_header(data, offset) {
1437                                    debug!(
1438                                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition {} complete: {} rows parsed (next partition detected at offset {})",
1439                                        partition_index, row_count, offset
1440                                    );
1441                                    break; // Next partition starts here
1442                                }
1443
1444                                // Peek failed - not a partition header, so continue parsing rows
1445                                debug!(
1446                                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition {} - Continuing to row {} at offset {} (peek confirmed this is NOT a partition header)",
1447                                    partition_index, row_count + 1, offset
1448                                );
1449                            }
1450                            Err(e) => {
1451                                // End of valid data in partition
1452                                debug!(
1453                                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition {} ended after {} rows: {}",
1454                                    partition_index, row_count, e
1455                                );
1456                                if row_count == 0 {
1457                                    // If we couldn't parse even one row, log as error
1458                                    log::error!(
1459                                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition {} - Failed to parse first row at offset {}: {}",
1460                                        partition_index, offset, e
1461                                    );
1462                                }
1463                                break; // End of valid data in partition
1464                            }
1465                        }
1466                    }
1467
1468                    partition_index += 1;
1469                }
1470                Err(e) => {
1471                    log::warn!(
1472                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse partition header at offset {} \
1473                         (partition={}): {}. Attempting to continue to next partition.",
1474                        offset,
1475                        partition_index,
1476                        e
1477                    );
1478                    // Try to skip forward to find next partition
1479                    skipped_partitions += 1;
1480                    offset += 1;
1481                    continue; // Skip this partition, try next
1482                }
1483            }
1484        }
1485
1486        if skipped_partitions > 0 {
1487            log::warn!(
1488                "V5CompressedLegacy: Successfully parsed {} entries, skipped {} malformed partitions",
1489                emitted,
1490                skipped_partitions
1491            );
1492        }
1493
1494        debug!(
1495            "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsed {} total entries from block",
