1496            emitted
1497        );
1498
1499        Ok(())
1500    }
1501
1502    /// Parse all partitions in a decompressed block, returning per-row timestamps.
1503    ///
1504    /// This is the compaction-specific variant of [`parse_block`].  It returns
1505    /// `(TableId, RowKey, Value, row_timestamp_micros)` so that the k-way merger
1506    /// can perform timestamp-accurate last-write-wins ordering rather than
1507    /// falling back to `SystemTime::now()`.
1508    ///
1509    /// Row tombstones are emitted as `Value::Tombstone(RowTombstone)` with their
1510    /// actual `deletion_time`.  Cell tombstones within live rows are stored as
1511    /// `Value::Tombstone(CellTombstone)` inside the `Value::Map`, again carrying
1512    /// the cell-level deletion timestamp.
1513    ///
1514    /// The `row_timestamp_micros` in the returned tuple is the row-level write
1515    /// timestamp decoded from the `HAS_TIMESTAMP` field in the row header
1516    /// (`min_timestamp + delta`).  For row tombstones the same timestamp also
1517    /// appears in `TombstoneInfo::deletion_time`.
1518    ///
1519    /// Normal user-facing scan/get paths should use [`parse_block`] instead.
1520    /// (Issue #505)
1521    pub fn parse_block_with_timestamps(
1522        &self,
1523        data: &[u8],
1524        schema: Option<&TableSchema>,
1525        reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
1526    ) -> Result<Vec<(TableId, RowKey, Value, i64)>> {
1527        // Thin wrapper that collects the streaming emit variant into a Vec, so
1528        // every existing caller/test is byte-for-byte unchanged (issue #827).
1529        let mut results: Vec<(TableId, RowKey, Value, i64)> = Vec::new();
1530        self.parse_block_with_timestamps_emit(data, schema, reader, |entry| {
1531            results.push(entry);
1532            Ok(std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(()))
1533        })?;
1534        Ok(results)
1535    }
1536
1537    /// Streaming variant of [`parse_block_with_timestamps`]: invokes `emit` for
1538    /// each parsed `(TableId, RowKey, Value, row_timestamp_micros)` entry rather
1539    /// than collecting into a `Vec`, so the compaction read path can forward
1540    /// rows into a bounded channel without materialising the whole block at once
1541    /// (issue #827). Returning `ControlFlow::Break` from `emit` stops parsing
1542    /// early — used when the streaming consumer is dropped.
1543    ///
1544    /// The tombstone/timestamp semantics are byte-identical to
1545    /// [`parse_block_with_timestamps`] (Issue #505/#533): a row tombstone is
1546    /// emitted as `Value::Tombstone` carrying its `markedForDeleteAt`, and the
1547    /// fourth tuple element is the row write timestamp for live rows.
1548    pub fn parse_block_with_timestamps_emit<F>(
1549        &self,
1550        data: &[u8],
1551        schema: Option<&TableSchema>,
1552        reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
1553        mut emit: F,
1554    ) -> Result<()>
1555    where
1556        F: FnMut((TableId, RowKey, Value, i64)) -> Result<std::ops::ControlFlow<()>>,
1557    {
1558        if data.is_empty() {
1559            return Ok(());
1560        }
1561
1562        let schema = schema.ok_or_else(|| {
1563            Error::schema(format!(
1564                "V5CompressedLegacy (compaction) format requires schema for {}.{}",
1565                self.keyspace, self.table_name
1566            ))
1567        })?;
1568
1569        let mut offset = 0;
1570        let mut skipped_partitions = 0;
1571
1572        // Wrap `emit` so a Break is observable here as well as inside the
1573        // one-partition parser (which stops its inner row loop on Break). This
1574        // lets the outer loop terminate promptly when the consumer is dropped.
1575        // `Cell` so the wrapping closure can borrow it shared while the outer
1576        // loop also reads it between calls.
1577        let broke = std::cell::Cell::new(false);
1578        let mut tracking_emit = |entry| -> Result<std::ops::ControlFlow<()>> {
1579            let flow = emit(entry)?;
1580            if matches!(flow, std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(())) {
1581                broke.set(true);
1582            }
1583            Ok(flow)
1584        };
1585
1586        while offset < data.len() {
1587            match self.parse_one_partition_with_timestamps(
1588                &data[offset..],
1589                Some(schema),
1590                reader,
1591                // The whole block is present; never request a refill. A trailing
1592                // parse failure is terminal here (matches the legacy
1593                // `Err(_) => break` behaviour of the original loop).
1594                true,
1595                &mut tracking_emit,
1596            )? {
1597                ParseStep::Emitted(consumed) => {
1598                    if consumed == 0 {
1599                        // Defensive: avoid an infinite loop on a zero-byte
1600                        // partition (should not happen — a header is >= 2 bytes).
1601                        skipped_partitions += 1;
1602                        offset += 1;
1603                    } else {
1604                        offset += consumed;
1605                    }
1606                }
1607                // `at_final_chunk = true` collapses NeedMore into Done: there is
1608                // no further chunk to append, so a truncated tail is end-of-data.
1609                ParseStep::NeedMore | ParseStep::Done => break,
1610            }
1611            // Propagate an early Break from `emit` (consumer dropped).
1612            if broke.get() {
1613                break;
1614            }
1615        }
1616
1617        if skipped_partitions > 0 {
1618            log::warn!(
1619                "V5CompressedLegacy (compaction): skipped {} malformed partitions",
1620                skipped_partitions
1621            );
1622        }
1623
1624        Ok(())
1625    }
1626
1627    /// Parse exactly ONE partition from the front of `data`, emitting each row
1628    /// via `emit`, and report how the parse terminated (issue #827).
1629    ///
1630    /// This isolates the body of the outer partition loop so the sliding-window
1631    /// compaction driver can drain one partition at a time and `drain(0..consumed)`
1632    /// from its window between calls. The crucial distinction over the legacy
1633    /// monolithic loop is `NeedMore` vs `Done`:
1634    ///
1635    /// - [`ParseStep::Emitted(consumed)`] — a full partition was parsed and
1636    ///   terminated by an END_OF_PARTITION marker or a confirmed next-partition
1637    ///   header. `consumed` bytes may be drained from the window.
1638    /// - [`ParseStep::NeedMore`] — `data` is (possibly) truncated mid-partition
1639    ///   and `!at_final_chunk`, so the caller must append the next chunk and
1640    ///   retry. NEVER returned when `at_final_chunk` is true.
1641    /// - [`ParseStep::Done`] — genuine end of partitions, or (when
1642    ///   `at_final_chunk`) a trailing truncation that cannot be resolved by more
1643    ///   data. Terminal.
1644    ///
1645    /// `at_final_chunk` flips a mid-partition parse failure between a refill
1646    /// request (`NeedMore`) and a terminal stop. The legacy code conflated
1647    /// parse-error with end-of-partitions (`Err(_) => break`); doing that
1648    /// mid-stream would silently drop every partition after a chunk boundary, so
1649    /// we return `NeedMore` whenever the buffer may simply be truncated and we
1650    /// are not yet at the final chunk.
1651    pub fn parse_one_partition_with_timestamps<F>(
1652        &self,
1653        data: &[u8],
1654        schema: Option<&TableSchema>,
1655        reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
1656        at_final_chunk: bool,
1657        emit: &mut F,
1658    ) -> Result<ParseStep>
1659    where
1660        F: FnMut((TableId, RowKey, Value, i64)) -> Result<std::ops::ControlFlow<()>>,
1661    {
1662        if data.is_empty() {
1663            return Ok(ParseStep::Done);
1664        }
1665
1666        let schema = schema.ok_or_else(|| {
1667            Error::schema(format!(
1668                "V5CompressedLegacy (compaction) format requires schema for {}.{}",
1669                self.keyspace, self.table_name
1670            ))
1671        })?;
1672
1673        let table_id = TableId::new(format!("{}.{}", self.keyspace, self.table_name));
1674
1675        const CASSANDRA_MAX_KEY_SIZE: usize = 65536;
1676        const FORMAT_MAX_KEY_SIZE: usize = 255;
1677
1678        // A partition header is at least flags(1) + key_len(1). If we cannot even
1679        // read those two bytes, we are truncated: request more unless final.
1680        if data.len() < 2 {
1681            return Ok(if at_final_chunk {
1682                ParseStep::Done
1683            } else {
1684                ParseStep::NeedMore
1685            });
1686        }
1687
1688        let key_len = data[1] as usize;
1689        let header_min_size = 1 + 1 + key_len + 4 + 8;
1690
1691        // Invalid header shape (zero/over-long key) → malformed; advance by one
1692        // byte so the outer loop can resynchronise. Returning Emitted(1) here
1693        // mirrors the legacy `offset += 1; continue` skip-a-byte recovery.
1694        if key_len == 0 || key_len > FORMAT_MAX_KEY_SIZE.min(CASSANDRA_MAX_KEY_SIZE) {
1695            return Ok(ParseStep::Emitted(1));
1696        }
1697
1698        // Header declared but not fully present in `data` → truncated mid-header.
1699        if header_min_size > data.len() {
1700            return Ok(if at_final_chunk {
1701                // No more bytes will ever arrive; the legacy loop treated this
1702                // as the end of parseable partitions.
1703                ParseStep::Done
1704            } else {
1705                ParseStep::NeedMore
1706            });
1707        }
1708
1709        let (partition_key, mut offset) = match self.parse_partition_header(data, 0) {
1710            Ok(v) => v,
1711            Err(_) => {
1712                // Fixed header bytes are present but did not parse: skip a byte
1713                // to resynchronise — matching the legacy
1714                // `Err(_) => { offset += 1; continue }` recovery.
1715                return Ok(ParseStep::Emitted(1));
1716            }
1717        };
1718
1719        let mut static_cells: HashMap<String, Value> = HashMap::new();
1720
1721        // Finding 1 (#827): buffer this partition's emitted rows locally and only
1722        // forward them to the external `emit` once the partition is CONFIRMED
1723        // complete (a `ParseStep::Emitted` return). If the buffer is truncated
1724        // mid-partition (`NeedMore`) after one or more rows were parsed, we must
1725        // emit NOTHING and let the caller refill and re-parse this partition from
1726        // its start — otherwise the already-forwarded rows would be re-emitted on
1727        // the retry, duplicating them in the streaming compaction output.
1728        //
1729        // The buffer is bounded by ONE partition's rows (the documented
1730        // `max_partition_size` bound), not the whole file, so memory stays
1731        // bounded as required by the #827 deliverable.
1732        let mut pending: Vec<(TableId, RowKey, Value, i64)> = Vec::new();
1733
1734        // Flush the buffered rows to the external `emit`, honouring an early
1735        // `Break`. Returns the `ParseStep` to surface to the caller: on `Break`
1736        // we still report the bytes consumed for this (complete) partition so the
1737        // caller drains correctly, but stop forwarding the remaining buffered
1738        // rows. `flushed_break` becomes true so the driver can stop promptly.
1739        macro_rules! flush_and_emitted {
1740            ($consumed:expr, $pending:expr, $emit:expr) => {{
1741                for entry in $pending.drain(..) {
1742                    match $emit(entry)? {
1743                        std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(()) => {}
1744                        std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(()) => break,
1745                    }
1746                }
1747                Ok(ParseStep::Emitted($consumed))
1748            }};
1749        }
1750
1751        loop {
1752            // END_OF_PARTITION (0x01): partition complete, consume the marker.
1753            if offset < data.len() && Self::is_end_of_partition(data[offset]) {
1754                offset += 1;
1755                return flush_and_emitted!(offset, pending, emit);
1756            }
1757
1758            // Consumed everything but never saw END_OF_PARTITION: the partition
1759            // may continue in the next chunk. On NeedMore emit NOTHING (drop the
1760            // buffered rows) so the caller can refill and re-parse from the start
1761            // without duplicating already-buffered rows (Finding 1).
1762            if offset >= data.len() {
1763                if at_final_chunk {
1764                    return flush_and_emitted!(offset, pending, emit);
1765                }
1766                return Ok(ParseStep::NeedMore);
1767            }
1768
1769            if Self::is_range_tombstone_marker(data[offset]) {
1770                match self.skip_range_tombstone_marker(data, offset, schema) {
1771                    Ok(next_offset) => {
1772                        offset = next_offset;
1773                        continue;
1774                    }
1775                    Err(_) => {
1776                        // Marker body truncated? request more unless final.
1777                        if at_final_chunk {
1778                            return flush_and_emitted!(offset, pending, emit);
1779                        }
1780                        return Ok(ParseStep::NeedMore);
1781                    }
1782                }
1783            }
1784
1785            match self.parse_row_data_with_offset(data, offset, Some(schema), reader, false) {
1786                Ok((
1787                    mut cells,
1788                    _row_cell_meta,
1789                    row_header_opt,
1790                    next_offset,
1791                    is_static,
1792                    _complex_meta,
1793                )) => {
1794                    offset = next_offset;
1795
1796                    // For a row tombstone the authoritative timestamp is
1797                    // markedForDeleteAt (HAS_TIMESTAMP is absent for pure row
1798                    // deletes). For a live row it is the row write timestamp.
1799                    // Both the merger tuple `row_ts` and the emitted
1800                    // Value::Tombstone must agree, so resolve once here (#505).
1801                    let row_tombstone = row_header_opt.as_ref().filter(|h| h.is_row_tombstone());
1802                    // Issue #932: a HAS_DELETION row may ALSO carry a liveness
1803                    // timestamp (surviving cells written strictly after the
1804                    // deletion). Prefer the liveness timestamp as the row
1805                    // timestamp so those cells inherit it and are NOT shadowed by
1806                    // the older row deletion during reconcile; fall back to
1807                    // markedForDeleteAt only for a PURE row tombstone (which has no
1808                    // HAS_TIMESTAMP).
1809                    let row_ts = row_header_opt
1810                        .as_ref()
1811                        .and_then(|h| h.timestamp)
1812                        .or_else(|| row_tombstone.map(|h| h.row_tombstone_deletion_time()))
1813                        .unwrap_or(0);
1814
1815                    if is_static {
1816                        static_cells = cells;
1817                    } else {
1818                        for (k, v) in &static_cells {
1819                            cells.entry(k.clone()).or_insert_with(|| v.clone());
1820                        }
1821
1822                        // Row tombstone → Value::Tombstone(markedForDeleteAt).
1823                        // Issue #932: unless the row ALSO carries surviving cells
1824                        // (newer than the deletion), in which case it displays as a
1825                        // live row — the deletion shadows only already-absent older
1826                        // cells.
1827                        let has_data_cell = row_has_non_key_cell(&cells, schema);
1828                        let row_value = if row_tombstone.is_some() && !has_data_cell {
1829                            row_tombstone
1830                                .map(|h| h.row_tombstone())
1831                                .unwrap_or(Value::Null)
1832                        } else if cells.is_empty() {
1833                            Value::Null
1834                        } else {
1835                            let mut map_entries: Vec<(Value, Value)> = cells
1836                                .into_iter()
1837                                .map(|(name, value)| (Value::Text(name), value))
1838                                .collect();
1839                            map_entries.sort_by(|a, b| {
1840                                let a_key = if let Value::Text(s) = &a.0 {
1841                                    s.as_str()
1842                                } else {
1843                                    ""
1844                                };
1845                                let b_key = if let Value::Text(s) = &b.0 {
1846                                    s.as_str()
1847                                } else {
1848                                    ""
1849                                };
1850                                a_key.cmp(b_key)
1851                            });
1852                            Value::Map(map_entries)
1853                        };
1854
1855                        // Finding 1: buffer the row instead of forwarding it now.
1856                        // It is flushed to `emit` only when the partition is
1857                        // confirmed complete (a `flush_and_emitted!` return). A
1858                        // mid-partition `NeedMore` discards `pending` and the
1859                        // caller re-parses from the partition start.
1860                        pending.push((table_id.clone(), partition_key.clone(), row_value, row_ts));
1861                    }
1862
1863                    if offset >= data.len() {
1864                        // End of the buffer without an explicit END_OF_PARTITION:
1865                        // the partition may continue in the next chunk.
1866                        if at_final_chunk {
1867                            return flush_and_emitted!(offset, pending, emit);
1868                        }
1869                        return Ok(ParseStep::NeedMore);
1870                    }
1871                    if self.peek_is_partition_header(data, offset) {
1872                        // Next partition starts here — current one is complete.
1873                        return flush_and_emitted!(offset, pending, emit);
1874                    }
1875                }
1876                Err(_) => {
1877                    // A row failed to parse. The legacy loop unconditionally
1878                    // `break`s here (end-of-partition). Mid-stream that may
1879                    // instead be a row straddling the chunk boundary, so request
1880                    // more bytes unless this is the final chunk.
1881                    if at_final_chunk {
1882                        return flush_and_emitted!(offset, pending, emit);
1883                    }
1884                    return Ok(ParseStep::NeedMore);
1885                }
1886            }
1887        }
1888    }
1889
1890    /// Build a [`CompactionRow`] from a parsed row's pieces (epic #899).
1891    ///
1892    /// `cells` is the collapsed column→value map (simple columns plus the
1893    /// collapsed `Value` for each complex column); `cell_meta` carries per-simple
1894    /// -cell write timestamps / TTLs; `complex` carries the per-element capture
1895    /// for the complex columns. The complex columns are split out of `cells` (the
1896    /// collapsed complex `Value` is dropped in favour of the per-element cells).
1897    ///
1898    /// A row tombstone produces [`CompactionRowData::Tombstone`]; an empty row
1899    /// (no cells, no tombstone) produces an empty `Live`.
1900    fn build_compaction_row_data(
1901        &self,
1902        cells: HashMap<String, Value>,
1903        cell_meta: Option<HashMap<String, CellWriteMetadata>>,
1904        complex: CompactionComplexColumns,
1905        row_header_opt: &Option<RowHeader>,
1906        row_ts: i64,
1907        schema: &TableSchema,
1908    ) -> crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::CompactionRowData {
1909        use crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::{
1910            CompactionRowData, ComplexColumn, SimpleCell,
1911        };
1912
1913        // Issue #932: a row with `HAS_DELETION` may ALSO carry surviving cells
1914        // (cells written strictly after the row deletion). The row deletion is
1915        // captured here either as the coexisting `row_deletion` on a `Live` row
1916        // (when data cells survive) or as a pure `Tombstone` (when only the
1917        // deletion remains). The decision is made AFTER building the cell sets so
1918        // we can tell whether any NON-clustering data cell survived.
1919        let row_deletion: Option<(i64, i32)> = row_header_opt
1920            .as_ref()
1921            .filter(|h| h.is_row_tombstone())
1922            .map(|h| {
1923                (
1924                    h.row_tombstone_deletion_time(),
1925                    // localDeletionTime in SECONDS (GC-grace clock). Preserve the
1926                    // far-future [2^31, 2^32) encoding via wrapping `as u32 as i32`.
1927                    h.local_deletion_time.unwrap_or(0),
1928                )
1929            });
1930
1931        // Build complex columns (sorted by name for deterministic output, mirroring
1932        // the collapsed-value path's column ordering).
1933        let mut complex_cols: Vec<ComplexColumn> = complex
1934            .into_iter()
1935            .map(
1936                |(column, (complex_deletion, elements, collapsed_value))| ComplexColumn {
1937                    column,
1938                    complex_deletion,
1939                    elements,
1940                    collapsed_value,
1941                },
1942            )
1943            .collect();
1944        complex_cols.sort_by(|a, b| a.column.cmp(&b.column));
1945
1946        // Simple cells are every collapsed cell whose column is NOT a complex
1947        // column. Per-cell timestamp / ttl / local-deletion-time come from
1948        // `cell_meta` when present, else inherit the row timestamp.
1949        let complex_names: std::collections::HashSet<&str> =
1950            complex_cols.iter().map(|c| c.column.as_str()).collect();
1951
1952        let mut simple_cells: Vec<SimpleCell> = cells
1953            .into_iter()
1954            .filter(|(name, _)| !complex_names.contains(name.as_str()))
1955            .map(|(column, value)| {
1956                let (timestamp, ttl, local_deletion_time) =
1957                    match cell_meta.as_ref().and_then(|m| m.get(&column)) {
1958                        Some(meta) => {
1959                            let ttl = meta.expiration.as_ref().map(|e| e.ttl_seconds as u32);
1960                            let ldt = meta
1961                                .expiration
1962                                .as_ref()
1963                                .map(|e| e.expires_at_seconds as u32 as i32);
1964                            (meta.write_timestamp_micros, ttl, ldt)
1965                        }
1966                        None => (row_ts, None, None),
1967                    };
1968                SimpleCell {
1969                    column,
1970                    value,
1971                    timestamp,
1972                    ttl,
1973                    local_deletion_time,
1974                }
1975            })
1976            .collect();
1977        simple_cells.sort_by(|a, b| a.column.cmp(&b.column));
1978
1979        // Issue #932: a row deletion either COEXISTS with surviving data cells
1980        // (kept as `Live { row_deletion: Some(..) }`) or — when no NON-primary-key
1981        // cell and no complex element survives — is a pure row tombstone (kept as
1982        // `Tombstone`, preserving the #912 clustering-prefix capture). The earlier
1983        // code always took the `Tombstone` branch, DROPPING surviving cells and
1984        // letting older cells of other columns resurrect in a partial compaction.
1985        if let Some((deletion_time, local_deletion_time)) = row_deletion {
1986            let primary_key: std::collections::HashSet<&str> = schema
1987                .partition_keys
1988                .iter()
1989                .map(|k| k.name.as_str())
1990                .chain(schema.clustering_keys.iter().map(|c| c.name.as_str()))
1991                .collect();
1992            let has_simple_data = simple_cells
1993                .iter()
1994                .any(|c| !primary_key.contains(c.column.as_str()));
1995            let has_complex_data = complex_cols
1996                .iter()
1997                .any(|c| !c.elements.is_empty() || c.complex_deletion.is_some());
1998
1999            if !has_simple_data && !has_complex_data {
2000                // Pure row tombstone: rebuild the clustering prefix in schema
2001                // order from the surfaced clustering pseudo-cells (#912). A
2002                // missing clustering column falls back to the `None` bucket.
2003                let mut clustering: Vec<(String, Value)> =
2004                    Vec::with_capacity(schema.clustering_keys.len());
2005                for ck in &schema.clustering_keys {
2006                    match simple_cells.iter().find(|c| c.column == ck.name) {
2007                        Some(c) => clustering.push((ck.name.clone(), c.value.clone())),
2008                        None => {
2009                            clustering.clear();
2010                            break;
2011                        }
2012                    }
2013                }
2014                return CompactionRowData::Tombstone {
2015                    deletion_time,
2016                    local_deletion_time,
2017                    clustering,
2018                };
2019            }
2020        }
2021
2022        CompactionRowData::Live {
2023            simple: simple_cells,
2024            complex: complex_cols,
2025            row_deletion,
2026        }
2027    }
2028
2029    /// Parse all partitions in a decompressed block into per-element
2030    /// [`CompactionRow`]s (epic #899, compaction-only). Thin Vec wrapper over
2031    /// [`Self::parse_block_for_compaction_emit`].
2032    pub fn parse_block_for_compaction(
2033        &self,
2034        data: &[u8],
2035        schema: Option<&TableSchema>,
2036        reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
2037    ) -> Result<Vec<crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::CompactionRow>> {
2038        let mut results = Vec::new();
2039        self.parse_block_for_compaction_emit(data, schema, reader, |row| {
2040            results.push(row);
2041            Ok(std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(()))
2042        })?;
2043        Ok(results)
2044    }
2045
2046    /// Streaming per-element compaction variant of
2047    /// [`Self::parse_block_with_timestamps_emit`]: emits a [`CompactionRow`]
2048    /// (per-element complex cells + real complex deletion) per row (epic #899).
2049    pub fn parse_block_for_compaction_emit<F>(
2050        &self,
2051        data: &[u8],
2052        schema: Option<&TableSchema>,
2053        reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
2054        mut emit: F,
2055    ) -> Result<()>
2056    where
2057        F: FnMut(
2058            crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::CompactionRow,
2059        ) -> Result<std::ops::ControlFlow<()>>,
2060    {
2061        if data.is_empty() {
2062            return Ok(());
2063        }
2064
2065        let schema = schema.ok_or_else(|| {
2066            Error::schema(format!(
2067                "V5CompressedLegacy (compaction) format requires schema for {}.{}",
2068                self.keyspace, self.table_name
2069            ))
2070        })?;
2071
2072        let mut offset = 0;
2073        let mut skipped_partitions = 0;
2074
2075        let broke = std::cell::Cell::new(false);
2076        let mut tracking_emit = |row| -> Result<std::ops::ControlFlow<()>> {
2077            let flow = emit(row)?;
2078            if matches!(flow, std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(())) {
2079                broke.set(true);
2080            }
2081            Ok(flow)
2082        };
2083
2084        while offset < data.len() {
2085            match self.parse_one_partition_for_compaction(
2086                &data[offset..],
2087                Some(schema),
2088                reader,
2089                true,
2090                &mut tracking_emit,
2091            )? {
2092                ParseStep::Emitted(consumed) => {
2093                    if consumed == 0 {
2094                        skipped_partitions += 1;
2095                        offset += 1;
2096                    } else {
2097                        offset += consumed;
2098                    }
2099                }
2100                ParseStep::NeedMore | ParseStep::Done => break,
2101            }
2102            if broke.get() {
2103                break;
2104            }
2105        }
2106
2107        if skipped_partitions > 0 {
2108            log::warn!(
2109                "V5CompressedLegacy (compaction): skipped {} malformed partitions",
2110                skipped_partitions
2111            );
2112        }
2113
2114        Ok(())
2115    }
2116
2117    /// Per-element compaction counterpart of
2118    /// [`Self::parse_one_partition_with_timestamps`] (epic #899). Identical
2119    /// sliding-window / `ParseStep` / buffering semantics, but emits a
2120    /// [`CompactionRow`] carrying per-element complex cells and the real complex
2121    /// deletion instead of the collapsed `(RowKey, Value, ts)` tuple.
2122    pub fn parse_one_partition_for_compaction<F>(
2123        &self,
2124        data: &[u8],
2125        schema: Option<&TableSchema>,
2126        reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
2127        at_final_chunk: bool,
2128        emit: &mut F,
2129    ) -> Result<ParseStep>
2130    where
2131        F: FnMut(
2132            crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::CompactionRow,
2133        ) -> Result<std::ops::ControlFlow<()>>,
2134    {
2135        use crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::CompactionRow;
2136
2137        if data.is_empty() {
2138            return Ok(ParseStep::Done);
2139        }
2140
2141        let schema = schema.ok_or_else(|| {
2142            Error::schema(format!(
2143                "V5CompressedLegacy (compaction) format requires schema for {}.{}",
2144                self.keyspace, self.table_name
2145            ))
2146        })?;
2147
2148        const CASSANDRA_MAX_KEY_SIZE: usize = 65536;
2149        const FORMAT_MAX_KEY_SIZE: usize = 255;
2150
2151        if data.len() < 2 {
2152            return Ok(if at_final_chunk {
2153                ParseStep::Done
2154            } else {
2155                ParseStep::NeedMore
2156            });
2157        }
2158
2159        let key_len = data[1] as usize;
2160        let header_min_size = 1 + 1 + key_len + 4 + 8;
2161
2162        if key_len == 0 || key_len > FORMAT_MAX_KEY_SIZE.min(CASSANDRA_MAX_KEY_SIZE) {
2163            return Ok(ParseStep::Emitted(1));
2164        }
2165
2166        if header_min_size > data.len() {
2167            return Ok(if at_final_chunk {
2168                ParseStep::Done
2169            } else {
2170                ParseStep::NeedMore
2171            });
2172        }
2173
2174        let (partition_key, mut offset) = match self.parse_partition_header(data, 0) {
2175            Ok(v) => v,
2176            Err(_) => return Ok(ParseStep::Emitted(1)),
2177        };
2178
2179        // Static cells are kept as the collapsed map so they can be folded into
2180        // subsequent clustering rows, exactly like the legacy path. They are
2181        // surfaced as simple cells on each emitted row.
2182        let mut static_cells: HashMap<String, Value> = HashMap::new();
2183        let mut pending: Vec<CompactionRow> = Vec::new();
2184
2185        // In-flight range tombstone start bound (issue #933). A range tombstone is
2186        // a pair of adjacent bound markers (start then end), or a sequence of
2187        // boundary markers that close one range and open the next. We buffer the
2188        // open start here and emit a complete `CompactionRowData::RangeMarker` when
2189        // the matching end/boundary arrives. Local to this call so it is re-derived
2190        // from the partition start on every sliding-window re-parse (the `pending`
2191        // rows are only flushed on a clean `Emitted`).
2192        //
2193        // Tuple: (start bound, deletion_time µs, local_deletion_time s).
2194        let mut pending_range_start: Option<(
2195            crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::CompactionBound,
2196            i64,
2197            i32,
2198        )> = None;
2199
2200        // Build a `CompactionBound` from decoded clustering prefix values. The
2201        // writer emits an OPEN bound (Bottom/Top) as an inclusive bound with zero
2202        // clustering values, so an empty prefix decodes to Bottom (start) / Top
2203        // (end). A non-empty prefix pairs each value with its schema clustering
2204        // column name (positionally; bounds may be PREFIX-length).
2205        let make_bound = |values: Vec<Value>, inclusive: bool, is_start: bool| {
2206            use crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::CompactionBound;
2207            if values.is_empty() {
2208                return if is_start {
2209                    CompactionBound::Bottom
2210                } else {
2211                    CompactionBound::Top
2212                };
2213            }
2214            let pairs: Vec<(String, Value)> = values
2215                .into_iter()
2216                .enumerate()
2217                .map(|(i, v)| {
2218                    let name = schema
2219                        .clustering_keys
2220                        .get(i)
2221                        .map(|c| c.name.clone())
2222                        .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("ck{i}"));
2223                    (name, v)
2224                })
2225                .collect();
2226            if inclusive {
2227                CompactionBound::Inclusive(pairs)
2228            } else {
2229                CompactionBound::Exclusive(pairs)
2230            }
2231        };
2232
2233        macro_rules! flush_and_emitted {
2234            ($consumed:expr, $pending:expr, $emit:expr) => {{
2235                for row in $pending.drain(..) {
2236                    match $emit(row)? {
2237                        std::ops::ControlFlow::Continue(()) => {}
2238                        std::ops::ControlFlow::Break(()) => break,
2239                    }
2240                }
2241                Ok(ParseStep::Emitted($consumed))
2242            }};
2243        }
2244
2245        loop {
2246            if offset < data.len() && Self::is_end_of_partition(data[offset]) {
2247                offset += 1;
2248                return flush_and_emitted!(offset, pending, emit);
2249            }
2250
2251            if offset >= data.len() {
2252                if at_final_chunk {
2253                    return flush_and_emitted!(offset, pending, emit);
2254                }
2255                return Ok(ParseStep::NeedMore);
2256            }
2257
2258            if Self::is_range_tombstone_marker(data[offset]) {
2259                // Issue #933: parse the range-tombstone bound marker and pair it
2260                // into a complete `RangeMarker` so the merge can shadow covered
2261                // cells AND re-emit the surviving marker (previously SKIPPED, which
2262                // dropped the tombstone entirely).
2263                let (bound_values, bound_kind, (mfda_p, ldt_p), secondary, next_offset) =
2264                    match self.parse_range_tombstone_marker_with_ldt(data, offset, schema) {
2265                        Ok(v) => v,
2266                        Err(_) => {
2267                            // Truncated marker body at a chunk boundary (or corrupt
2268                            // at the final chunk): request more / flush, exactly as
2269                            // the prior skip path did.
2270                            if at_final_chunk {
2271                                return flush_and_emitted!(offset, pending, emit);
2272                            }
2273                            return Ok(ParseStep::NeedMore);
2274                        }
2275                    };
2276                offset = next_offset;
2277
2278                use crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::{
2279                    CompactionBound, CompactionRowData,
2280                };
2281
2282                // Emit a complete range tombstone given a (start, deletion) and an
2283                // end bound + the end's deletion time/ldt.
2284                let mut emit_range =
2285                    |start: CompactionBound, end: CompactionBound, dt: i64, ldt: i32| {
2286                        pending.push(CompactionRow {
2287                            key: partition_key.clone(),
2288                            row_timestamp: dt,
2289                            row_data: CompactionRowData::RangeMarker {
2290                                start,
2291                                end,
2292                                deletion_time: dt,
2293                                local_deletion_time: ldt,
2294                            },
2295                        });
2296                    };
2297
2298                // ClusteringPrefix.Kind ordinals:
2299                //   0 EXCL_END, 1 INCL_START, 2 EXCL_END_INCL_START_BOUNDARY,
2300                //   5 INCL_END_EXCL_START_BOUNDARY, 6 INCL_END, 7 EXCL_START.
2301                match bound_kind {
2302                    1 | 7 => {
2303                        // Simple start bound: buffer until the matching end.
2304                        let start = make_bound(bound_values, bound_kind == 1, true);
2305                        pending_range_start = Some((start, mfda_p, ldt_p));
2306                    }
2307                    0 | 6 => {
2308                        // Simple end bound: close the buffered start.
2309                        let end = make_bound(bound_values, bound_kind == 6, false);
2310                        let start = pending_range_start
2311                            .take()
2312                            .map(|(s, _, _)| s)
2313                            .unwrap_or(CompactionBound::Bottom);
2314                        emit_range(start, end, mfda_p, ldt_p);
2315                    }
2316                    2 | 5 => {
2317                        // Boundary marker: primary closes the previous range, the
2318                        // secondary opens the next. kind 2 = EXCL_END + INCL_START,
2319                        // kind 5 = INCL_END + EXCL_START.
2320                        let end_inclusive = bound_kind == 5;
2321                        if let Some((start, _, _)) = pending_range_start.take() {
2322                            let end = make_bound(bound_values.clone(), end_inclusive, false);
2323                            emit_range(start, end, mfda_p, ldt_p);
2324                        }
2325                        let (new_mfda, new_ldt) = secondary.unwrap_or((mfda_p, ldt_p));
2326                        let new_start = make_bound(bound_values, bound_kind == 2, true);
2327                        pending_range_start = Some((new_start, new_mfda, new_ldt));
2328                    }
2329                    _ => {
2330                        // Unknown bound kind: skip it rather than mis-parse the
2331                        // partition (the offset already advanced past the marker).
2332                    }
2333                }
2334                continue;
2335            }
2336
2337            // Compaction mode: capture per-column complex elements and request
2338            // per-cell metadata so simple cells carry per-cell timestamps/TTLs.
2339            let mut complex_capture: CompactionComplexColumns = HashMap::new();
2340            match self.parse_row_data_with_offset_impl(
2341                data,
2342                offset,
2343                Some(schema),
2344                reader,
2345                true,
2346                Some(&mut complex_capture),
2347            ) {
2348                Ok((
2349                    mut cells,
2350                    cell_meta,
2351                    row_header_opt,
2352                    next_offset,
2353                    is_static,
2354                    _complex_meta,
2355                )) => {
2356                    offset = next_offset;
2357
2358                    let row_tombstone = row_header_opt.as_ref().filter(|h| h.is_row_tombstone());
2359                    // Issue #932: a HAS_DELETION row may ALSO carry a liveness
2360                    // timestamp (surviving cells written strictly after the
2361                    // deletion). Prefer the liveness timestamp as the row
2362                    // timestamp so those cells inherit it and are NOT shadowed by
2363                    // the older row deletion during reconcile; fall back to
2364                    // markedForDeleteAt only for a PURE row tombstone (which has no
2365                    // HAS_TIMESTAMP).
2366                    let row_ts = row_header_opt
2367                        .as_ref()
2368                        .and_then(|h| h.timestamp)
2369                        .or_else(|| row_tombstone.map(|h| h.row_tombstone_deletion_time()))
2370                        .unwrap_or(0);
2371
2372                    if is_static {
2373                        static_cells = cells;
2374                    } else {
2375                        for (k, v) in &static_cells {
2376                            cells.entry(k.clone()).or_insert_with(|| v.clone());
2377                        }
2378
2379                        let row_data = self.build_compaction_row_data(
2380                            cells,
2381                            cell_meta,
2382                            complex_capture,
2383                            &row_header_opt,
2384                            row_ts,
2385                            schema,
2386                        );
2387
2388                        pending.push(CompactionRow {
2389                            key: partition_key.clone(),
2390                            row_timestamp: row_ts,
2391                            row_data,
2392                        });
2393                    }
2394
2395                    if offset >= data.len() {
2396                        if at_final_chunk {
2397                            return flush_and_emitted!(offset, pending, emit);
2398                        }
2399                        return Ok(ParseStep::NeedMore);
2400                    }
2401                    if self.peek_is_partition_header(data, offset) {
2402                        return flush_and_emitted!(offset, pending, emit);
2403                    }
2404                }
2405                Err(_) => {
2406                    if at_final_chunk {
2407                        return flush_and_emitted!(offset, pending, emit);
2408                    }
2409                    return Ok(ParseStep::NeedMore);
2410                }
2411            }
2412        }
2413    }
2414
2415    /// Parse row flags only (Issue #213 fix: split from parse_row_header)
2416    ///
2417    /// # Format
2418    /// ```text
2419    /// [row_flags: u8]
2420    /// [extended_flags: u8 if 0x80 set]
2421    /// ```
2422    ///
2423    /// Returns (row_flags, extended_flags, bytes_consumed)
2424    fn parse_row_flags(&self, data: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Result<(u8, Option<u8>, usize)> {
2425        let mut pos = offset;
2426
2427        // Read row flags
2428        if pos >= data.len() {
2429            return Err(Error::corruption(
2430                "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end reading row flags",
2431            ));
2432        }
2433        let row_flags = data[pos];
2434        pos += 1;
2435
2436        debug!(
2437            "V5CompressedLegacy: Row flags=0x{:02x} at offset {}",
2438            row_flags, offset
2439        );
2440
2441        // Read extended flags if present
2442        let extended_flags = if (row_flags & ROW_HAS_EXTENDED_FLAGS) != 0 {
2443            if pos >= data.len() {
2444                return Err(Error::corruption(
2445                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end reading extended flags",
2446                ));
2447            }
2448            let ext = data[pos];
2449            pos += 1;
2450            Some(ext)
2451        } else {
2452            None
2453        };
2454
2455        let bytes_consumed = pos - offset;
2456        Ok((row_flags, extended_flags, bytes_consumed))
2457    }
2458
2459    /// Check if row flags indicate end of partition (Issue #229 fix)
2460    ///
2461    /// Per Cassandra's UnfilteredSerializer.java, END_OF_PARTITION is written as exactly 0x01
2462    /// by the `writeEndOfPartition()` method. The Cassandra source uses a bitmask check
2463    /// `(flags & END_OF_PARTITION) != 0`, but in practice the marker is always 0x01.
2464    ///
2465    /// We use an EXACT match to 0x01 to avoid false positives with row data that
2466    /// incidentally has bit 0 set (e.g., 0xb7 which would wrongly match a bitmask check).
2467    ///
2468    /// When END_OF_PARTITION (0x01) is detected, nothing follows the flags byte.
2469    /// The partition is complete and parsing should move to the next partition.
2470    #[inline]
2471    fn is_end_of_partition(flags: u8) -> bool {
2472        flags == END_OF_PARTITION // Exact match, not bitmask
2473    }
2474
2475    /// Check if row flags indicate a range tombstone marker (not a data row)
2476    ///
2477    /// Per Cassandra's UnfilteredSerializer.java, IS_MARKER (0x02) indicates a range
2478    /// tombstone boundary. The marker flag can be combined with other metadata flags
2479    /// (e.g., 0x52 = IS_MARKER | deletion metadata, 0x7a, 0x36, etc.).
2480    ///
2481    /// Issue #258 fix: Use bitwise AND to detect markers with additional flags.
2482    /// Previously used exact match (flags == 0x02) which missed markers like 0x52.
2483    #[inline]
2484    fn is_range_tombstone_marker(flags: u8) -> bool {
2485        // Check if IS_MARKER bit is set, but END_OF_PARTITION bit is NOT set
2486        // IS_MARKER = 0x02, END_OF_PARTITION = 0x01
2487        // If END_OF_PARTITION bit is set (even with other bits), it's end of partition, not a marker
2488        (flags & IS_MARKER) != 0 && (flags & END_OF_PARTITION) == 0
2489    }
2490
2491    /// Skip a range tombstone marker body (Issue #229 fix, VG6 fix)
2492    ///
2493    /// Range tombstone markers for SSTable format have this on-disk layout:
2494    ///   [flags: u8]                        ← IS_MARKER (0x02) bit set
2495    ///   [extended_flags: u8]               ← only if ROW_HAS_EXTENDED_FLAGS set
2496    ///   [bound_kind: u8]                   ← ordinal of ClusteringBoundOrBoundary.Kind
2497    ///   [cluster_count: u16 big-endian]    ← number of clustering values (bound.size())
2498    ///   [cluster_header: VUInt]            ← 2 bits per value (0=present, 1=empty, 2=null)
2499    ///   [cluster_values: ...]              ← type-specific bytes for non-null/non-empty values
2500    ///   [marker_body_size: VUInt]          ← size of the body that follows (including prev_size)
2501    ///   [prev_unfiltered_size: VUInt]      ← size of the previous unfiltered item
2502    ///   [marked_for_delete_at: VUInt]      ← timestamp delta from min_timestamp (µs)
2503    ///   [local_deletion_time: VUInt32]     ← seconds delta from min_local_deletion_time
2504    ///   [marked_for_delete_at2: VUInt]     ← ONLY for boundaries (kind 2 or 5)
2505    ///   [local_deletion_time2: VUInt32]    ← ONLY for boundaries (kind 2 or 5)
2506    ///
2507    /// Authority:
2508    ///   UnfilteredSerializer.java:282-303  (serialize(RangeTombstoneMarker, ...))
2509    ///   ClusteringBoundOrBoundary.Serializer.serialize (lines 103-107):
2510    ///     out.writeByte(bound.kind().ordinal())   ← kind byte
2511    ///     out.writeShort(bound.size())            ← u16 cluster count
2512    ///     ClusteringPrefix.serializer.serializeValuesWithoutSize(...)
2513    ///   SerializationHeader.writeDeletionTime (lines 180-183):
2514    ///     writeTimestamp → writeUnsignedVInt      ← VUInt, NOT ZigZag
2515    ///     writeLocalDeletionTime → writeUnsignedVInt32 ← VUInt, NOT ZigZag
2516    ///
2517    /// VG6 fix: The previous implementation had three bugs:
2518    ///   1. After kind byte: did not read the u16 cluster_count before the VUInt header.
2519    ///      The 2-byte short was being consumed as part of the clustering values, causing
2520    ///      all deletion-time bytes to be misaligned.
2521    ///   2. After clustering values: did not skip marker_body_size + prev_unfiltered_size
2522    ///      VUInts that precede the deletion times in SSTable format.
2523    ///   3. Used parse_vint (ZigZag) instead of parse_vuint (unsigned) for deletion times.
2524    ///
2525    /// Implementation strategy: use marker_body_size to skip the entire body
2526    /// (prev_size + deletion times) without manually decoding individual fields.
2527    fn skip_range_tombstone_marker(
2528        &self,
2529        data: &[u8],
2530        offset: usize,
2531        schema: &TableSchema,
2532    ) -> Result<usize> {
2533        let mut pos = offset;
2534
2535        if pos >= data.len() {
2536            return Err(Error::corruption(
2537                "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end at range tombstone marker",
2538            ));
2539        }
2540
2541        let marker_flags = data[pos];
2542        pos += 1; // Skip flags byte
2543
2544        log::debug!(
2545            "V5CompressedLegacy: Skipping range tombstone marker with flags=0x{:02x} at offset {}",
2546            marker_flags,
2547            offset
2548        );
2549
2550        // Extended flags if present (unlikely for markers, but handle it)
2551        if (marker_flags & ROW_HAS_EXTENDED_FLAGS) != 0 {
2552            if pos >= data.len() {
2553                return Err(Error::corruption(
2554                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end reading marker extended flags",
2555                ));
2556            }
2557            pos += 1;
2558        }
2559
2560        // Read bound kind byte.
2561        // Authority: ClusteringBoundOrBoundary.Serializer.serialize (line 104):
2562        //   out.writeByte(bound.kind().ordinal())
2563        //
2564        // Kind ordinals (ClusteringPrefix.java:67-81):
2565        //   0 = EXCL_END_BOUND (simple, 1 deletion time)
2566        //   1 = INCL_START_BOUND (simple, 1 deletion time)
2567        //   2 = EXCL_END_INCL_START_BOUNDARY (boundary, 2 deletion times)
2568        //   5 = INCL_END_EXCL_START_BOUNDARY (boundary, 2 deletion times)
2569        //   6 = INCL_END_BOUND (simple, 1 deletion time)
2570        //   7 = EXCL_START_BOUND (simple, 1 deletion time)
2571        if pos >= data.len() {
2572            return Err(Error::corruption(
2573                "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end reading range tombstone bound kind",
2574            ));
2575        }
2576        let bound_kind = data[pos];
2577        pos += 1;
2578
2579        log::debug!(
2580            "V5CompressedLegacy: Range tombstone bound_kind={}",
2581            bound_kind,
2582        );
2583
2584        // Read cluster count (u16 big-endian).
2585        // Authority: ClusteringBoundOrBoundary.Serializer.serialize (line 105):
2586        //   out.writeShort(bound.size())
2587        //
2588        // This is the number of clustering values in the bound. It is NOT the same as
2589        // schema.clustering_keys.len() — for regular rows, no count is written; for markers,
2590        // a u16 is always present. Failing to read this u16 causes all subsequent bytes to
2591        // be misaligned (the two count bytes get consumed as the VUInt header + first value
2592        // byte, producing garbage alignment).
2593        if pos + 2 > data.len() {
2594            return Err(Error::corruption(
2595                "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end reading range tombstone cluster count (u16)",
2596            ));
2597        }
2598        let cluster_count = u16::from_be_bytes([data[pos], data[pos + 1]]) as usize;
2599        pos += 2;
2600
2601        log::debug!(
2602            "V5CompressedLegacy: Range tombstone cluster_count={}",
2603            cluster_count,
2604        );
2605
2606        // Read the clustering VUInt header + clustering values.
2607        // Authority: ClusteringPrefix.Serializer.serializeValuesWithoutSize (lines 455-477):
2608        //   Writes VUInt header (2 bits per value, 0=present/1=empty/2=null), then value bytes.
2609        //
2610        // Use a truncated schema when cluster_count < schema.clustering_keys.len() to avoid
2611        // reading past the bound's bytes into the marker body (prefix bound case).
2612        if cluster_count > 0 {
2613            let prefix_schema_owned = Self::clustering_prefix_schema(schema, cluster_count);
2614            let effective_schema = prefix_schema_owned.as_ref().unwrap_or(schema);
2615            let (_, new_pos) = self.parse_clustering_prefix(data, pos, effective_schema)?;
2616            pos = new_pos;
2617        }
2618
2619        // Read marker_body_size and skip the body.
2620        // Authority: UnfilteredSerializer.java:291 (for SSTable format):
2621        //   out.writeUnsignedVInt(serializedMarkerBodySize(marker, header, previousUnfilteredSize, version))
2622        //   out.writeUnsignedVInt(previousUnfilteredSize)
2623        //   ... deletion time(s) ...
2624        //
2625        // serializedMarkerBodySize() returns the size of (prev_size + deletion_times).
2626        // So after reading marker_body_size, we can skip exactly that many bytes to reach
2627        // the next unfiltered item, without needing to decode individual deletion time VUInts.
2628        //
2629        // This is exactly the same pattern as regular row_size: after reading row_size,
2630        // skip row_size bytes to reach the next row/marker.
2631        let (remaining, marker_body_size) = parse_vuint(&data[pos..]).map_err(|e| {
2632            Error::corruption(format!(
2633                "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse marker_body_size at offset {}: {:?}",
2634                pos, e
2635            ))
2636        })?;
2637        let body_size_vint_len = data[pos..].len() - remaining.len();
2638        pos += body_size_vint_len;
2639
2640        // Skip marker_body_size bytes (prev_size + deletion time(s))
2641        let body_end = pos + marker_body_size as usize;
2642        if body_end > data.len() {
2643            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
2644                "V5CompressedLegacy: marker_body_size={} at pos={} exceeds data length {}",
2645                marker_body_size,
2646                pos,
2647                data.len()
2648            )));
2649        }
2650        pos = body_end;
2651
2652        log::debug!(
2653            "V5CompressedLegacy: Skipped range tombstone marker, advanced from {} to {}",
2654            offset,
2655            pos
2656        );
2657
2658        Ok(pos)
2659    }
2660
2661    /// Parse row metadata AFTER flags and clustering prefix (Issue #213 fix)
2662    ///
2663    /// # Corrected Format (from Cassandra UnfilteredSerializer.java)
2664    /// ```text
2665    /// [row_flags: u8]           ← Parsed by parse_row_flags()
2666    /// [extended_flags: u8]      ← Parsed by parse_row_flags()
2667    /// [clustering_prefix]       ← Parsed by parse_clustering_prefix()
2668    /// [row_size: VInt]          ← This function starts here
2669    /// [prev_size: VInt]
2670    /// [timestamp: VInt if 0x04 set] ← Delta from min_timestamp
2671    /// [ttl: VInt if 0x08 set] ← Delta from min_ttl
2672    /// [deletion: 2 VInts if 0x10 set]
2673    /// [column_bitmap: VUInt bitmask of missing columns if NOT 0x20]
2674    /// ```
2675    ///
2676    /// Returns RowHeader with decoded metadata, calculated header_size, and row_size.
2677    fn parse_row_metadata(
2678        &self,
2679        data: &[u8],
2680        offset: usize,
2681        row_flags: u8,
2682        _extended_flags: Option<u8>,
2683    ) -> Result<(RowHeader, u64)> {
2684        let mut pos = offset;
2685
2686        // V5CompressedLegacy format: row_size and prev_size come AFTER clustering
2687        // (which has already been parsed before this function is called)
2688
2689        // Read row size (VInt) - CRITICAL for partition boundary detection!
2690        debug!(
2691            "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsing row_size VInt at pos={}, hex={:02x?}",
2692            pos,
2693            &data[pos..std::cmp::min(pos + 5, data.len())]
2694        );
2695        let (remaining, row_size) = parse_vuint(&data[pos..]).map_err(|e| {
2696            Error::corruption(format!(
2697                "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse row size at offset {}: {:?}",
2698                pos, e
2699            ))
2700        })?;
2701        let row_size_vint_len = data[pos..].len() - remaining.len();
2702        debug!(
2703            "V5CompressedLegacy: row_size={}, consumed {} bytes, pos before={}, pos after={}",
2704            row_size,
2705            row_size_vint_len,
2706            pos,
2707            pos + row_size_vint_len
2708        );
2709        pos += row_size_vint_len;
2710
2711        // Read prev size (VInt)
2712        debug!(
2713            "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsing prev_size VInt at pos={}, hex={:02x?}",
2714            pos,
2715            &data[pos..std::cmp::min(pos + 5, data.len())]
2716        );
2717        let (remaining, _prev_size) = parse_vuint(&data[pos..]).map_err(|e| {
2718            Error::corruption(format!(
2719                "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse prev size at offset {}: {:?}",
2720                pos, e
2721            ))
2722        })?;
2723        let bytes_consumed = data[pos..].len() - remaining.len();
2724        debug!(
2725            "V5CompressedLegacy: prev_size={}, consumed {} bytes, pos before={}, pos after={}",
2726            _prev_size,
2727            bytes_consumed,
2728            pos,
2729            pos + bytes_consumed
2730        );
2731        pos += bytes_consumed;
2732
2733        // Read timestamp if HAS_TIMESTAMP flag is set.
2734        //
2735        // Fix #629 (C2): Cassandra writes an UNSIGNED VInt delta here
2736        // (SerializationHeader.java:165: out.writeUnsignedVInt(timestamp - stats.minTimestamp)).
2737        // The old code used parse_vint (ZigZag), causing ~50% undercount of timestamp deltas.
2738        let timestamp = if (row_flags & ROW_HAS_TIMESTAMP) != 0 {
2739            let (remaining, delta) = parse_vuint(&data[pos..]).map_err(|e| {
2740                Error::corruption(format!(
2741                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse timestamp delta at offset {}: {:?}",
2742                    pos, e
2743                ))
2744            })?;
2745            let bytes_consumed = data[pos..].len() - remaining.len();
2746            pos += bytes_consumed;
2747
2748            // Apply delta decoding: absolute_timestamp = min_timestamp + delta
2749            let absolute_timestamp = self.min_timestamp.wrapping_add(delta as i64);
2750            debug!(
2751                "V5CompressedLegacy: Row timestamp: delta={}, min={}, absolute={}",
2752                delta, self.min_timestamp, absolute_timestamp
2753            );
2754            Some(absolute_timestamp)
2755        } else {
2756            None
2757        };
2758
2759        // Read TTL and liveness local expiration time if HAS_TTL flag is set.
2760        //
2761        // Fix #630 (C3): Cassandra writes TWO VInt32 fields when HAS_TTL is set
2762        // (UnfilteredSerializer.java:225-228):
2763        //   1. pk_liveness.ttl()               → header.writeTTL(ttl, out)        [VInt32]
2764        //   2. pk_liveness.localExpirationTime()→ header.writeLocalDeletionTime(ldt, out) [VInt32]
2765        // The old code read only ONE VInt (TTL), leaving the LDT byte(s) unread and
2766        // misaligning all subsequent fields in HAS_TTL rows.
2767        let (ttl, ttl_liveness_ldt) = if (row_flags & ROW_HAS_TTL) != 0 {
2768            let (remaining, ttl_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[pos..]).map_err(|e| {
2769                Error::corruption(format!(
2770                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse TTL delta at offset {}: {:?}",
2771                    pos, e
2772                ))
2773            })?;
2774            let bytes_consumed = data[pos..].len() - remaining.len();
2775            pos += bytes_consumed;
2776
2777            // Apply delta decoding: absolute_ttl = min_ttl + delta
2778            let absolute_ttl = if let Some(min_ttl) = self.min_ttl {
2779                min_ttl.wrapping_add(ttl_delta as i64) as i32
2780            } else {
2781                ttl_delta as i32
2782            };
2783
2784            // Read liveness local expiration time (second mandatory field after TTL).
2785            let (remaining, ldt_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[pos..]).map_err(|e| {
2786                Error::corruption(format!(
2787                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse liveness LDT delta at offset {}: {:?}",
2788                    pos, e
2789                ))
2790            })?;
2791            let ldt_bytes_consumed = data[pos..].len() - remaining.len();
2792            pos += ldt_bytes_consumed;
2793
2794            let absolute_ldt = self.min_local_deletion_time.wrapping_add(ldt_delta as i64) as i32;
2795
2796            debug!(
2797                "V5CompressedLegacy: Row TTL: ttl_delta={}, min={:?}, ttl={}, ldt_delta={}, ldt={}",
2798                ttl_delta, self.min_ttl, absolute_ttl, ldt_delta, absolute_ldt
2799            );
2800            (Some(absolute_ttl), Some(absolute_ldt))
2801        } else {
2802            (None, None)
2803        };
2804
2805        // Read deletion if HAS_DELETION flag is set.
2806        //
2807        // Cassandra canonical DeletionTime.Serializer order (matches the CQLite writer,
2808        // data_writer.rs write_*_row HAS_DELETION block and write_complex_deletion):
2809        //   1. markedForDeleteAt: UNSIGNED VInt delta, base min_timestamp, MICROSECONDS
2810        //      -> the authoritative reconciliation timestamp (LWW shadowing).
2811        //   2. localDeletionTime: UNSIGNED VInt delta, base min_local_deletion_time, SECONDS
2812        //      -> the GC-grace clock, NOT a reconciliation timestamp.
2813        //
2814        // Fix #629 (C2): Both deltas are UNSIGNED per Cassandra SerializationHeader.java.
2815        // The old code used parse_vint (ZigZag) for markedForDeleteAt, causing ~50% undercount.
2816        //
2817        // (The complex-cell deletion reader, parse_complex_column, already uses this
2818        // markedForDeleteAt-first order; this aligns the row-level header with it.)
2819        let (marked_for_delete_at, local_deletion_time) = if (row_flags & ROW_HAS_DELETION) != 0 {
2820            // First VInt: markedForDeleteAt delta (unsigned).
2821            let (remaining, mfda_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[pos..]).map_err(|e| {
2822                Error::corruption(format!(
2823                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse markedForDeleteAt delta at offset {}: {:?}",
2824                    pos, e
2825                ))
2826            })?;
2827            let bytes_consumed = data[pos..].len() - remaining.len();
2828            pos += bytes_consumed;
2829
2830            // Second VInt: localDeletionTime delta (unsigned VInt32).
2831            //
2832            // For both nb and oa the on-disk format is the same: an unsigned VInt32
2833            // encoding `(int)(localDeletionTime - stats.minLocalDeletionTime)`.
2834            // See: SerializationHeader.java — `writeLocalDeletionTime` /
2835            //      `readLocalDeletionTime` (same for all BIG versions).
2836            //
2837            // VG3 gate: hasUIntDeletionTime (BigFormat.java:409, oa+)
2838            // The interpretation of the *result* differs:
2839            //   nb: `min_local_deletion_time + delta` cast to i32 (values capped at ~year 2038)
2840            //   oa: `min_local_deletion_time + delta` treated as u32 to support ~year 2106
2841            //
2842            // When the sum overflows an i32 (> 2^31-1 seconds) the value is negative
2843            // in a signed context; with hasUIntDeletionTime we reinterpret it as an
2844            // unsigned u32 (CassandraUInt.toLong, CassandraUInt.java).  For current
2845            // test fixtures all deletion times are well within i32 range so both
2846            // interpretations produce identical bit patterns; the gate is a no-op
2847            // in practice but is wired correctly for future large TTL values.
2848            let (remaining, ldt_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[pos..]).map_err(|e| {
2849                Error::corruption(format!(
2850                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse localDeletionTime delta at offset {}: {:?}",
2851                    pos, e
2852                ))
2853            })?;
2854            let bytes_consumed = data[pos..].len() - remaining.len();
2855            pos += bytes_consumed;
2856
2857            // markedForDeleteAt: absolute = min_timestamp + delta (microseconds).
2858            let absolute_marked_for_delete_at = self.min_timestamp.wrapping_add(mfda_delta as i64);
2859            // localDeletionTime: absolute = min_local_deletion_time + delta (seconds).
2860            //
2861            // VG3 gate: hasUIntDeletionTime (BigFormat.java:409, oa/da)
2862            //   nb: store as i32 (may overflow for dates > ~year 2038)
2863            //   oa: reinterpret the 32-bit bit-pattern as unsigned (supports ~year 2106)
2864            //
2865            // Source: SerializationHeader.java readLocalDeletionTime + UnfilteredSerializer.java:671-676
2866            // "if (complexDeletion.localDeletionTime() < 0) {
2867            //    complexDeletion = DeletionTime.build(..., Cell.deletionTimeUnsignedIntegerToLong((int) ...));
2868            //  }" — this reinterpretation fires when hasUIntDeletionTime && bit31 set.
2869            let has_uint_ldt = match self.version_gates.as_ref() {
2870                crate::storage::sstable::version_gate::VersionGates::Big(g) => {
2871                    g.has_uint_deletion_time
2872                }
2873                crate::storage::sstable::version_gate::VersionGates::Bti(g) => {
2874                    g.has_uint_deletion_time
2875                }
2876            };
2877            let raw_ldt = self.min_local_deletion_time.wrapping_add(ldt_delta as i64);
2878            let absolute_local_deletion_time = if has_uint_ldt {
2879                // Reinterpret the low 32 bits as an unsigned integer (year-2106-safe).
2880                // CassandraUInt.toLong(int) = Integer.toUnsignedLong(int), so negative
2881                // i32 values get promoted to the [2^31, 2^32) long range.
2882                (raw_ldt as u32) as i32
2883            } else {
2884                raw_ldt as i32
2885            };
2886            debug!(
2887                "V5CompressedLegacy: Row deletion: markedForDeleteAt(delta={}, min_ts={}, abs={} us), localDeletionTime(delta={}, min_ldt={}, abs={} s)",
2888                mfda_delta,
2889                self.min_timestamp,
2890                absolute_marked_for_delete_at,
2891                ldt_delta,
2892                self.min_local_deletion_time,
2893                absolute_local_deletion_time
2894            );
2895            (
2896                Some(absolute_marked_for_delete_at),
2897                Some(absolute_local_deletion_time),
2898            )
2899        } else {
2900            (None, None)
2901        };
2902
2903        // Parse column bitmap if HAS_ALL_COLUMNS is NOT set
2904        let missing_columns_bitmap = if (row_flags & ROW_HAS_ALL_COLUMNS) == 0 {
2905            // Cassandra Columns.Serializer.serializeSubset() format:
2906            // Single unsigned VInt encoding a bitmask of MISSING columns
2907            // (bit=1 means column is missing, bit=0 means present)
2908            let (remaining, bitmap) = parse_vuint(&data[pos..]).map_err(|e| {
2909                Error::corruption(format!(
2910                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse column bitmap at offset {}: {:?}",
2911                    offset + pos,
2912                    e
2913                ))
2914            })?;
2915            let bytes_consumed = data[pos..].len() - remaining.len();
2916            pos += bytes_consumed;
2917
2918            debug!(
2919                "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsed column bitmap: missing_bitmap=0x{:X} ({} bytes)",
2920                bitmap, bytes_consumed
2921            );
2922            Some(bitmap)
2923        } else {
2924            None
2925        };
2926
2927        let header_size = pos - offset;
2928        debug!(
2929            "V5CompressedLegacy: Row header parsing complete: offset_start={}, pos_end={}, header_size={} bytes, row_size={} bytes (total row including cells), timestamp={:?}, ttl={:?}, deletion={:?}",
2930            offset, pos, header_size, row_size, timestamp, ttl, local_deletion_time
2931        );
2932
2933        // Note: ttl_liveness_ldt (from HAS_TTL) is the pk_liveness local expiration time.
2934        // It is distinct from local_deletion_time (from HAS_DELETION, row tombstone GC clock).
2935        // We store it in RowHeader so the delta-scan path can populate CellMeta.expires_at
2936        // for TTL-bearing INSERT rows (Issue #702).  is_row_tombstone() still checks
2937        // local_deletion_time (HAS_DELETION only), so TTL rows are NOT misclassified.
2938
2939        Ok((
2940            RowHeader {
2941                timestamp,
2942                ttl,
2943                liveness_expires_at_seconds: ttl_liveness_ldt,
2944                local_deletion_time,
2945                marked_for_delete_at,
2946                header_size,
2947                row_size_vint_len,
2948                missing_columns_bitmap,
2949            },
2950            row_size,
2951        ))
2952    }
2953
2954    /// Parse partition header (flags, key, deletion time)
2955    ///
2956    /// # Format
2957    /// ```text
2958    /// [flags: u8][key_len: u8][key_bytes: [u8; key_len]][del_time: i32][unknown: 8 bytes]
2959    /// ```
2960    ///
2961    /// # Visibility
2962    /// Exposed for integration testing to validate partition header parsing
2963    #[doc(hidden)]
2964    pub fn parse_partition_header(&self, data: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Result<(RowKey, usize)> {
2965        let (row_key, next_offset, _deletion_time) =
2966            self.parse_partition_header_full(data, offset)?;
2967        Ok((row_key, next_offset))
2968    }
2969
2970    /// Like [`parse_partition_header`] but also returns the partition-level deletion
2971    /// timestamp (`markedForDeleteAt` in µs since epoch), if the partition is deleted.
2972    ///
2973    /// Returns `(RowKey, next_offset, Option<markedForDeleteAt_micros>)`.
2974    ///
2975    /// `None` means the partition is live (no partition tombstone).
2976    /// `Some(ts)` means the partition carries a tombstone; `ts` is the authoritative
2977    /// reconciliation timestamp in microseconds since the Unix epoch.
2978    ///
2979    /// Authority: DeletionTime.java (getSerializer / legacySerializer / Serializer),
2980    /// BigFormat.java:409 (`hasUIntDeletionTime`).
2981    pub fn parse_partition_header_full(
2982        &self,
2983        data: &[u8],
2984        mut offset: usize,
2985    ) -> Result<(RowKey, usize, Option<i64>)> {
2986        let start_offset = offset;
2987
2988        if offset >= data.len() {
2989            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
2990                "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition header offset {} out of bounds (data len: {})",
2991                offset,
2992                data.len()
2993            )));
2994        }
2995
2996        // Byte 0: Flags (ignore for now - may indicate static rows, deletions, etc.)
2997        let _flags = data[offset];
2998        offset += 1;
2999
3000        // Byte 1: Partition key length (u8, NOT VInt)
3001        if offset >= data.len() {
3002            return Err(Error::corruption(
3003                "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end at partition key length",
3004            ));
3005        }
3006        let key_len = data[offset] as usize;
3007        offset += 1;
3008
3009        // Issue #258 FIX: Partition key length must be non-zero
3010        // A key_len of 0 indicates this is NOT a valid partition header (likely row data).
3011        // This validation is critical for peek_is_partition_header() to correctly
3012        // distinguish partition headers from row data in the row loop.
3013        if key_len == 0 {
3014            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
3015                "V5CompressedLegacy: Invalid partition key length 0 at offset {} (not a partition header)",
3016                start_offset
3017            )));
3018        }
3019
3020        debug!(
3021            "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition key length = {} bytes",
3022            key_len
3023        );
3024
3025        // Next key_len bytes: Partition key data (raw bytes, no component structure)
3026        if offset + key_len > data.len() {
3027            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
3028                "V5CompressedLegacy: Partition key extends beyond data (offset: {}, key_len: {}, data_len: {})",
3029                offset, key_len, data.len()
3030            )));
3031        }
3032        let key_bytes = data[offset..offset + key_len].to_vec();
3033        offset += key_len;
3034
3035        // Partition-level DeletionTime deserialization.
3036        //
3037        // VG3 gate: hasUIntDeletionTime (BigFormat.java:409, oa+)
3038        //
3039        // oa format uses a compact DeletionTime.Serializer
3040        // (DeletionTime.java, Serializer inner class):
3041        //   LIVE:    1 byte = 0x80 (IS_LIVE_DELETION = 0b10000000)
3042        //   DELETED: 8 bytes markedForDeleteAt (long) +
3043        //            4 bytes localDeletionTimeUnsignedInteger (int) = 12 bytes total
3044        //
3045        // nb format uses DeletionTime.legacySerializer:
3046        //   Always:  4 bytes localDeletionTime (int) +
3047        //            8 bytes markedForDeleteAt (long) = 12 bytes total
3048        //
3049        // Authority: DeletionTime.java:191-219 (getSerializer / Serializer.serialize)
3050        let partition_deletion: Option<i64>;
3051        if self.has_uint_deletion_time() {
3052            // oa / da format
3053            if offset >= data.len() {
3054                return Err(Error::corruption(
3055                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end at oa partition deletion time byte",
3056                ));
3057            }
3058            let del_flags = data[offset];
3059            const IS_LIVE_DELETION: u8 = 0x80; // DeletionTime.java:208
3060            if (del_flags & IS_LIVE_DELETION) != 0 {
3061                // LIVE partition: exactly 1 byte — no tombstone.
3062                if del_flags != IS_LIVE_DELETION {
3063                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
3064                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Invalid IS_LIVE_DELETION byte 0x{:02x} at offset {} \
3065                         (only 0x80 is valid for oa-format LIVE partitions, per DeletionTime.java:227-229)",
3066                        del_flags, offset
3067                    )));
3068                }
3069                offset += 1;
3070                partition_deletion = None;
3071            } else {
3072                // DELETED partition (oa): 8 bytes markedForDeleteAt (big-endian i64)
3073                //                       + 4 bytes localDeletionTime (big-endian u32)
3074                if offset + 12 > data.len() {
3075                    return Err(Error::corruption(
3076                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end at oa partition deletion time (deleted)",
3077                    ));
3078                }
3079                let mfda = i64::from_be_bytes(
3080                    data[offset..offset + 8]
3081                        .try_into()
3082                        .map_err(|_| Error::corruption("V5CompressedLegacy: oa mfda slice"))?,
3083                );
3084                offset += 12; // markedForDeleteAt(8) + localDeletionTime(4)
3085                partition_deletion = Some(mfda);
3086            }
3087        } else {
3088            // nb format: 4 bytes localDeletionTime (big-endian i32)
3089            //          + 8 bytes markedForDeleteAt (big-endian i64)
3090            if offset + 12 > data.len() {
3091                return Err(Error::corruption(
3092                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end at nb partition deletion time",
3093                ));
3094            }
3095            // localDeletionTime is the first 4 bytes.
3096            let local_deletion_time = i32::from_be_bytes(
3097                data[offset..offset + 4]
3098                    .try_into()
3099                    .map_err(|_| Error::corruption("V5CompressedLegacy: nb ldt slice"))?,
3100            );
3101            offset += 4;
3102            // markedForDeleteAt is next 8 bytes (big-endian i64).
3103            let mfda = i64::from_be_bytes(
3104                data[offset..offset + 8]
3105                    .try_into()
3106                    .map_err(|_| Error::corruption("V5CompressedLegacy: nb mfda slice"))?,
3107            );
3108            offset += 8;
3109            // A live (not deleted) partition in nb format has
3110            // localDeletionTime = 0x7fffffff (i32::MAX, DeletionTime.LIVE sentinel).
3111            // Any other value indicates a real partition tombstone.
3112            const NB_LIVE_LOCAL_DELETION_TIME: i32 = i32::MAX;
3113            if local_deletion_time == NB_LIVE_LOCAL_DELETION_TIME {
3114                partition_deletion = None;
3115            } else {
3116                partition_deletion = Some(mfda);
3117            }
3118        }
3119
3120        // Create RowKey from partition key bytes
3121        let row_key = RowKey(key_bytes);
3122
3123        debug!(
3124            "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsed partition header at offset {}, consumed {} bytes, \
3125             partition_deletion={:?}",
3126            start_offset,
3127            offset - start_offset,
3128            partition_deletion
3129        );
3130
3131        Ok((row_key, offset, partition_deletion))
3132    }
3133
3134    /// Parse a range tombstone marker in full, returning the decoded bound values,
3135    /// inclusivity flags, and deletion timestamp(s).
3136    ///
