3137    /// This is the delta-scan counterpart to `skip_range_tombstone_marker`: instead
3138    /// of discarding the clustering values and deletion time, it decodes and returns
3139    /// them so the caller can emit `DeltaRecord::RangeDelete`.
3140    ///
3141    /// ## Return value
3142    ///
3143    /// `Ok((bound_values, bound_kind, deleted_at_primary, deleted_at_secondary, next_offset))`
3144    ///
3145    /// - `bound_values`: clustering-key prefix values for this bound (may be shorter
3146    ///   than the full clustering arity — a prefix bound).
3147    /// - `bound_kind`: the raw Cassandra `ClusteringPrefix.Kind` ordinal (0/1/2/5/6/7).
3148    /// - `deleted_at_primary`: `markedForDeleteAt` in µs for this bound's tombstone.
3149    /// - `deleted_at_secondary`: present only for boundary markers (kind 2 or 5) and
3150    ///   carries the deletion time for the *other* side of the boundary.
3151    /// - `next_offset`: position after this marker in `data`.
3152    ///
3153    /// ## Bound kind ordinals
3154    ///
3155    /// | ordinal | name | meaning |
3156    /// |---------|------|---------|
3157    /// | 0 | `EXCL_END_BOUND` | end of range, exclusive (`< ck`) |
3158    /// | 1 | `INCL_START_BOUND` | start of range, inclusive (`>= ck`) |
3159    /// | 2 | `EXCL_END_INCL_START_BOUNDARY` | boundary: end of prev range (exclusive) + start of new range (inclusive) |
3160    /// | 5 | `INCL_END_EXCL_START_BOUNDARY` | boundary: end of prev range (inclusive) + start of new range (exclusive) |
3161    /// | 6 | `INCL_END_BOUND` | end of range, inclusive (`<= ck`) |
3162    /// | 7 | `EXCL_START_BOUND` | start of range, exclusive (`> ck`) |
3163    ///
3164    /// Boundary markers (kind 2 or 5) carry **two** deletion times; simple markers (all others)
3165    /// carry **one** deletion time and `deleted_at_secondary` is `None`.
3166    ///
3167    /// Authority: UnfilteredSerializer.java:282-303, ClusteringBoundOrBoundary.java
3168    #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
3169    pub fn parse_range_tombstone_marker_full(
3170        &self,
3171        data: &[u8],
3172        offset: usize,
3173        schema: &TableSchema,
3174    ) -> Result<(Vec<Value>, u8, i64, Option<i64>, usize)> {
3175        // Delegate to the LDT-carrying parser and drop the localDeletionTime
3176        // fields the delta-scan caller does not need — the on-disk marker grammar
3177        // is decoded in exactly one place (issue #933 cleanup).
3178        let (bound_values, bound_kind, (mfda_primary, _ldt_primary), secondary, next_offset) =
3179            self.parse_range_tombstone_marker_with_ldt(data, offset, schema)?;
3180        Ok((
3181            bound_values,
3182            bound_kind,
3183            mfda_primary,
3184            secondary.map(|(mfda, _ldt)| mfda),
3185            next_offset,
3186        ))
3187    }
3188
3189    /// Return a schema view truncated to `n` clustering keys.
3190    ///
3191    /// Range-tombstone bound markers may be **prefix bounds**: the Cassandra serializer
3192    /// writes only `cluster_count` clustering values when a DELETE specifies fewer
3193    /// clustering components than the full key arity (e.g. `DELETE WHERE pk=? AND ck1=?`
3194    /// on a table with `(ck1, ck2)` only pins the first component).
3195    ///
3196    /// Returns `None` (callers use the original schema) when `n >= schema.clustering_keys.len()`,
3197    /// avoiding a clone in the common non-prefix case.  Returns `Some(truncated)` when a
3198    /// shorter view is needed.
3199    fn clustering_prefix_schema(schema: &TableSchema, n: usize) -> Option<TableSchema> {
3200        if n >= schema.clustering_keys.len() {
3201            None
3202        } else {
3203            Some(TableSchema {
3204                keyspace: schema.keyspace.clone(),
3205                table: schema.table.clone(),
3206                partition_keys: schema.partition_keys.clone(),
3207                clustering_keys: schema.clustering_keys[..n].to_vec(),
3208                columns: schema.columns.clone(),
3209                comments: schema.comments.clone(),
3210                dropped_columns: schema.dropped_columns.clone(),
3211            })
3212        }
3213    }
3214
3215    /// Decode one `(markedForDeleteAt, localDeletionTime)` pair, returning BOTH
3216    /// absolute values (issue #933 compaction range-tombstone surfacing).
3217    ///
3218    /// Decodes the `(markedForDeleteAt delta, localDeletionTime delta)` VInt pair
3219    /// and returns BOTH absolute values — the absolute
3220    /// `localDeletionTime` (GC-grace clock, seconds) so the compaction merger can
3221    /// retain/purge a surviving range marker by gc_grace AND the writer can
3222    /// re-emit the marker's LDT verbatim. The LDT is decoded with the same
3223    /// `hasUIntDeletionTime` reinterpretation as the row-level deletion reader
3224    /// (`min_local_deletion_time + delta`, then `as u32 as i32` for far-future
3225    /// values) so a year-2106 LDT round-trips bit-for-bit (#853/#889).
3226    ///
3227    /// Advances `*pos` past both fields.
3228    fn parse_deletion_time_pair_with_ldt(
3229        &self,
3230        data: &[u8],
3231        pos: &mut usize,
3232    ) -> Result<(i64, i32)> {
3233        // markedForDeleteAt delta (unsigned VInt, µs since epoch delta).
3234        let (remaining, mfda_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[*pos..]).map_err(|e| {
3235            Error::corruption(format!(
3236                "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse markedForDeleteAt in marker body at {}: {:?}",
3237                *pos, e
3238            ))
3239        })?;
3240        *pos += data[*pos..].len() - remaining.len();
3241        let absolute_mfda = self.min_timestamp.wrapping_add(mfda_delta as i64);
3242
3243        // localDeletionTime delta (unsigned VInt, seconds delta).
3244        let (remaining2, ldt_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[*pos..]).map_err(|e| {
3245            Error::corruption(format!(
3246                "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse localDeletionTime in marker body at {}: {:?}",
3247                *pos, e
3248            ))
3249        })?;
3250        *pos += data[*pos..].len() - remaining2.len();
3251
3252        let has_uint_ldt = match self.version_gates.as_ref() {
3253            crate::storage::sstable::version_gate::VersionGates::Big(g) => g.has_uint_deletion_time,
3254            crate::storage::sstable::version_gate::VersionGates::Bti(g) => g.has_uint_deletion_time,
3255        };
3256        let raw_ldt = self.min_local_deletion_time.wrapping_add(ldt_delta as i64);
3257        let absolute_ldt = if has_uint_ldt {
3258            (raw_ldt as u32) as i32
3259        } else {
3260            raw_ldt as i32
3261        };
3262
3263        Ok((absolute_mfda, absolute_ldt))
3264    }
3265
3266    /// Parse a range-tombstone bound marker in full, returning the decoded bound
3267    /// values, kind, AND the primary/secondary `(markedForDeleteAt, localDeletionTime)`
3268    /// pairs (issue #933).
3269    ///
3270    /// This is the compaction counterpart of [`Self::parse_range_tombstone_marker_full`]:
3271    /// it additionally surfaces the `localDeletionTime` of each deletion so the
3272    /// compaction path can re-emit / gc_grace-purge the marker faithfully.
3273    ///
3274    /// Returns `(bound_values, bound_kind, (mfda_primary, ldt_primary),
3275    /// Option<(mfda_secondary, ldt_secondary)>, next_offset)`.
3276    #[allow(clippy::type_complexity)]
3277    fn parse_range_tombstone_marker_with_ldt(
3278        &self,
3279        data: &[u8],
3280        offset: usize,
3281        schema: &TableSchema,
3282    ) -> Result<(Vec<Value>, u8, (i64, i32), Option<(i64, i32)>, usize)> {
3283        let mut pos = offset;
3284
3285        if pos >= data.len() {
3286            return Err(Error::corruption(
3287                "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end at range tombstone marker (compaction)",
3288            ));
3289        }
3290
3291        let marker_flags = data[pos];
3292        pos += 1;
3293
3294        if (marker_flags & ROW_HAS_EXTENDED_FLAGS) != 0 {
3295            if pos >= data.len() {
3296                return Err(Error::corruption(
3297                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end reading marker extended flags (compaction)",
3298                ));
3299            }
3300            pos += 1;
3301        }
3302
3303        // Bound kind byte.
3304        if pos >= data.len() {
3305            return Err(Error::corruption(
3306                "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end reading range tombstone bound kind (compaction)",
3307            ));
3308        }
3309        let bound_kind = data[pos];
3310        pos += 1;
3311
3312        // Cluster count (u16 big-endian).
3313        if pos + 2 > data.len() {
3314            return Err(Error::corruption(
3315                "V5CompressedLegacy: Unexpected end reading range tombstone cluster count (compaction)",
3316            ));
3317        }
3318        let cluster_count = u16::from_be_bytes([data[pos], data[pos + 1]]) as usize;
3319        pos += 2;
3320
3321        // Clustering values (may be a PREFIX shorter than the full arity).
3322        let bound_values = if cluster_count > 0 {
3323            let prefix_schema_owned = Self::clustering_prefix_schema(schema, cluster_count);
3324            let effective_schema = prefix_schema_owned.as_ref().unwrap_or(schema);
3325            let (values, new_pos) = self.parse_clustering_prefix(data, pos, effective_schema)?;
3326            pos = new_pos;
3327            values
3328        } else {
3329            Vec::new()
3330        };
3331
3332        // marker_body_size VUInt — size of (prev_size VUInt + deletion_time(s)).
3333        let (remaining, marker_body_size) = parse_vuint(&data[pos..]).map_err(|e| {
3334            Error::corruption(format!(
3335                "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse marker_body_size (compaction) at offset {}: {:?}",
3336                pos, e
3337            ))
3338        })?;
3339        pos += data[pos..].len() - remaining.len();
3340
3341        let body_end = pos + marker_body_size as usize;
3342        if body_end > data.len() {
3343            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
3344                "V5CompressedLegacy: marker_body_size={} at pos={} exceeds data length {} (compaction)",
3345                marker_body_size,
3346                pos,
3347                data.len()
3348            )));
3349        }
3350
3351        // prev_unfiltered_size VUInt — skip.
3352        let (remaining2, _prev_size) = parse_vuint(&data[pos..]).map_err(|e| {
3353            Error::corruption(format!(
3354                "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse prev_size in marker body (compaction) at {}: {:?}",
3355                pos, e
3356            ))
3357        })?;
3358        pos += data[pos..].len() - remaining2.len();
3359
3360        let primary = self.parse_deletion_time_pair_with_ldt(data, &mut pos)?;
3361        let secondary = if bound_kind == 2 || bound_kind == 5 {
3362            Some(self.parse_deletion_time_pair_with_ldt(data, &mut pos)?)
3363        } else {
3364            None
3365        };
3366
3367        pos = body_end;
3368
3369        Ok((bound_values, bound_kind, primary, secondary, pos))
3370    }
3371
3372    /// Parse clustering prefix section (between row header and cells)
3373    ///
3374    /// The clustering prefix encodes clustering key values using a compact VInt header
3375    /// with 2 bits per clustering column to indicate value state.
3376    ///
3377    /// # Format
3378    /// ```text
3379    /// [prefix_header: VInt] ← 2 bits per clustering column
3380    ///   - 00 = null
3381    ///   - 01 = empty
3382    ///   - 10/11 = has value
3383    /// [value_1: bytes if present]
3384    /// [value_2: bytes if present]
3385    /// [... more values ...]
3386    /// ```
3387    ///
3388    /// Returns: (clustering_values, new_offset)
3389    fn parse_clustering_prefix(
3390        &self,
3391        data: &[u8],
3392        mut offset: usize,
3393        schema: &TableSchema,
3394    ) -> Result<(Vec<Value>, usize)> {
3395        // If no clustering keys, skip this section
3396        if schema.clustering_keys.is_empty() {
3397            log::debug!(
3398                "V5CompressedLegacy: No clustering keys in schema, skipping clustering prefix"
3399            );
3400            return Ok((Vec::new(), offset));
3401        }
3402
3403        log::debug!(
3404            "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsing clustering prefix at offset {} for {} clustering keys",
3405            offset,
3406            schema.clustering_keys.len()
3407        );
3408
3409        // Read header VInt (2 bits per clustering column)
3410        let (remaining, header_vint) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
3411            Error::corruption(format!(
3412                "V5CompressedLegacy: Failed to parse clustering prefix header VInt at offset {}: {:?}",
3413                offset, e
3414            ))
3415        })?;
3416        let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
3417        offset += bytes_consumed;
3418
3419        log::debug!(
3420            "V5CompressedLegacy: Clustering prefix header = 0x{:x}, consumed {} bytes",
3421            header_vint,
3422            bytes_consumed
3423        );
3424
3425        // Decode each clustering value based on 2-bit state
3426        let mut clustering_values = Vec::new();
3427        for (i, col) in schema.clustering_keys.iter().enumerate() {
3428            let state = (header_vint >> (i * 2)) & 0x03;
3429            log::debug!(
3430                "V5CompressedLegacy: Clustering key {} '{}' state = {} (from bits {}..{})",
3431                i,
3432                col.name,
3433                state,
3434                i * 2,
3435                i * 2 + 1
3436            );
3437
3438            // Issue #229 FIX: Correct state interpretation per Cassandra's ClusteringPrefix.Kind
3439            //
3440            // Per Cassandra 5.0 UnfilteredSerializer.java and ClusteringPrefix.Kind:
3441            // - 0 (PRESENT): Value is present, type-specific bytes follow
3442            // - 1 (EMPTY): Empty value (zero-length, no bytes follow)
3443            // - 2 (NULL): NULL value (no bytes follow)
3444            // - 3: Reserved
3445            //
3446            // Previous code had 0=NULL, 2/3=PRESENT which was inverted!
3447            match state {
3448                0 => {
3449                    // PRESENT - parse value based on type
3450                    let (value, new_off) = self.parse_clustering_value(data, offset, col)?;
3451                    log::debug!(
3452                        "V5CompressedLegacy:   -> PRESENT: {:?} (consumed {} bytes)",
3453                        value,
3454                        new_off - offset
3455                    );
3456                    clustering_values.push(value);
3457                    offset = new_off;
3458                }
3459                1 => {
3460                    // EMPTY - zero-length value
3461                    //
3462                    // Per Cassandra's ClusteringPrefix, EMPTY means zero-length byte array.
3463                    // For variable-width types, this is valid. For fixed-width types (int,
3464                    // bigint, UUID), EMPTY should not normally occur.
3465                    let col_type = col.data_type.to_lowercase();
3466                    let empty_value = match col_type.as_str() {
3467                        "text" | "varchar" | "ascii" => Value::Text(String::new()),
3468                        "blob" => Value::Blob(vec![]),
3469                        _ => {
3470                            // Fixed-width types shouldn't have EMPTY state in normal data
3471                            log::warn!(
3472                                "V5CompressedLegacy: EMPTY state for clustering key '{}' (type {}), treating as NULL",
3473                                col.name, col.data_type
3474                            );
3475                            Value::Null
3476                        }
3477                    };
3478                    clustering_values.push(empty_value);
3479                    log::debug!("V5CompressedLegacy:   -> EMPTY");
3480                }
3481                2 => {
3482                    // NULL
3483                    clustering_values.push(Value::Null);
3484                    log::debug!("V5CompressedLegacy:   -> NULL");
3485                }
3486                3 => {
3487                    // Reserved - treat as NULL for safety
3488                    log::warn!("V5CompressedLegacy: Clustering key {} has reserved state 3, treating as NULL", col.name);
3489                    clustering_values.push(Value::Null);
3490                }
3491                _ => unreachable!(),
3492            }
3493        }
3494
3495        log::debug!(
3496            "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsed {} clustering values, new offset = {}",
3497            clustering_values.len(),
3498            offset
3499        );
3500
3501        Ok((clustering_values, offset))
3502    }
3503
3504    /// Parse individual clustering value (type-specific)
3505    ///
3506    /// Clustering values are encoded based on their CQL type. This handles the most
3507    /// common clustering key types: timestamp, text, int, uuid.
3508    ///
3509    /// Returns: (value, new_offset)
3510    fn parse_clustering_value(
3511        &self,
3512        data: &[u8],
3513        offset: usize,
3514        col: &crate::schema::ClusteringColumn,
3515    ) -> Result<(Value, usize)> {
3516        let normalized = col.data_type.to_lowercase();
3517        log::debug!(
3518            "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsing clustering value '{}' type '{}' at offset {}",
3519            col.name,
3520            normalized,
3521            offset
3522        );
3523
3524        match normalized.as_str() {
3525            "timestamp" | "reversedtype(timestamptype)" => {
3526                // Fixed 8-byte timestamp (big-endian i64)
3527                if offset + 8 > data.len() {
3528                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
3529                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Clustering '{}': need 8 bytes for timestamp, only {} available",
3530                        col.name,
3531                        data.len() - offset
3532                    )));
3533                }
3534                let ts = i64::from_be_bytes([
3535                    data[offset],
3536                    data[offset + 1],
3537                    data[offset + 2],
3538                    data[offset + 3],
3539                    data[offset + 4],
3540                    data[offset + 5],
3541                    data[offset + 6],
3542                    data[offset + 7],
3543                ]);
3544                Ok((Value::Timestamp(ts), offset + 8))
3545            }
3546
3547            "text" | "utf8type" | "varchar" => {
3548                // VInt length + UTF-8 bytes
3549                let (remaining, len) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
3550                    Error::corruption(format!(
3551                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Clustering '{}': failed to parse text length: {:?}",
3552                        col.name, e
3553                    ))
3554                })?;
3555                let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
3556                let len_offset = offset + bytes_consumed;
3557
3558                if len_offset + len as usize > data.len() {
3559                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
3560                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Clustering '{}': need {} bytes for text, only {} available",
3561                        col.name,
3562                        len,
3563                        data.len() - len_offset
3564                    )));
3565                }
3566
3567                let text = String::from_utf8(data[len_offset..len_offset + len as usize].to_vec())
3568                    .map_err(|e| {
3569                        Error::corruption(format!(
3570                            "V5CompressedLegacy: Clustering '{}': invalid UTF-8: {:?}",
3571                            col.name, e
3572                        ))
3573                    })?;
3574                Ok((Value::Text(text), len_offset + len as usize))
3575            }
3576
3577            "int" => {
3578                // Issue #258 fix: Fixed 4-byte int (big-endian i32) - NO length prefix
3579                // Per Cassandra format, fixed-width clustering types have no VInt length prefix
3580                if offset + 4 > data.len() {
3581                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
3582                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Clustering '{}': need 4 bytes for int, only {} available",
3583                        col.name,
3584                        data.len() - offset
3585                    )));
3586                }
3587
3588                let val = i32::from_be_bytes([
3589                    data[offset],
3590                    data[offset + 1],
3591                    data[offset + 2],
3592                    data[offset + 3],
3593                ]);
3594                Ok((Value::Integer(val), offset + 4))
3595            }
3596
3597            "uuid" | "timeuuid" => {
3598                // Issue #258 fix: Fixed 16-byte UUID - NO length prefix
3599                // Per Cassandra format, fixed-width clustering types have no VInt length prefix
3600                if offset + 16 > data.len() {
3601                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
3602                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Clustering '{}': need 16 bytes for UUID, only {} available",
3603                        col.name,
3604                        data.len() - offset
3605                    )));
3606                }
3607
3608                let uuid_bytes: [u8; 16] = data[offset..offset + 16]
3609                    .try_into()
3610                    .map_err(|_| Error::corruption("UUID byte conversion failed"))?;
3611
3612                Ok((Value::Uuid(uuid_bytes), offset + 16))
3613            }
3614
3615            "bigint" | "counter" => {
3616                // Issue #258 fix: Fixed 8-byte bigint (big-endian i64) - NO length prefix
3617                // Per Cassandra format, fixed-width clustering types have no VInt length prefix
3618                if offset + 8 > data.len() {
3619                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
3620                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Clustering '{}': need 8 bytes for bigint, only {} available",
3621                        col.name,
3622                        data.len() - offset
3623                    )));
3624                }
3625
3626                let val = i64::from_be_bytes([
3627                    data[offset],
3628                    data[offset + 1],
3629                    data[offset + 2],
3630                    data[offset + 3],
3631                    data[offset + 4],
3632                    data[offset + 5],
3633                    data[offset + 6],
3634                    data[offset + 7],
3635                ]);
3636                Ok((Value::BigInt(val), offset + 8))
3637            }
3638
3639            _ => {
3640                // For other types, read VInt length + skip that many bytes
3641                // Return as blob for now
3642                warn!(
3643                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Clustering '{}' has unsupported type '{}', treating as blob",
3644                    col.name, col.data_type
3645                );
3646                let (remaining, len) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
3647                    Error::corruption(format!(
3648                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Clustering '{}': failed to parse blob length: {:?}",
3649                        col.name, e
3650                    ))
3651                })?;
3652                let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
3653                let len_offset = offset + bytes_consumed;
3654
3655                if len_offset + len as usize > data.len() {
3656                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
3657                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Clustering '{}': need {} bytes, only {} available",
3658                        col.name,
3659                        len,
3660                        data.len() - len_offset
3661                    )));
3662                }
3663
3664                Ok((
3665                    Value::Blob(data[len_offset..len_offset + len as usize].to_vec()),
3666                    len_offset + len as usize,
3667                ))
3668            }
3669        }
3670    }
3671
3672    /// Parse row data (header + cells) and return cells with new offset
3673    ///
3674    /// V5CompressedLegacy format stores cells WITHOUT column names in schema column order.
3675    /// Schema is REQUIRED to determine which column each value belongs to.
3676    ///
3677    /// Returns: `ParsedRow` = `(cells, row_header, new_offset, is_static)` where
3678    /// `is_static` is `true` when the row's `EXTENDED_IS_STATIC` flag was set.
3679    /// Static rows must be merged into clustering rows by the caller, not emitted directly.
3680    fn parse_row_data_with_offset(
3681        &self,
3682        data: &[u8],
3683        offset: usize,
3684        schema: Option<&TableSchema>,
3685        reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
3686        want_cell_metadata: bool,
3687    ) -> Result<ParsedRow> {
3688        self.parse_row_data_with_offset_impl(data, offset, schema, reader, want_cell_metadata, None)
3689    }
3690
3691    /// Implementation of [`Self::parse_row_data_with_offset`] with an optional
3692    /// per-column complex-element collector for the compaction read path
3693    /// (epic #899). When `compaction_complex_out` is `Some`, every complex
3694    /// column's per-element cells + complex deletion are captured into it
3695    /// alongside the normal collapsed-`Value` cells. On user-facing reads it is
3696    /// `None` and behavior is byte-unchanged.
3697    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
3698    fn parse_row_data_with_offset_impl(
3699        &self,
3700        data: &[u8],
3701        mut offset: usize,
3702        schema: Option<&TableSchema>,
3703        reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
3704        want_cell_metadata: bool,
3705        mut compaction_complex_out: Option<&mut CompactionComplexColumns>,
3706    ) -> Result<ParsedRow> {
3707        let mut cells = HashMap::new();
3708        // Parallel per-cell write metadata map (populated alongside `cells`).
3709        // Only allocated when the caller actually needs WRITETIME/TTL metadata
3710        // (i.e. `want_cell_metadata == true`).  On the normal read path this stays
3711        // `None` so that zero HashMap allocations or inserts occur per cell.
3712        let mut cell_meta: Option<HashMap<String, CellWriteMetadata>> = if want_cell_metadata {
3713            Some(HashMap::new())
3714        } else {
3715            None
3716        };
3717
3718        // DS4 (Issue #700): Per-column complex collection metadata.  Only allocated when
3719        // want_cell_metadata is true (same gate as cell_meta to avoid hot-path overhead).
3720        let mut complex_col_meta: Option<HashMap<String, ComplexColumnMeta>> = if want_cell_metadata
3721        {
3722            Some(HashMap::new())
3723        } else {
3724            None
3725        };
3726
3727        let schema = schema.ok_or_else(|| {
3728            Error::schema(format!(
3729                "V5CompressedLegacy: Schema required for {}.{} (cells stored without column names)",
3730                self.keyspace, self.table_name
3731            ))
3732        })?;
3733
3734        debug!(
3735            "V5CompressedLegacy: Starting row data parse at offset {} with {} schema columns",
3736            offset,
3737            schema.columns.len()
3738        );
3739
3740        // ISSUE #213 FIX: Correct parsing order for V5CompressedLegacy format
3741        //
3742        // The CORRECT format from Cassandra UnfilteredSerializer.java is:
3743        //   1. [row_flags: u8]
3744        //   2. [extended_flags: u8 if 0x80 set]
3745        //   3. [clustering_prefix: variable]  ← BEFORE row_size!
3746        //   4. [row_size: VInt]
3747        //   5. [prev_size: VInt]
3748        //   6. [row_body: timestamp, ttl, deletion, bitmap, cells]
3749        //
3750        // The previous code parsed row_size BEFORE clustering, which caused
3751        // clustering key bytes to be misinterpreted as row_size (often 0).
3752
3753        // Step 1: Parse row flags (1-2 bytes)
3754        let (row_flags, extended_flags, flags_size) = self.parse_row_flags(data, offset)?;
3755        offset += flags_size;
3756
3757        // Issue #258 fix: Check if this is a static row (no clustering prefix)
3758        // Per Cassandra UnfilteredSerializer.java lines 114-122, 190-191:
3759        // Static rows have the IS_STATIC bit (0x01) set in extended flags and
3760        // do NOT have a clustering prefix - skip directly to row_size.
3761        let is_static = extended_flags
3762            .map(|ef| (ef & EXTENDED_IS_STATIC) != 0)
3763            .unwrap_or(false);
3764
3765        // Step 2: Parse clustering prefix BEFORE row_size (Issue #213 fix)
3766        // This is the critical change - clustering comes AFTER flags but BEFORE row_size
3767        // EXCEPT for static rows which have no clustering prefix at all.
3768        let (clustering_values, offset) = if !is_static {
3769            self.parse_clustering_prefix(data, offset, schema)?
3770        } else {
3771            log::debug!(
3772                "V5CompressedLegacy: Static row detected (extended_flags=0x{:02x}), skipping clustering prefix",
3773                extended_flags.unwrap_or(0)
3774            );
3775            (vec![], offset)
3776        };
3777
3778        log::debug!(
3779            "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsed {} clustering values after flags, now at offset {} (is_static={})",
3780            clustering_values.len(),
3781            offset,
3782            is_static
3783        );
3784
3785        // Issue #229 FIX: Add clustering key values to cells HashMap
3786        //
3787        // Cassandra stores clustering keys separately from regular columns, but they
3788        // must be included in the result for proper query output. Without this fix,
3789        // tables with clustering keys show fallback column names because the clustering
3790        // values weren't being added to the cells HashMap.
3791        for (i, ck) in schema.clustering_keys.iter().enumerate() {
3792            if i < clustering_values.len() {
3793                cells.insert(ck.name.clone(), clustering_values[i].clone());
3794            }
3795        }
3796
3797        // Step 3: Parse row metadata (row_size, prev_size, timestamps, etc.)
3798        //
3799        // CRITICAL (Issue #237): Save offset where row_size VInt STARTS.
3800        // The row_size value is measured from AFTER this VInt is consumed.
3801        // Formula: next_offset = (row_metadata_offset + row_size_vint_len) + row_size
3802        // This offset is right after the clustering prefix (which was already parsed).
3803        let row_metadata_offset = offset;
3804        let (row_header, row_size) =
3805            self.parse_row_metadata(data, offset, row_flags, extended_flags)?;
3806
3807        // CRITICAL VALIDATION: row_size must be reasonable
3808        //
3809        // In V5CompressedLegacy format, row_size should never exceed the block size (typically 16KB).
3810        // If row_size is unreasonably large, it indicates either:
3811        // 1. Partition tombstone or deletion marker (no actual row data)
3812        // 2. Format parsing error (landed at wrong offset)
3813        // 3. Corrupted data
3814        //
3815        // In all cases, we should skip this partition rather than panic.
3816        const MAX_REASONABLE_ROW_SIZE: u64 = 1_000_000; // 1MB max (very generous)
3817        if row_size > MAX_REASONABLE_ROW_SIZE {
3818            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
3819                "V5CompressedLegacy: Unreasonably large row_size={} at offset {} (max: {}). Likely partition tombstone or format error.",
3820                row_size,
3821                offset,
3822                MAX_REASONABLE_ROW_SIZE
3823            )));
3824        }
3825
3826        // Row payloads can span multiple compressed chunks in V5CompressedLegacy format.
3827        // The reader has already stitched all chunks together (see get_all_entries()),
3828        // so row_size is valid across chunk boundaries. We MUST NOT validate against
3829        // individual chunk sizes as rows naturally span chunks in Cassandra's format.
3830        // This is NOT corruption - it's the intended file layout.
3831
3832        log::debug!(
3833            "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsed row metadata at offset {}: header_size={} bytes, row_size={} bytes, timestamp={:?}, ttl={:?}, deletion={:?}",
3834            offset, row_header.header_size, row_size, row_header.timestamp, row_header.ttl, row_header.local_deletion_time
3835        );
3836
3837        // Row tombstone detection (Issue #191, Phase 2) + coexistence (Issue #932).
3838        //
3839        // A row with ROW_HAS_DELETION (0x10) carries a row-level deletion. HISTORICALLY
3840        // such a row had NO cells, so the parser skipped cell parsing entirely. But a
3841        // row deletion can COEXIST with surviving cells (cells written strictly after
3842        // the deletion — issue #932): the writer emits HAS_DELETION + HAS_TIMESTAMP +
3843        // the surviving cells. We must therefore skip cell parsing ONLY when there are
3844        // no cell bytes after the row header; otherwise fall through to the normal cell
3845        // loop so the surviving cells are read (the row header still carries the
3846        // deletion via `local_deletion_time` / `marked_for_delete_at`).
3847        //
3848        // Calculate offset after row data (based on row_size from header).
3849        //
3850        // CRITICAL FIX (Issue #237): row_size is measured from AFTER the row_size VInt,
3851        // not from where it starts. This matches Cassandra's getFilePointer() semantics:
3852        //   next_position = row_size_value + position_after_reading_row_size_vint
3853        let after_row_offset =
3854            (row_metadata_offset + row_header.row_size_vint_len) + row_size as usize;
3855        // Cell data (if any) begins right after the row header. When that start
3856        // reaches the row boundary there are no cells — a pure row tombstone.
3857        let cell_data_start = row_metadata_offset + row_header.header_size;
3858        let has_cell_bytes = cell_data_start < after_row_offset;
3859
3860        if row_header.local_deletion_time.is_some() && !has_cell_bytes {
3861            log::debug!(
3862                "V5CompressedLegacy: Pure row tombstone (deletion_time={:?}), skipping cell parsing",
3863                row_header.local_deletion_time
3864            );
3865
3866            // Validate we have enough data
3867            if after_row_offset > data.len() {
3868                let remaining = data
3869                    .len()
3870                    .saturating_sub(row_metadata_offset + row_header.row_size_vint_len);
3871                return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
3872                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Not enough bytes for row data at offset {} (need {}, have {})",
3873                    row_metadata_offset + row_header.row_size_vint_len,
3874                    row_size,
3875                    remaining
3876                )));
3877            }
3878
3879            let next_offset = after_row_offset;
3880            log::debug!(
3881                "V5CompressedLegacy: Skipped tombstoned row, next offset = {}",
3882                next_offset
3883            );
3884
3885            // Return empty cells for tombstoned row (no cell metadata, no complex meta)
3886            return Ok((
3887                cells,
3888                cell_meta,
3889                Some(row_header),
3890                next_offset,
3891                is_static,
3892                None,
3893            ));
3894        }
3895
3896        // Advance offset past row metadata to start of cell data
3897        let mut offset = offset + row_header.header_size;
3898
3899        log::debug!(
3900            "V5CompressedLegacy: Cell data starts at offset {}, first 32 bytes: {}",
3901            offset,
3902            hex::encode(&data[offset..std::cmp::min(offset + 32, data.len())])
3903        );
3904
3905        // Cell flags validation: First byte should be valid cell flags (0x00-0x1F) for simple cells
3906        // Common flags: 0x00 (basic cell), 0x08 (USE_ROW_TIMESTAMP), 0x04 (HAS_EMPTY_VALUE)
3907        // Deleted cells have 0x01 (IS_DELETED), expiring cells have 0x02 (IS_EXPIRING)
3908        //
3909        // NOTE: For complex columns (non-frozen collections), the first byte is a VInt for the
3910        // cell count, which may have values > 0x1F. This is normal and not an error.
3911        // The validation below is only accurate for tables with all simple cells.
3912        if offset < data.len() {
3913            let first_byte = data[offset];
3914            if first_byte <= 0x1F {
3915                debug!(
3916                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Valid cell flags 0x{:02x} at offset {} after row header",
3917                    first_byte, offset
3918                );
3919            } else {
3920                debug!(
3921                    "V5CompressedLegacy: First byte 0x{:02x} at offset {} (> 0x1F) - may be VInt for complex column cell count",
3922                    first_byte, offset
3923                );
3924            }
3925        }
3926
3927        // CRITICAL: V5CompressedLegacy format stores cells WITHOUT column names
3928        // or column IDs in the binary data. Cells appear in SCHEMA DEFINITION ORDER
3929        // (the order columns were defined in CREATE TABLE), NOT alphabetical order.
3930        //
3931        // NULL/missing columns are handled by:
3932        // - Checking for cell marker (0x08) before attempting to parse
3933        // - If no marker found or parse fails, column is NULL (not present)
3934        // - Continue to next column in schema order
3935        //
3936        // This implementation uses schema definition order directly, which is the
3937        // correct approach per Cassandra 5.0 SerializationHeader semantics.
3938
3939        // CRITICAL FIX (Issue #164): Filter out partition keys and clustering keys!
3940        // The schema.columns list contains ALL columns (including keys), but cells
3941        // are only stored for REGULAR columns. Partition/clustering keys are part
3942        // of the row key and do NOT have cell data.
3943        let partition_key_names: std::collections::HashSet<_> = schema
3944            .partition_keys
3945            .iter()
3946            .map(|k| k.name.as_str())
3947            .collect();
3948        let clustering_key_names: std::collections::HashSet<_> = schema
3949            .clustering_keys
3950            .iter()
3951            .map(|k| k.name.as_str())
3952            .collect();
3953
3954        // CRITICAL FIX (Issue #191): Use serialization header column order, not schema order
3955        // Cassandra 5.0 V5CompressedLegacy stores cells in the order defined by Statistics.db
3956        // serialization header (alphabetical by ColumnIdentifier/comparator), NOT CQL schema order.
3957        // We must iterate reader.header.columns directly to align binary layout with logical columns.
3958        //
3959        // Issue #702 FIX: For tables with BOTH static and regular columns, Cassandra's
3960        // missing_columns_bitmap is relative to the column group of the current row kind:
3961        //   - Static rows:  bitmap covers only static columns
3962        //   - Regular rows: bitmap covers only regular columns
3963        // Including the wrong group shifts all bitmap indices, causing columns to be
3964        // silently absent or misread.  Filter columns_in_order to the matching kind.
3965        let columns_in_order: Vec<_> = if !reader.header.columns.is_empty() {
3966            // Build lookup map from schema for column details
3967            let schema_map: HashMap<String, &crate::schema::Column> = schema
3968                .columns
3969                .iter()
3970                .map(|col| (col.name.clone(), col))
3971                .collect();
3972
3973            // Iterate serialization header columns in exact order (skipping keys,
3974            // and filtering to match the current row's static/regular kind).
3975            reader
3976                .header
3977                .columns
3978                .iter()
3979                .filter(|col_info| {
3980                    !col_info.is_primary_key
3981                        && !col_info.is_clustering
3982                        && col_info.is_static == is_static
3983                })
3984                .filter_map(|col_info| schema_map.get(&col_info.name).copied())
3985                .collect()
3986        } else {
3987            // Fallback to schema order when header is empty (shouldn't happen for real SSTables)
3988            log::warn!("V5CompressedLegacy: reader.header.columns is empty, falling back to schema order (may cause column misalignment)");
3989            schema
3990                .columns
3991                .iter()
3992                .filter(|col| {
3993                    !partition_key_names.contains(col.name.as_str())
3994                        && !clustering_key_names.contains(col.name.as_str())
3995                        && col.is_static == is_static // Issue #702: match row kind
3996                })
3997                .collect()
3998        };
3999
4000        // Filter columns by missing_columns_bitmap when present.
4001        // The bitmap indicates which columns are MISSING (bit=1 → absent).
4002        // We only parse cells for columns that are actually present in the data.
4003        let columns_to_parse: Vec<&crate::schema::Column> = match row_header.missing_columns_bitmap
4004        {
4005            Some(bitmap) => {
4006                let filtered: Vec<_> = columns_in_order
4007                    .iter()
4008                    .enumerate()
4009                    .filter(|(idx, _)| {
4010                        // Bitmap only covers the first 64 columns (u64).
4011                        // Columns beyond index 63 are not represented in the
4012                        // bitmap and are treated as present.
4013                        *idx >= 64 || (bitmap & (1u64 << idx)) == 0
4014                    })
4015                    .map(|(_, col)| *col)
4016                    .collect();
4017                log::debug!(
4018                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Column bitmap 0x{:X} filters {} → {} columns",
4019                    bitmap,
4020                    columns_in_order.len(),
4021                    filtered.len()
4022                );
4023                filtered
4024            }
4025            None => columns_in_order,
4026        };
4027
4028        log::debug!("V5CompressedLegacy: Parsing {} cells in SERIALIZATION HEADER ORDER starting at offset {} (row header was {} bytes)", columns_to_parse.len(), offset, row_header.header_size);
4029        log::debug!(
4030            "V5CompressedLegacy: Column order: {:?}",
4031            columns_to_parse.iter().map(|c| &c.name).collect::<Vec<_>>()
4032        );
4033        log::debug!(
4034            "V5CompressedLegacy: Cell data hex (first 64 bytes): {}",
4035            hex::encode(&data[offset..std::cmp::min(offset + 64, data.len())])
4036        );
4037
4038        // Issue #221: Check if row has complex deletion info for non-frozen collections
4039        let has_complex_deletion = (row_flags & ROW_HAS_COMPLEX_DELETION) != 0;
4040        if has_complex_deletion {
4041            log::debug!("V5CompressedLegacy: Row has HAS_COMPLEX_DELETION flag (0x40) set");
4042        }
4043
4044        for (col_idx, &column) in columns_to_parse.iter().enumerate() {
4045            if offset >= data.len() {
4046                log::debug!(
4047                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Reached end of data at column {} ('{}'), parsed {}/{} cells",
4048                    col_idx,
4049                    column.name,
4050                    cells.len(),
4051                    columns_to_parse.len()
4052                );
4053                break;
4054            }
4055
4056            // Issue #221: Branch based on column type - complex columns need special parsing
4057            // Issue #693: simple columns return 4-tuple including cell timestamp / expiration;
4058            //             complex columns return 2-tuple and inherit the row-level timestamp.
4059            if Self::is_complex_column(&column.data_type) {
4060                log::debug!(
4061                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Column '{}' is complex (non-frozen collection), using parse_complex_column",
4062                    column.name
4063                );
4064                // Epic #899: on the compaction read path collect per-element
4065                // cells + the real complex deletion into `compaction_complex_out`
4066                // (otherwise this is the user-facing read path: collapsed value
4067                // only, byte-unchanged). Elements inherit the row liveness
4068                // timestamp when they carry USE_ROW_TIMESTAMP.
4069                let parse_result = if compaction_complex_out.is_some() {
4070                    let row_ts = row_header.timestamp.unwrap_or(0);
4071                    let mut element_buf = Vec::new();
4072                    self.parse_complex_column_inner(
4073                        data,
4074                        offset,
4075                        column,
4076                        has_complex_deletion,
4077                        row_ts,
4078                        Some(&mut element_buf),
4079                    )
4080                    .map(|(value, new_offset, col_meta)| {
4081                        if let Some(ref mut out) = compaction_complex_out {
4082                            // Capture the whole-collection collapsed value for the
4083                            // byte-neutral Phase A output path (roborev #863).
4084                            out.insert(
4085                                column.name.clone(),
4086                                (col_meta.complex_deletion, element_buf, value.clone()),
4087                            );
4088                        }
4089                        (value, new_offset, col_meta)
4090                    })
4091                } else {
4092                    self.parse_complex_column(data, offset, column, has_complex_deletion, reader)
4093                };
4094                match parse_result {
4095                    Ok((value, new_offset, col_meta)) => {
4096                        log::debug!(
4097                            "V5CompressedLegacy:   ✓ Complex column {} '{}' = {:?}, consumed {} bytes",
4098                            col_idx, column.name, value, new_offset - offset
4099                        );
4100                        // Normal read-path (WRITETIME/TTL queries): use the row-level liveness
4101                        // timestamp unchanged.  Cassandra's WRITETIME(non_frozen_collection) on
4102                        // the standard read path returns the row timestamp, not per-element max.
4103                        // The delta-scan path computes its own max-element-writetime from
4104                        // ComplexColumnMeta (stored separately below) and never reads this field
4105                        // for collection columns.  Do NOT mutate this with max_element_writetime
4106                        // here — that would silently change WRITETIME(col) on the ordinary path
4107                        // (roborev Finding 1).
4108                        if let Some(ref mut meta_map) = cell_meta {
4109                            let row_ts = row_header.timestamp.unwrap_or(0);
4110                            meta_map.insert(
4111                                column.name.clone(),
4112                                CellWriteMetadata {
4113                                    write_timestamp_micros: row_ts,
4114                                    expiration: None,
4115                                },
4116                            );
4117                        }
4118                        // DS4 (Issue #700): Store ComplexColumnMeta for delta-scan callers.
4119                        if let Some(ref mut ccm_map) = complex_col_meta {
4120                            ccm_map.insert(column.name.clone(), col_meta);
4121                        }
4122                        cells.insert(column.name.clone(), value);
4123                        offset = new_offset;
4124                    }
4125                    Err(e) => {
4126                        log::debug!(
4127                            "V5CompressedLegacy:   ✗ Complex column {} '{}' at offset {} FAILED: {}",
4128                            col_idx, column.name, offset, e
4129                        );
4130                        break;
4131                    }
4132                }
4133            } else {
4134                match self.parse_cell_value_schema_order(data, offset, column, reader) {
4135                    Ok((value, cell_own_ts, cell_exp, new_offset)) => {
4136                        log::debug!(
4137                            "V5CompressedLegacy:   ✓ Column {} '{}' ({}) = {:?}, consumed {} bytes",
4138                            col_idx,
4139                            column.name,
4140                            column.data_type,
4141                            value,
4142                            new_offset - offset
4143                        );
4144                        // Only compute and store per-cell metadata when the caller requested it.
4145                        // On the normal read hot-path (want_cell_metadata == false), cell_meta is
4146                        // None and this entire block is skipped — zero allocations per cell.
4147                        if let Some(ref mut meta_map) = cell_meta {
4148                            // Resolve effective write timestamp:
4149                            // use cell's own timestamp when present, else row-level liveness timestamp.
4150                            let effective_ts =
4151                                cell_own_ts.unwrap_or_else(|| row_header.timestamp.unwrap_or(0));
4152                            // Resolve expiration: cell-level wins; fall back to row-level TTL when
4153                            // the cell used USE_ROW_TTL (cell_exp is None in that case).
4154                            // USE_ROW_TTL path: row_header.ttl is the row-level TTL in seconds.
4155                            // row_header.local_deletion_time is the corresponding expires_at (seconds).
4156                            let row_level_exp =
4157                                match (row_header.ttl, row_header.local_deletion_time) {
4158                                    (Some(ttl_s), Some(ldt_s)) => Some(CellExpiration {
4159                                        ttl_seconds: ttl_s,
4160                                        expires_at_seconds: ldt_s as i64,
4161                                    }),
4162                                    _ => None,
4163                                };
4164                            let effective_exp = cell_exp.or(row_level_exp);
4165                            meta_map.insert(
4166                                column.name.clone(),
4167                                CellWriteMetadata {
4168                                    write_timestamp_micros: effective_ts,
4169                                    expiration: effective_exp,
4170                                },
4171                            );
4172                        }
4173                        cells.insert(column.name.clone(), value);
4174                        offset = new_offset;
4175                    }
4176                    Err(e) => {
4177                        log::debug!(
4178                            "V5CompressedLegacy:   ✗ Column {} '{}' ({}) at offset {} FAILED: {}",
4179                            col_idx,
4180                            column.name,
4181                            column.data_type,
4182                            offset,
4183                            e
4184                        );
4185                        // CRITICAL FIX: Stop parsing remaining columns when we hit an error
4186                        // The offset doesn't advance here, but we exit the loop cleanly
4187                        // rather than continuing with invalid offset
4188                        break;
4189                    }
4190                }
4191            }
4192        }
4193
4194        log::debug!(
4195            "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsed {}/{} columns (missing columns are NULL)",
4196            cells.len(),
4197            columns_to_parse.len()
4198        );
4199        log::debug!(
4200            "V5CompressedLegacy: Cells HashMap keys: {:?}",
4201            cells.keys().collect::<Vec<_>>()
4202        );
4203
4204        debug!("V5CompressedLegacy: Parsed total of {} cells", cells.len());
4205
4206        // Calculate offset after cell data (based on row_size from header)
4207        //
4208        // CRITICAL (Issue #237): row_size is measured from AFTER the row_size VInt,
4209        // not from where it starts. This matches Cassandra's getFilePointer() semantics:
4210        //   next_position = row_size_value + position_after_reading_row_size_vint
4211        //
4212        // Formula: (row_metadata_offset + row_size_vint_len) + row_size
4213        //
4214        // There is NO trailing field in V5CompressedLegacy format - the next partition/row
4215        // starts immediately after row_size bytes from this position.
4216        let row_size_counted_from = row_metadata_offset + row_header.row_size_vint_len;
4217        let after_cells_offset = row_size_counted_from + row_size as usize;
4218
4219        // Validate we have enough data
4220        if after_cells_offset > data.len() {
4221            let remaining = data.len().saturating_sub(row_size_counted_from);
4222            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4223                "V5CompressedLegacy: Not enough bytes for row data at offset {} (need {}, have {})",
4224                row_size_counted_from, row_size, remaining
4225            )));
4226        }
4227
4228        // No trailing field - next partition/row starts immediately
4229        let next_offset = after_cells_offset;
4230
4231        debug!(
4232            "V5CompressedLegacy: Row complete - row_size={} bytes, next offset = {} (counted from {}, is_static={})",
4233            row_size, next_offset, row_size_counted_from, is_static
4234        );
4235
4236        Ok((
4237            cells,
4238            cell_meta,
4239            Some(row_header),
4240            next_offset,
4241            is_static,
4242            complex_col_meta,
4243        ))
4244    }
4245
4246    /// Parse a single cell value WITHOUT column name (schema-order format)
4247    ///
4248    /// Cell format in V5CompressedLegacy follows Cassandra 5.0 cell serialization:
4249    /// - First byte: Cell flags (bitset, valid range: 0x00-0x1F)
4250    ///   - 0x01 = IS_DELETED_MASK (tombstone)
4251    ///   - 0x02 = IS_EXPIRING_MASK (has TTL)
4252    ///   - 0x04 = HAS_EMPTY_VALUE_MASK (no value bytes)
4253    ///   - 0x08 = USE_ROW_TIMESTAMP_MASK (use row timestamp)
4254    ///   - 0x10 = USE_ROW_TTL_MASK (use row TTL)
4255    /// - Conditional timestamp/TTL/deletion fields (based on flags)
4256    /// - Value data (if HAS_EMPTY_VALUE not set)
4257    ///
4258    /// See CASSANDRA_5_CELL_DESERIALIZATION_FORMAT.md for complete specification.
4259    ///
4260    /// Returns: `(value, cell_own_timestamp, expiration, new_offset)` where:
4261    /// - `cell_own_timestamp`: the cell's own decoded timestamp in µs, or `None`
4262    ///   when the cell inherits the row-level timestamp (`USE_ROW_TIMESTAMP` flag).
4263    /// - `expiration`: TTL / localDeletionTime pair when the cell is expiring, or
4264    ///   `None` when the cell has no TTL.
4265    fn parse_cell_value_schema_order(
4266        &self,
4267        data: &[u8],
4268        mut offset: usize,
4269        column: &crate::schema::Column,
4270        _reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
4271    ) -> Result<(Value, Option<i64>, Option<CellExpiration>, usize)> {
4272        // Cell flag constants (from Cassandra 5.0 Cell.Serializer)
4273        const CELL_IS_DELETED: u8 = 0x01;
4274        const CELL_IS_EXPIRING: u8 = 0x02;
4275        const CELL_HAS_EMPTY_VALUE: u8 = 0x04;
4276        const CELL_USE_ROW_TIMESTAMP: u8 = 0x08;
4277        const CELL_USE_ROW_TTL: u8 = 0x10;
4278
4279        // Read cell flags byte
4280        if offset >= data.len() {
4281            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4282                "Cell '{}': unexpected end at flags byte",
4283                column.name
4284            )));
4285        }
4286        let flags = data[offset];
4287
4288        // CRITICAL FIX (Issue #191): Validate flags are in valid range (0x00-0x1F)
4289        // Bits 0x20, 0x40, 0x80 are row-level flags and should NEVER appear in cell flags.
4290        // If we see these bits, the offset is misaligned (reading row data at cell position).
4291        if flags > 0x1F {
4292            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4293                "Cell '{}': invalid cell flags 0x{:02x} at offset {} (bits 0x20/0x40/0x80 indicate offset misalignment)",
4294                column.name, flags, offset
4295            )));
4296        }
4297
4298        offset += 1;
4299
4300        // Decode flags
4301        let is_deleted = (flags & CELL_IS_DELETED) != 0;
4302        let is_expiring = (flags & CELL_IS_EXPIRING) != 0;
4303        let has_empty_value = (flags & CELL_HAS_EMPTY_VALUE) != 0;
4304        let use_row_timestamp = (flags & CELL_USE_ROW_TIMESTAMP) != 0;
4305        let use_row_ttl = (flags & CELL_USE_ROW_TTL) != 0;
4306
4307        log::debug!(
4308            "V5CompressedLegacy: Cell '{}' flags=0x{:02x} (deleted={}, expiring={}, empty={}, use_row_ts={}, use_row_ttl={})",
4309            column.name, flags, is_deleted, is_expiring, has_empty_value, use_row_timestamp, use_row_ttl
4310        );
4311
4312        // === PHASE 2: Parse conditional fields between flags and value ===
4313        // Based on Cassandra 5.0 Cell.Serializer format specification
4314
4315        // Step 1: Read timestamp (if not using row timestamp)
4316        // Issue #505: capture the actual cell timestamp so deleted cells can carry it
4317        // in a Value::Tombstone.
4318        //
4319        // Fix #629 (C2): Cell timestamp delta is UNSIGNED VInt per Cassandra
4320        // SerializationHeader.java:165: out.writeUnsignedVInt(timestamp - stats.minTimestamp).
4321        let mut cell_timestamp: Option<i64> = None;
4322        if !use_row_timestamp {
4323            let (remaining, timestamp_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
4324                Error::corruption(format!(
4325                    "Cell '{}': failed to parse timestamp delta as VUInt at offset {}: {:?}",
4326                    column.name, offset, e
4327                ))
4328            })?;
4329            let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
4330            offset += bytes_consumed;
4331            let absolute_ts = self.min_timestamp.wrapping_add(timestamp_delta as i64);
4332            log::debug!(
4333                "V5CompressedLegacy: Cell '{}' timestamp_delta={} (min_timestamp={}) absolute={}",
4334                column.name,
4335                timestamp_delta,
4336                self.min_timestamp,
4337                absolute_ts,
4338            );
4339            cell_timestamp = Some(absolute_ts);
4340        }
4341
4342        // Step 2: Read localDeletionTime (if deleted or expiring, and not using row TTL)
4343        // Captured as absolute epoch-seconds for CellExpiration.expires_at_seconds.
4344        let mut cell_local_deletion_time: Option<i64> = None;
4345        if !use_row_ttl && (is_deleted || is_expiring) {
4346            let (remaining, deletion_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
4347                Error::corruption(format!(
4348                    "Cell '{}': failed to parse localDeletionTime delta as VUInt at offset {}: {:?}",
4349                    column.name, offset, e
4350                ))
4351            })?;
4352            let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
4353            offset += bytes_consumed;
4354            let abs_ldt = self
4355                .min_local_deletion_time
4356                .wrapping_add(deletion_delta as i64);
4357            log::debug!(
4358                "V5CompressedLegacy: Cell '{}' deletion_delta={} (min_local_deletion_time={}) abs_ldt={}",
4359                column.name,
4360                deletion_delta,
4361                self.min_local_deletion_time,
4362                abs_ldt
4363            );
4364            cell_local_deletion_time = Some(abs_ldt);
4365        }
4366
4367        // Step 3: Read TTL (if expiring and not using row TTL)
4368        // Captured as absolute TTL seconds for CellExpiration.ttl_seconds.
4369        let mut cell_ttl_seconds: Option<i32> = None;
4370        if !use_row_ttl && is_expiring {
4371            let (remaining, ttl_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
4372                Error::corruption(format!(
4373                    "Cell '{}': failed to parse TTL delta as VUInt at offset {}: {:?}",
4374                    column.name, offset, e
4375                ))
4376            })?;
4377            let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
4378            offset += bytes_consumed;
4379            // Absolute TTL = min_ttl + delta (seconds).  Clamp to i32 range for the
4380            // CellExpiration.ttl_seconds field (Cassandra caps TTL at ~630M seconds).
4381            let abs_ttl = self.min_ttl.unwrap_or(0).wrapping_add(ttl_delta as i64);
4382            log::debug!(
4383                "V5CompressedLegacy: Cell '{}' ttl_delta={} (min_ttl={:?}) abs_ttl={}",
4384                column.name,
4385                ttl_delta,
4386                self.min_ttl,
4387                abs_ttl
4388            );
4389            cell_ttl_seconds = Some(abs_ttl.min(i32::MAX as i64) as i32);
4390        }
4391
4392        // Build per-cell expiration metadata (used when the flag is set).
4393        // Available at both return sites below — the tombstone path also uses
4394        // cell_timestamp so we compute expiration here before the tombstone check.
4395        let cell_expiration: Option<CellExpiration> =
4396            match (is_expiring, cell_local_deletion_time, cell_ttl_seconds) {
4397                (true, Some(expires_at), Some(ttl_secs)) => Some(CellExpiration {
4398                    ttl_seconds: ttl_secs,
4399                    expires_at_seconds: expires_at,
4400                }),
4401                // use_row_ttl path: expiration info comes from the row header (caller handles it).
4402                _ => None,
4403            };
4404
4405        // Step 4: Cell path for complex columns (multi-cell collections/UDTs)
4406        // For now, skip this - we'll add in a future iteration when we handle complex columns.
4407        // Simple columns (int, text, boolean, uuid, etc.) don't have cell paths.
4408
4409        // === End of Phase 2 conditional field parsing ===
4410
4411        // CRITICAL: Inverted logic for HAS_EMPTY_VALUE_MASK
4412        // Flag NOT set (0x04 absent) = cell HAS value → read value bytes
4413        // Flag SET (0x04 present) = cell has NO value → return empty/null immediately
4414        let has_value = !has_empty_value;
4415
4416        // Handle deleted cells (tombstones)
4417        // According to Cassandra 5.0 Cell.Serializer, deleted cells:
4418        // 1. Have IS_DELETED flag set
4419        // 2. May have deletion metadata (timestamp, localDeletionTime)
4420        // 3. Do NOT have value data (even if HAS_EMPTY_VALUE not set)
4421        //
4422        // Issue #505: emit Value::Tombstone(CellTombstone) so that the compaction
4423        // merger can apply cell-level shadowing semantics.  The actual deletion
4424        // timestamp is carried in the tombstone for timestamp-based LWW ordering.
4425        if is_deleted {
4426            let deletion_time = cell_timestamp.unwrap_or(0);
4427            log::debug!(
4428                "V5CompressedLegacy: Cell '{}' is tombstone (deleted), returning Tombstone(deletion_time={})",
4429                column.name, deletion_time
4430            );
4431            return Ok((
4432                Value::Tombstone(TombstoneInfo {
4433                    deletion_time,
4434                    tombstone_type: TombstoneType::CellTombstone,
4435                    // On-disk `localDeletionTime` (GC clock, seconds) for the cell
4436                    // tombstone; `0` when not surfaced (#873).
4437                    local_deletion_time: cell_local_deletion_time.unwrap_or(0),
4438                    ttl: None,
4439                    range_start: None,
4440                    range_end: None,
4441                }),
4442                cell_timestamp,
4443                cell_expiration,
4444                offset,
4445            ));
4446        }
4447
4448        // Handle empty cells (no value bytes to read)
4449        if !has_value {
4450            log::debug!(
4451                "V5CompressedLegacy: Cell '{}' has HAS_EMPTY_VALUE flag, returning empty value",
4452                column.name
4453            );
4454            // Return appropriate empty value for type
4455            // For most types, empty = empty string or empty collection
4456            return Ok((
4457                Value::Text(String::new()),
4458                cell_timestamp,
4459                cell_expiration,
4460                offset,
4461            ));
4462        }
4463
4464        // At this point, we have a live cell with value data
4465        // The value parsing logic below is unchanged from the original implementation
4466
4467        // Parse based on column type (data_type is a String with CQL type name)
4468        // CRITICAL: Normalize type name to lowercase for case-insensitive matching
4469        // Schema may provide "TEXT", "INT", etc. (uppercase) while match arms use lowercase
4470        let normalized_type = column.data_type.to_lowercase();
4471        let value = match normalized_type.as_str() {
4472            "boolean" => {
4473                // Boolean: [0x08][u8 value]
4474                if offset >= data.len() {
4475                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4476                        "Cell '{}': unexpected end at boolean value",
4477                        column.name
4478                    )));
4479                }
4480                let bool_byte = data[offset];
4481                offset += 1;
4482                Value::Boolean(bool_byte != 0)
4483            }
4484
4485            "int" => {
4486                // Integer (i32): fixed-width 4 bytes (no length prefix in Cassandra 5.0)
4487                if offset + 4 > data.len() {
4488                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4489                        "Cell '{}': need 4 bytes for int, only {} available",
4490                        column.name,
4491                        data.len() - offset
4492                    )));
4493                }
4494                let int_val = i32::from_be_bytes([
4495                    data[offset],
4496                    data[offset + 1],
4497                    data[offset + 2],
4498                    data[offset + 3],
4499                ]);
4500                offset += 4;
4501                Value::Integer(int_val)
4502            }
4503
4504            "text" | "varchar" | "ascii" => {
4505                // Text: [VInt len][text bytes]
4506                // V5CompressedLegacy uses VInt length encoding for variable-length types
4507                let (remaining, text_len) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
4508                    Error::corruption(format!(
4509                        "Cell '{}': failed to parse text length as VInt: {:?}",
4510                        column.name, e
4511                    ))
4512                })?;
4513                let text_len = text_len as usize;
4514                let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
4515                offset += bytes_consumed;
4516
4517                if offset + text_len > data.len() {
4518                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4519                        "Cell '{}': need {} bytes for text, only {} available",
4520                        column.name,
4521                        text_len,
4522                        data.len() - offset
4523                    )));
4524                }
4525
4526                let text_bytes = &data[offset..offset + text_len];
4527                let text = String::from_utf8(text_bytes.to_vec()).map_err(|e| {
4528                    Error::corruption(format!(
4529                        "Cell '{}': invalid UTF-8 in text value: {}",
4530                        column.name, e
4531                    ))
4532                })?;
4533
4534                offset += text_len;
4535                Value::Text(text)
4536            }
4537
4538            "uuid" | "timeuuid" => {
4539                // UUID/TimeUUID: fixed-width 16 bytes (no length prefix in Cassandra 5.0 writer)
4540                if offset + 16 > data.len() {
4541                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4542                        "Cell '{}': need 16 bytes for UUID, only {} available",
4543                        column.name,
4544                        data.len() - offset
4545                    )));
4546                }
4547
4548                let uuid_bytes: [u8; 16] = data[offset..offset + 16]
4549                    .try_into()
4550                    .map_err(|_| Error::corruption("UUID byte conversion failed"))?;
4551
4552                offset += 16;
4553                Value::Uuid(uuid_bytes)
4554            }
4555
4556            "decimal" => {
4557                // Decimal: [VInt total_len][i32 scale][unscaled bytes]
4558                if offset >= data.len() {
4559                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4560                        "Cell '{}': unexpected end at decimal length",
4561                        column.name
4562                    )));
4563                }
4564
4565                let (remaining, total_len) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
4566                    Error::corruption(format!(
4567                        "Cell '{}': failed to parse decimal length as VInt: {:?}",
4568                        column.name, e
4569                    ))
4570                })?;
4571                let total_len = total_len as usize;
4572                let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
4573                offset += bytes_consumed;
4574
4575                if offset + total_len > data.len() {
4576                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4577                        "Cell '{}': need {} bytes for decimal, only {} available",
4578                        column.name,
4579                        total_len,
4580                        data.len() - offset
4581                    )));
4582                }
4583
4584                // First 4 bytes: scale (i32 BE)
4585                if total_len < 4 {
4586                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4587                        "Cell '{}': decimal length {} too small for scale",
4588                        column.name, total_len
4589                    )));
4590                }
4591                let scale = i32::from_be_bytes([
4592                    data[offset],
4593                    data[offset + 1],
4594                    data[offset + 2],
4595                    data[offset + 3],
4596                ]);
4597
4598                // Remaining bytes: unscaled value
4599                let unscaled = data[offset + 4..offset + total_len].to_vec();
4600                offset += total_len;
4601
4602                Value::Decimal { scale, unscaled }
4603            }
4604
4605            "bigint" => {
4606                // BigInt: fixed-width 8 bytes (no length prefix in Cassandra 5.0)
4607                if offset + 8 > data.len() {
4608                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4609                        "Cell '{}': need 8 bytes for bigint, only {} available",
4610                        column.name,
4611                        data.len() - offset
4612                    )));
4613                }
4614                let val = i64::from_be_bytes([
4615                    data[offset],
4616                    data[offset + 1],
4617                    data[offset + 2],
4618                    data[offset + 3],
4619                    data[offset + 4],
4620                    data[offset + 5],
4621                    data[offset + 6],
4622                    data[offset + 7],
4623                ]);
4624                offset += 8;
4625                Value::BigInt(val)
4626            }
4627
4628            "counter" => {
4629                // Counter cells can arrive in two formats:
4630                //
4631                // 1. Real Cassandra CounterContext: [VInt length][header_size:i16][indices][shards]
4632                //    The counter value is the sum of all shard counts.
4633                //
4634                // 2. CQLite writer format (raw i64): [VInt(8)][8 bytes big-endian i64]
4635                //    The writer serialises Value::Counter as a plain 8-byte integer with a
4636                //    length prefix of 8, identical to how BigInt is written.
4637                //
4638                // We try CounterContext first and fall back to the raw-i64 interpretation
4639                // when the length prefix equals exactly 8 (the size of a raw i64).
4640
4641                // Read the VInt length prefix.
4642                let (remaining, context_len) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
4643                    Error::corruption(format!(
4644                        "Cell '{}': failed to parse counter context length as VInt: {:?}",
4645                        column.name, e
4646                    ))
4647                })?;
4648                let context_len = context_len as usize;
4649                let len_bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
4650                offset += len_bytes_consumed;
4651
4652                log::debug!(
4653                    "V5CompressedLegacy: Counter '{}' context_len={} (len prefix: {} bytes)",
4654                    column.name,
4655                    context_len,
4656                    len_bytes_consumed
4657                );
4658
4659                if offset + context_len > data.len() {
4660                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4661                        "Cell '{}': need {} bytes for counter context, only {} available",
4662                        column.name,
4663                        context_len,
4664                        data.len() - offset
4665                    )));
4666                }
4667
4668                // Try the full CounterContext parse first.
4669                match Self::parse_counter_context(data, offset, &column.name) {
4670                    Ok((total, consumed)) if consumed == context_len => {
4671                        // Successfully parsed a proper CounterContext.
4672                        offset += consumed;
4673                        log::debug!(
4674                            "V5CompressedLegacy: Counter '{}' value={} (CounterContext), total consumed {} bytes",
4675                            column.name,
4676                            total,
4677                            len_bytes_consumed + context_len
4678                        );
4679                        Value::Counter(total)
4680                    }
4681                    _ if context_len == 8 => {
4682                        // A real Cassandra CounterContext is at minimum 36 bytes
4683                        // (2 header + 2 indices + 32 body for 1 shard), so
4684                        // context_len == 8 can only be produced by the CQLite writer
4685                        // which serialises Counter as a raw big-endian i64.
4686                        // This intentionally swallows any parse_counter_context error
4687                        // for 8-byte payloads, which is safe since a valid
4688                        // CounterContext can never be 8 bytes.
4689                        //
4690                        // Bounds already verified by the context_len check above.
4691                        let val = i64::from_be_bytes([
4692                            data[offset],
4693                            data[offset + 1],
4694                            data[offset + 2],
4695                            data[offset + 3],
4696                            data[offset + 4],
4697                            data[offset + 5],
4698                            data[offset + 6],
4699                            data[offset + 7],
4700                        ]);
4701                        offset += 8;
4702                        log::debug!(
4703                            "V5CompressedLegacy: Counter '{}' value={} (raw i64 fallback), total consumed {} bytes",
4704                            column.name,
4705                            val,
4706                            len_bytes_consumed + 8
4707                        );
4708                        Value::Counter(val)
4709                    }
4710                    Err(e) => return Err(e),
4711                    Ok((_, consumed)) => {
4712                        return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4713                            "Counter '{}': VInt length ({}) doesn't match parsed context size ({})",
4714                            column.name, context_len, consumed
4715                        )));
4716                    }
4717                }
4718            }
4719
4720            "double" => {
4721                // Double: 8 bytes, f64 big-endian (NO length prefix)
4722                if offset + 8 > data.len() {
4723                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
4724                        "Cell '{}': need 8 bytes for double, only {} available",
4725                        column.name,
4726                        data.len() - offset
4727                    )));
4728                }
4729                let val = f64::from_be_bytes([
4730                    data[offset],
4731                    data[offset + 1],
4732                    data[offset + 2],
4733                    data[offset + 3],
4734                    data[offset + 4],
4735                    data[offset + 5],
4736                    data[offset + 6],
4737                    data[offset + 7],
4738                ]);
4739                offset += 8;
4740                Value::Float(val)
4741            }
4742
4743            "timestamp" => {
