6457        // excluded above (frozen<...> / FrozenType(...)), and a UDT nested inside
6458        // a collection (e.g. ListType(UserType(...))) is matched by its outer
6459        // list/set/map branch, so a bare `usertype(` prefix here is unambiguous.
6460        if dt.starts_with("org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.usertype(") {
6461            return true;
6462        }
6463
6464        false
6465    }
6466
6467    /// Parse the OUTERMOST `UserType(ks,hexname,hexfield:type,...)` marshal string
6468    /// into its DECLARED field order, returning `(field_name, field_marshal_type)`
6469    /// pairs (issue #927). The field type is kept as its raw marshal string so the
6470    /// per-field value bytes can be decoded with [`parse_value_from_raw_bytes`].
6471    ///
6472    /// Reuses the same paren-matching / hex-name decoding as
6473    /// [`parse_udt_type_definition`]; the two differ only in that this preserves
6474    /// the raw type string instead of converting it to a `CqlType`.
6475    fn udt_field_marshal_types(type_str: &str) -> Result<Vec<(String, String)>> {
6476        let start_marker = "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.UserType(";
6477        let type_lower = type_str.to_lowercase();
6478        let start_marker_lower = start_marker.to_lowercase();
6479        let start_idx = type_lower
6480            .find(&start_marker_lower)
6481            .ok_or_else(|| Error::schema(format!("Not a UserType: {}", type_str)))?;
6482
6483        let inner_start = start_idx + start_marker.len();
6484        let mut paren_depth = 1;
6485        let mut end_idx = inner_start;
6486        let chars: Vec<char> = type_str[inner_start..].chars().collect();
6487        for (i, c) in chars.iter().enumerate() {
6488            match c {
6489                '(' => paren_depth += 1,
6490                ')' => {
6491                    paren_depth -= 1;
6492                    if paren_depth == 0 {
6493                        end_idx = inner_start + i;
6494                        break;
6495                    }
6496                }
6497                _ => {}
6498            }
6499        }
6500        if paren_depth != 0 {
6501            return Err(Error::schema(format!(
6502                "Unbalanced parentheses in UserType: {}",
6503                type_str
6504            )));
6505        }
6506
6507        let inner = &type_str[inner_start..end_idx];
6508        let parts = Self::split_type_args(inner)?;
6509        if parts.len() < 2 {
6510            return Err(Error::schema(format!(
6511                "UserType requires at least keyspace and name: {}",
6512                inner
6513            )));
6514        }
6515
6516        let mut fields = Vec::with_capacity(parts.len().saturating_sub(2));
6517        for field_def in parts.iter().skip(2) {
6518            let field_def = field_def.trim();
6519            if field_def.is_empty() {
6520                continue;
6521            }
6522            let colon_idx = field_def.find(':').ok_or_else(|| {
6523                Error::schema(format!(
6524                    "Invalid UDT field definition (missing colon): {}",
6525                    field_def
6526                ))
6527            })?;
6528            let field_name = Self::decode_hex_name(&field_def[..colon_idx])?;
6529            let field_type = field_def[colon_idx + 1..].trim().to_string();
6530            fields.push((field_name, field_type));
6531        }
6532        Ok(fields)
6533    }
6534
6535    /// Extract `(keyspace, type_name)` from the outermost `UserType(...)` marshal
6536    /// string (issue #927). The keyspace is the first arg; the name is the
6537    /// hex-decoded second arg.
6538    fn udt_keyspace_and_name(type_str: &str) -> Result<(String, String)> {
6539        let udt_def = Self::parse_udt_type_definition(type_str)?;
6540        Ok((udt_def.keyspace, udt_def.name))
6541    }
6542
6543    /// Parse a complex column (non-frozen collection).
6544    /// Complex columns have multiple cells with cell paths.
6545    ///
6546    /// Format when HAS_COMPLEX_DELETION is set:
6547    ///   [complex_deletion_time: 2 VInts]  // DeletionTime
6548    ///   [cell_count: VInt]
6549    ///   [cell_1..cell_n: each with cell_path]
6550    ///
6551    /// Format when HAS_COMPLEX_DELETION is NOT set:
6552    ///   [cell_count: VInt]
6553    ///   [cell_1..cell_n: each with cell_path]
6554    ///
6555    /// Issue #221: This enables parsing of typed_collections_table and other
6556    /// tables with non-frozen collections.
6557    /// Outer entry point — the `reader` parameter is forwarded to the inner
6558    /// cells but is currently unused there (`_reader`).  The outer/inner split
6559    /// lets unit tests call `parse_complex_column_inner` without constructing a
6560    /// full `SSTableReader`.
6561    ///
6562    /// Returns `(value, new_offset, collection_meta)` where `collection_meta`
6563    /// carries DS4 extra info: whether the collection carries a tombstone
6564    /// (overwrite semantics), the max element writetime, and the element tombstone count.
6565    fn parse_complex_column(
6566        &self,
6567        data: &[u8],
6568        offset: usize,
6569        column: &crate::schema::Column,
6570        has_complex_deletion: bool,
6571        _reader: &super::super::types::SSTableReader,
6572    ) -> Result<(Value, usize, ComplexColumnMeta)> {
6573        self.parse_complex_column_inner(data, offset, column, has_complex_deletion, 0, None)
6574    }
6575
6576    /// Inner complex-column parser.
6577    ///
6578    /// When `elements_out` is `Some`, each parsed element (live, empty, or
6579    /// tombstoned) is also pushed as a
6580    /// [`crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::ComplexElement`] in
6581    /// on-disk order, so the compaction read path can surface per-element cells
6582    /// (epic #899). `row_timestamp` is the row liveness timestamp (µs) inherited
6583    /// by elements that carry the `USE_ROW_TIMESTAMP` (0x08) flag — only read
6584    /// when collecting elements. On the user-facing read path `elements_out` is
6585    /// `None`, `row_timestamp` is `0`, and no per-element collection occurs.
6586    pub(crate) fn parse_complex_column_inner(
6587        &self,
6588        data: &[u8],
6589        mut offset: usize,
6590        column: &crate::schema::Column,
6591        has_complex_deletion: bool,
6592        row_timestamp: i64,
6593        mut elements_out: Option<
6594            &mut Vec<crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::ComplexElement>,
6595        >,
6596    ) -> Result<(Value, usize, ComplexColumnMeta)> {
6597        use crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::ComplexElement;
6598
6599        // Helper to push a per-element cell into `elements_out` (compaction
6600        // path only). `decoded_value` is the resolved element value (the list
6601        // member, the set member parsed from the path, or the map value);
6602        // `None` for a tombstoned / empty element. The effective timestamp is
6603        // the element-own writetime when present, else the inherited row
6604        // timestamp (USE_ROW_TIMESTAMP).
6605        fn record_element(
6606            out: &mut Option<&mut Vec<ComplexElement>>,
6607            cell: &ComplexCellParse,
6608            decoded_value: Option<Value>,
6609            decoded_key: Option<Value>,
6610            row_timestamp: i64,
6611        ) {
6612            if let Some(vec) = out.as_mut() {
6613                vec.push(ComplexElement {
6614                    cell_path: cell.path_bytes.clone(),
6615                    value: decoded_value,
6616                    decoded_key,
6617                    timestamp: cell.element_writetime.unwrap_or(row_timestamp),
6618                    ttl: cell.element_ttl,
6619                    local_deletion_time: cell.element_local_deletion_time,
6620                    is_deleted: cell.is_deleted,
6621                    has_empty_value: cell.has_empty_value,
6622                });
6623            }
6624        }
6625        log::debug!(
6626            "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsing complex column '{}' type='{}' has_complex_deletion={} at offset {}",
6627            column.name, column.data_type, has_complex_deletion, offset
6628        );
6629
6630        // Step 1: Parse complex deletion time if flag is set.
6631        //
6632        // DS4 (Issue #700): Capture the `markedForDeleteAt` to determine whether this
6633        // generation carries a **collection-level tombstone** (`s = {...}` overwrite).
6634        // Cassandra stores the LIVE sentinel as i64::MIN when there is no tombstone;
6635        // any other value means the collection was overwritten (replaced, not appended).
6636        //
6637        // Wire format: DeletionTime = markedForDeleteAt (VInt delta from min_timestamp)
6638        //                           + localDeletionTime (VInt).
6639        // We treat `marked_for_delete_at != i64::MIN` as "has collection tombstone".
6640        let mut has_collection_tombstone = false;
6641        // Epic #899: the real complex deletion `(markedForDeleteAt µs,
6642        // localDeletionTime s)` for the compaction contract; `None` is the LIVE
6643        // sentinel (no overwrite).
6644        let mut complex_deletion: Option<(i64, i32)> = None;
6645        if has_complex_deletion {
6646            // Cassandra (SerializationHeader.writeDeletionTime ->
6647            // writeUnsignedVInt) encodes the markedForDeleteAt delta from
6648            // min_timestamp as an UNSIGNED VInt — matching the row-deletion path
6649            // (see parse_row_metadata, ~line 2585) and the writer
6650            // (write_complex_column_deletion, encode_unsigned). The earlier
6651            // parse_vint (ZigZag/signed) here mis-decoded any delta whose top
6652            // data bit was set, while still consuming the same number of bytes
6653            // (both variants are driven by leading-ones). Fix (roborev #863).
6654            let (remaining, mfda_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
6655                Error::corruption(format!(
6656                    "Complex column '{}': failed to parse markedForDeleteAt at offset {}: {:?}",
6657                    column.name, offset, e
6658                ))
6659            })?;
6660            let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
6661            offset += bytes_consumed;
6662
6663            // Delta-decode to get the absolute timestamp.
6664            // The LIVE sentinel in Cassandra is Long.MIN_VALUE for markedForDeleteAt.
6665            let absolute_mfda = self.min_timestamp.wrapping_add(mfda_delta as i64);
6666            // Any value other than i64::MIN indicates a real collection tombstone.
6667            if absolute_mfda != i64::MIN {
6668                has_collection_tombstone = true;
6669            }
6670
6671            // localDeletionTime is also an UNSIGNED VInt delta from
6672            // min_local_deletion_time (writer: encode_unsigned). Use the SAME
6673            // i32 wrapping/cast as the row/range deletion paths so far-future
6674            // LDTs in [2^31, 2^32) round-trip via `as u32 as i32`.
6675            let (remaining, local_deletion_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
6676                Error::corruption(format!(
6677                    "Complex column '{}': failed to parse localDeletionTime at offset {}: {:?}",
6678                    column.name, offset, e
6679                ))
6680            })?;
6681            let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
6682            offset += bytes_consumed;
6683
6684            // Surface the real complex deletion for the compaction path. The
6685            // localDeletionTime is a delta from min_local_deletion_time; the
6686            // LIVE sentinel is i32::MAX. Far-future values in [2^31, 2^32) wrap
6687            // via `as u32 as i32` (epic #899 invariant). Only record a deletion
6688            // when markedForDeleteAt is not the LIVE sentinel.
6689            if absolute_mfda != i64::MIN {
6690                let absolute_ldt = self
6691                    .min_local_deletion_time
6692                    .wrapping_add(local_deletion_delta as i64);
6693                complex_deletion = Some((absolute_mfda, absolute_ldt as u32 as i32));
6694            }
6695
6696            log::debug!(
6697                "V5CompressedLegacy: Complex column '{}' deletion time parsed \
6698                 (absolute_mfda={} has_collection_tombstone={}), now at offset {}",
6699                column.name,
6700                absolute_mfda,
6701                has_collection_tombstone,
6702                offset
6703            );
6704        }
6705
6706        // Step 2: Parse cell count
6707        let (remaining, cell_count) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
6708            Error::corruption(format!(
6709                "Complex column '{}': failed to parse cell count at offset {}: {:?}",
6710                column.name, offset, e
6711            ))
6712        })?;
6713        let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
6714        offset += bytes_consumed;
6715
6716        log::debug!(
6717            "V5CompressedLegacy: Complex column '{}' has {} cells, now at offset {}",
6718            column.name,
6719            cell_count,
6720            offset
6721        );
6722
6723        // Step 3: Parse all cells and aggregate values
6724        // Issue #225: Bounds check to prevent DoS from corrupted data (match frozen collection pattern)
6725        if cell_count > MAX_FROZEN_COLLECTION_SIZE {
6726            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
6727                "Complex column '{}': cell count {} exceeds maximum {}",
6728                column.name, cell_count, MAX_FROZEN_COLLECTION_SIZE
6729            )));
6730        }
6731        // Convert cell_count to usize safely to prevent overflow on 32-bit systems
6732        let cell_count_usize: usize = cell_count.try_into().map_err(|_| {
6733            Error::corruption(format!(
6734                "Complex column '{}': cell count {} exceeds platform limit",
6735                column.name, cell_count
6736            ))
6737        })?;
6738
6739        // DS4 (Issue #700): Track max element writetime and element tombstone count
6740        // across all cells in this collection.
6741        let mut max_element_writetime: i64 = 0;
6742        let mut element_tombstone_count: u64 = 0;
6743
6744        /// Helper to update max_element_writetime from a parsed cell.
6745        #[inline]
6746        fn update_max_writetime(max: &mut i64, cell: &ComplexCellParse) {
6747            if let Some(ts) = cell.element_writetime {
6748                if ts > *max {
6749                    *max = ts;
6750                }
6751            }
6752        }
6753
6754        // Determine collection type and extract element type(s)
6755        let dt = column.data_type.to_lowercase();
6756        let value = if dt.starts_with("list<")
6757            || dt.starts_with("org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.listtype(")
6758        {
6759            // Parse list elements
6760            let element_type = self.extract_collection_element_type(&column.data_type, "list")?;
6761            let mut elements = Vec::with_capacity(cell_count_usize);
6762
6763            for i in 0..cell_count_usize {
6764                let cell =
6765                    self.parse_complex_cell_value(data, offset, &element_type, column, i as u64)?;
6766                offset = cell.next_offset;
6767
6768                // Issue #493: element-level tombstones (IS_DELETED 0x01) are not live
6769                // values and must not be surfaced. Skip them regardless of their path.
6770                // DS4: count them for the scan-summary warning counter.
6771                if cell.is_deleted {
6772                    element_tombstone_count += 1;
6773                    log::debug!(
6774                        "V5CompressedLegacy: list element {} in column '{}' is a tombstone \
6775                         (IS_DELETED=0x01) — counted for DS4 scan summary (Issue #700/#493)",
6776                        i,
6777                        column.name
6778                    );
6779                    // Epic #899: surface the tombstoned element to the compaction
6780                    // path (value None) so per-element reconcile can shadow it.
6781                    record_element(&mut elements_out, &cell, None, None, row_timestamp);
6782                    continue;
6783                }
6784
6785                // DS4: Track element timestamp for live elements only (roborev Finding 2).
6786                // Tombstoned elements are skipped above; their timestamps must not
6787                // inflate the max_element_writetime reported for the collection.
6788                update_max_writetime(&mut max_element_writetime, &cell);
6789
6790                // Epic #899: surface this live element to the compaction path.
6791                record_element(
6792                    &mut elements_out,
6793                    &cell,
6794                    cell.value.clone(),
6795                    None,
6796                    row_timestamp,
6797                );
6798
6799                // Add non-null values to the list
6800                if let Some(val) = cell.value {
6801                    elements.push(val);
6802                }
6803            }
6804
6805            Value::List(elements)
6806        } else if dt.starts_with("set<")
6807            || dt.starts_with("org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.settype(")
6808        {
6809            // Parse set elements
6810            // In Cassandra's complex cell format for sets, each element is a separate cell
6811            // where the cell PATH contains the raw bytes of the set element, and the cell
6812            // VALUE is always empty (HAS_EMPTY_VALUE flag = 0x04 set).
6813            // We must parse the path bytes as the element value, not the (empty) cell value.
6814            let element_type = self.extract_collection_element_type(&column.data_type, "set")?;
6815            let mut elements = Vec::with_capacity(cell_count_usize);
6816
6817            for i in 0..cell_count_usize {
6818                let cell =
6819                    self.parse_complex_cell_value(data, offset, &element_type, column, i as u64)?;
6820                offset = cell.next_offset;
6821
6822                // Issue #493: element-level tombstones must not surface as live members.
6823                // For a set, both a live element and a tombstoned element produce
6824                // `cell.value == None` with non-empty `path_bytes` (the element key),
6825                // because live set elements carry HAS_EMPTY_VALUE (0x04) and store the
6826                // element in the path. The authoritative IS_DELETED (0x01) flag is the
6827                // ONLY signal that distinguishes them, so we consult it directly and skip
6828                // tombstoned elements (no-heuristics mandate, Issue #28).
6829                // DS4: count them for the scan-summary warning counter.
6830                if cell.is_deleted {
6831                    element_tombstone_count += 1;
6832                    log::debug!(
6833                        "V5CompressedLegacy: set element {} in column '{}' is a tombstone \
6834                         (IS_DELETED=0x01) — counted for DS4 scan summary (Issue #700/#493)",
6835                        i,
6836                        column.name
6837                    );
6838                    // Epic #899: surface the tombstoned set element (the element
6839                    // identity lives in the cell_path).
6840                    record_element(&mut elements_out, &cell, None, None, row_timestamp);
6841                    continue;
6842                }
6843
6844                // DS4: Track element timestamp for live elements only (roborev Finding 2).
6845                // Tombstoned elements are skipped above; their timestamps must not
6846                // inflate the max_element_writetime reported for the collection.
6847                update_max_writetime(&mut max_element_writetime, &cell);
6848
6849                // For sets: the path bytes ARE the element value (cell value is always empty).
6850                // If cell.value is Some (unusual case where a set cell has a non-empty value),
6851                // use it. Otherwise parse the path bytes as the element type.
6852                let set_member: Option<Value> = if let Some(val) = cell.value.clone() {
6853                    Some(val)
6854                } else if !cell.path_bytes.is_empty() {
6855                    // Path bytes are the set element — parse them as the element type
6856                    match self.parse_value_from_raw_bytes(
6857                        &cell.path_bytes,
6858                        &element_type,
6859                        &column.name,
6860                        0,
6861                    ) {
6862                        Ok(val) => Some(val),
6863                        Err(e) => {
6864                            log::debug!(
6865                                "V5CompressedLegacy: set element {} parse failed (type={}): {}",
6866                                i,
6867                                element_type,
6868                                e
6869                            );
6870                            None
6871                        }
6872                    }
6873                } else {
6874                    None
6875                };
6876
6877                // Epic #899: surface the live set element (decoded member value)
6878                // to the compaction path, keyed by its cell_path.
6879                record_element(
6880                    &mut elements_out,
6881                    &cell,
6882                    set_member.clone(),
6883                    None,
6884                    row_timestamp,
6885                );
6886
6887                if let Some(val) = set_member {
6888                    elements.push(val);
6889                }
6890            }
6891
6892            Value::Set(elements)
6893        } else if dt.starts_with("map<")
6894            || dt.starts_with("org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.maptype(")
6895        {
6896            // Parse map entries
6897            let (key_type, value_type) = self.extract_map_types(&column.data_type)?;
6898            let mut entries = Vec::with_capacity(cell_count_usize);
6899
6900            for i in 0..cell_count_usize {
6901                let cell =
6902                    self.parse_complex_cell_value(data, offset, &value_type, column, i as u64)?;
6903                offset = cell.next_offset;
6904
6905                // For maps, the cell path IS the key
6906                // Parse the path as the key using the key type
6907                // Note: Cell path keys are stored WITHOUT length prefixes (raw bytes only)
6908                //
6909                // Map semantics are intentionally unchanged for Issue #493: a deleted
6910                // entry already surfaces as `cell.value == None` and is emitted as
6911                // (key, Value::Null), preserving existing behavior. Only set/list
6912                // element tombstones are skipped.
6913                // DS4: For maps with IS_DELETED entries, count them for the scan summary.
6914                // Tombstoned entries must NOT contribute to max_element_writetime so that
6915                // the reported writetime only reflects live content (roborev Finding 2).
6916                if cell.is_deleted {
6917                    element_tombstone_count += 1;
6918                    log::debug!(
6919                        "V5CompressedLegacy: map entry {} in column '{}' is a tombstone \
6920                         (IS_DELETED=0x01) — counted for DS4 scan summary (Issue #700/#493)",
6921                        i,
6922                        column.name
6923                    );
6924                } else {
6925                    // DS4: Track element timestamp for live map entries only.
6926                    update_max_writetime(&mut max_element_writetime, &cell);
6927                }
6928
6929                // Decode the map key (from cell_path) up front so it can be both
6930                // recorded on the per-element compaction entry and used to build
6931                // the collapsed `Value::Map`.
6932                let decoded_key = if !cell.path_bytes.is_empty() {
6933                    log::debug!(
6934                        "V5CompressedLegacy: Parsing map key for column '{}', key_type='{}', path_len={}",
6935                        column.name,
6936                        key_type,
6937                        cell.path_bytes.len()
6938                    );
6939                    // For cell path keys, parse directly without expecting length prefixes
6940                    Some(self.parse_cell_path_key(&cell.path_bytes, &key_type, &column.name)?)
6941                } else {
6942                    None
6943                };
6944
6945                // Epic #899: surface the map entry to the compaction path keyed
6946                // by its cell_path (the map key bytes); value is the map value
6947                // (`None` for a tombstoned / null entry), with the decoded key for
6948                // whole-`Value::Map` reconstruction downstream.
6949                record_element(
6950                    &mut elements_out,
6951                    &cell,
6952                    cell.value.clone(),
6953                    decoded_key.clone(),
6954                    row_timestamp,
6955                );
6956
6957                if let Some(key_value) = decoded_key {
6958                    // Add non-null entries to the map
6959                    if let Some(val) = cell.value {
6960                        entries.push((key_value, val));
6961                    } else {
6962                        // Map entry with null value (tombstone for that key)
6963                        entries.push((key_value, Value::Null));
6964                    }
6965                }
6966            }
6967
6968            Value::Map(entries)
6969        } else if dt.starts_with("org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.usertype(") {
6970            // Issue #927: TOP-LEVEL non-frozen UDT — each field is a cell whose
6971            // cell_path is the 2-byte (signed ShortType) declared field index and
6972            // whose value bytes are the field datum. Decode each cell's value with
6973            // the DECLARED field type resolved from the marshal string.
6974            let field_defs = Self::udt_field_marshal_types(&column.data_type)?;
6975            // Field values keyed by declared index; absent / null fields stay None.
6976            let mut field_values: Vec<Option<Value>> = vec![None; field_defs.len()];
6977
6978            for i in 0..cell_count_usize {
6979                // Capture the value bytes raw (BytesType is identity) so they can
6980                // be re-decoded with the per-field type AFTER the cell_path (which
6981                // carries the field index) is known.
6982                let cell = self.parse_complex_cell_value(
6983                    data,
6984                    offset,
6985                    "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.BytesType",
6986                    column,
6987                    i as u64,
6988                )?;
6989                offset = cell.next_offset;
6990
6991                // Resolve the declared field index from the 2-byte signed-short
6992                // cell_path. A path that is not exactly 2 bytes, or that names a
6993                // field index outside the declared range, is authoritative
6994                // corruption — surface it rather than guessing (no-heuristics).
6995                let field_index = if cell.path_bytes.len() == 2 {
6996                    i16::from_be_bytes([cell.path_bytes[0], cell.path_bytes[1]]) as i32
6997                } else {
6998                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
6999                        "UDT column '{}' cell {}: field-index cell_path must be 2 bytes, got {}",
7000                        column.name,
7001                        i,
7002                        cell.path_bytes.len()
7003                    )));
7004                };
7005
7006                if cell.is_deleted {
7007                    element_tombstone_count += 1;
7008                    record_element(&mut elements_out, &cell, None, None, row_timestamp);
7009                    continue;
7010                }
7011                update_max_writetime(&mut max_element_writetime, &cell);
7012
7013                // Decode the field value with its DECLARED type. `cell.value` is the
7014                // raw bytes wrapped as Blob (BytesType) above; an empty-value cell
7015                // yields None.
7016                let decoded = match &cell.value {
7017                    Some(Value::Blob(raw)) => {
7018                        let (_name, field_type) = field_defs
7019                            .get(field_index as usize)
7020                            .filter(|_| field_index >= 0)
7021                            .ok_or_else(|| {
7022                                Error::corruption(format!(
7023                                    "UDT column '{}' cell {}: field index {} out of range (0..{})",
7024                                    column.name,
7025                                    i,
7026                                    field_index,
7027                                    field_defs.len()
7028                                ))
7029                            })?;
7030                        Some(self.parse_value_from_raw_bytes(raw, field_type, &column.name, 0)?)
7031                    }
7032                    other => other.clone(),
7033                };
7034
7035                record_element(
7036                    &mut elements_out,
7037                    &cell,
7038                    decoded.clone(),
7039                    None,
7040                    row_timestamp,
7041                );
7042
7043                if field_index >= 0 && (field_index as usize) < field_values.len() {
7044                    field_values[field_index as usize] = decoded;
7045                }
7046            }
7047
7048            // Build the collapsed UDT in DECLARED field order for the user-facing
7049            // read path. The keyspace/type-name come from the marshal string.
7050            let (udt_keyspace, udt_name) = Self::udt_keyspace_and_name(&column.data_type)?;
7051            let fields = field_defs
7052                .iter()
7053                .zip(field_values)
7054                .map(|((name, _ty), value)| crate::types::UdtField {
7055                    name: name.clone(),
7056                    value,
7057                })
7058                .collect();
7059            Value::Udt(UdtValue {
7060                type_name: udt_name,
7061                keyspace: udt_keyspace,
7062                fields,
7063            })
7064        } else {
7065            // Unknown complex column type, skip cells
7066            for i in 0..cell_count_usize {
7067                offset = self.skip_complex_cell(data, offset, &column.name, i as u64)?;
7068            }
7069            Value::Null
7070        };
7071
7072        log::debug!(
7073            "V5CompressedLegacy: Complex column '{}' parsed, final offset {} \
7074             (has_collection_tombstone={} max_element_writetime={} element_tombstone_count={})",
7075            column.name,
7076            offset,
7077            has_collection_tombstone,
7078            max_element_writetime,
7079            element_tombstone_count
7080        );
7081
7082        Ok((
7083            value,
7084            offset,
7085            ComplexColumnMeta {
7086                has_collection_tombstone,
7087                max_element_writetime,
7088                element_tombstone_count,
7089                complex_deletion,
7090            },
7091        ))
7092    }
7093
7094    /// Parse a single complex cell and extract its value.
7095    /// Complex cells have: [flags] [timestamp?] [deletion?] [ttl?] [cell_path] [value?]
7096    ///
7097    /// Returns a [`ComplexCellParse`] describing the parsed cell.
7098    /// - `value` is None if the cell is deleted or has an empty value
7099    /// - `path_bytes` contains the raw path bytes (used as map key for map<> types,
7100    ///   and as the element value for set<> types)
7101    /// - `is_deleted` reflects the authoritative IS_DELETED (0x01) cell flag, so
7102    ///   callers can distinguish element-level tombstones from live elements that
7103    ///   simply carry an empty value (Issue #493).
7104    fn parse_complex_cell_value(
7105        &self,
7106        data: &[u8],
7107        mut offset: usize,
7108        element_type: &str,
7109        column: &crate::schema::Column,
7110        cell_index: u64,
7111    ) -> Result<ComplexCellParse> {
7112        log::debug!(
7113            "V5CompressedLegacy: parse_complex_cell_value '{}' cell {} element_type='{}' starting at offset {}",
7114            column.name,
7115            cell_index,
7116            element_type,
7117            offset
7118        );
7119
7120        // Step 1: Cell flags (standard 0x00-0x1F range)
7121        if offset >= data.len() {
7122            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7123                "Complex cell {}.{}: unexpected end at flags (offset {})",
7124                column.name, cell_index, offset
7125            )));
7126        }
7127        let flags = data[offset];
7128        offset += 1;
7129
7130        // Validate flags are in valid range
7131        if flags > 0x1F {
7132            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7133                "Complex cell {}.{}: invalid flags 0x{:02x} at offset {} (expected 0x00-0x1F)",
7134                column.name,
7135                cell_index,
7136                flags,
7137                offset - 1
7138            )));
7139        }
7140
7141        let is_deleted = (flags & 0x01) != 0;
7142        let is_expiring = (flags & 0x02) != 0;
7143        let has_empty_value = (flags & 0x04) != 0;
7144        let use_row_timestamp = (flags & 0x08) != 0;
7145        let use_row_ttl = (flags & 0x10) != 0;
7146
7147        log::debug!(
7148            "V5CompressedLegacy: parse_complex_cell_value '{}' cell {} flags=0x{:02x} (deleted={}, expiring={}, empty_value={}, use_row_ts={}, use_row_ttl={})",
7149            column.name,
7150            cell_index,
7151            flags,
7152            is_deleted,
7153            is_expiring,
7154            has_empty_value,
7155            use_row_timestamp,
7156            use_row_ttl
7157        );
7158
7159        // Step 2: Timestamp (if not using row timestamp)
7160        // Capture the element-level timestamp delta for DS4 max-writetime computation.
7161        // Cassandra encodes complex cell timestamps as UNSIGNED VInt deltas from
7162        // min_timestamp (SerializationHeader.writeUnsignedVInt; writer:
7163        // write_complex_cell_header, encode_unsigned). The earlier parse_vint
7164        // (ZigZag/signed) mis-decoded deltas with the top data bit set while
7165        // consuming the same byte count. Fix (roborev #863).
7166        let mut element_writetime: Option<i64> = None;
7167        if !use_row_timestamp {
7168            let (remaining, ts_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
7169                Error::corruption(format!(
7170                    "Complex cell {}.{}: failed to parse timestamp at offset {}: {:?}",
7171                    column.name, cell_index, offset, e
7172                ))
7173            })?;
7174            let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
7175            offset += bytes_consumed;
7176            // Delta decode: absolute_ts = min_timestamp + ts_delta
7177            let absolute_ts = self.min_timestamp.wrapping_add(ts_delta as i64);
7178            element_writetime = Some(absolute_ts);
7179        }
7180
7181        // Step 3: Local deletion time (if deleted/expiring and not using row TTL)
7182        // Epic #899: surface the absolute localDeletionTime (SECONDS) for the
7183        // per-element compaction contract. The on-disk value is an unsigned VInt
7184        // delta from `min_local_deletion_time`. Far-future values in
7185        // `[2^31, 2^32)` are preserved as the wrapping `as u32 as i32`
7186        // representation — do NOT widen to i64 (epic #899 invariant).
7187        let mut element_local_deletion_time: Option<i32> = None;
7188        if !use_row_ttl && (is_deleted || is_expiring) {
7189            let (remaining, ldt_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
7190                Error::corruption(format!(
7191                    "Complex cell {}.{}: failed to parse localDeletionTime at offset {}: {:?}",
7192                    column.name, cell_index, offset, e
7193                ))
7194            })?;
7195            let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
7196            offset += bytes_consumed;
7197            let absolute_ldt = self.min_local_deletion_time.wrapping_add(ldt_delta as i64);
7198            // Wrap into i32 preserving the far-future [2^31, 2^32) encoding.
7199            element_local_deletion_time = Some(absolute_ldt as u32 as i32);
7200        }
7201
7202        // Step 4: TTL (if expiring and not using row TTL)
7203        // Epic #899: surface the per-element TTL (SECONDS) for the compaction
7204        // contract. The on-disk value is an unsigned VInt delta from `min_ttl`.
7205        let mut element_ttl: Option<u32> = None;
7206        if !use_row_ttl && is_expiring {
7207            let (remaining, ttl_delta) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
7208                Error::corruption(format!(
7209                    "Complex cell {}.{}: failed to parse TTL at offset {}: {:?}",
7210                    column.name, cell_index, offset, e
7211                ))
7212            })?;
7213            let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
7214            offset += bytes_consumed;
7215            let absolute_ttl = self.min_ttl.unwrap_or(0).wrapping_add(ttl_delta as i64);
7216            element_ttl = Some(absolute_ttl as u32);
7217        }
7218
7219        // Step 5: Cell path (VInt length + bytes)
7220        let (remaining, path_len) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
7221            Error::corruption(format!(
7222                "Complex cell {}.{}: failed to parse path length at offset {}: {:?}",
7223                column.name, cell_index, offset, e
7224            ))
7225        })?;
7226        let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
7227        offset += bytes_consumed;
7228
7229        // Issue #225: Safe conversion to prevent overflow on large values
7230        let path_len_usize: usize = path_len.try_into().map_err(|_| {
7231            Error::corruption(format!(
7232                "Complex cell {}.{}: path length {} exceeds platform limit",
7233                column.name, cell_index, path_len
7234            ))
7235        })?;
7236        if path_len > MAX_CELL_VALUE_LENGTH {
7237            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7238                "Complex cell {}.{}: path length {} exceeds maximum {}",
7239                column.name, cell_index, path_len, MAX_CELL_VALUE_LENGTH
7240            )));
7241        }
7242
7243        // Bounds check before reading path
7244        if offset + path_len_usize > data.len() {
7245            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7246                "Complex cell {}.{}: cell path requires {} bytes but only {} available at offset {}",
7247                column.name,
7248                cell_index,
7249                path_len,
7250                data.len().saturating_sub(offset),
7251                offset
7252            )));
7253        }
7254
7255        let path_bytes = data[offset..offset + path_len_usize].to_vec();
7256        offset += path_len_usize;
7257
7258        // Step 6: Value (if not empty and not deleted)
7259        let value = if is_deleted || has_empty_value {
7260            log::debug!(
7261                "V5CompressedLegacy: parse_complex_cell_value '{}' cell {} is deleted or empty",
7262                column.name,
7263                cell_index
7264            );
7265            None
7266        } else {
7267            let (remaining, value_len) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
7268                Error::corruption(format!(
7269                    "Complex cell {}.{}: failed to parse value length at offset {}: {:?}",
7270                    column.name, cell_index, offset, e
7271                ))
7272            })?;
7273            let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
7274            offset += bytes_consumed;
7275
7276            // Issue #225: Safe conversion to prevent overflow on large values
7277            let value_len_usize: usize = value_len.try_into().map_err(|_| {
7278                Error::corruption(format!(
7279                    "Complex cell {}.{}: value length {} exceeds platform limit",
7280                    column.name, cell_index, value_len
7281                ))
7282            })?;
7283            if value_len > MAX_CELL_VALUE_LENGTH {
7284                return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7285                    "Complex cell {}.{}: value length {} exceeds maximum {}",
7286                    column.name, cell_index, value_len, MAX_CELL_VALUE_LENGTH
7287                )));
7288            }
7289
7290            // Bounds check before reading value
7291            if offset + value_len_usize > data.len() {
7292                return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7293                    "Complex cell {}.{}: value requires {} bytes but only {} available at offset {}",
7294                    column.name,
7295                    cell_index,
7296                    value_len,
7297                    data.len().saturating_sub(offset),
7298                    offset
7299                )));
7300            }
7301
7302            let value_data = &data[offset..offset + value_len_usize];
7303            offset += value_len_usize;
7304
7305            // Parse the value based on element type.
7306            // The value bytes have already been extracted (length was consumed above).
7307            // Use parse_value_from_raw_bytes which treats the entire slice as the value
7308            // WITHOUT an additional length prefix (unlike parse_raw_type_value which
7309            // expects a VInt length prefix — wrong for already-extracted complex cell values).
7310            // See Issue #481: using parse_raw_type_value here caused the first byte of
7311            // blob/text values to be misread as a length, producing corrupt parses.
7312            let parsed_value =
7313                self.parse_value_from_raw_bytes(value_data, element_type, &column.name, 0)?;
7314            Some(parsed_value)
7315        };
7316
7317        log::debug!(
7318            "V5CompressedLegacy: parse_complex_cell_value '{}' cell {} complete, value={:?}, final offset {}",
7319            column.name,
7320            cell_index,
7321            value.is_some(),
7322            offset
7323        );
7324
7325        Ok(ComplexCellParse {
7326            value,
7327            path_bytes,
7328            is_deleted,
7329            has_empty_value,
7330            next_offset: offset,
7331            element_writetime,
7332            element_ttl,
7333            element_local_deletion_time,
7334        })
7335    }
7336
7337    /// Skip over a single complex cell without fully parsing its value.
7338    /// Complex cells have: [flags] [timestamp?] [deletion?] [ttl?] [cell_path] [value?]
7339    ///
7340    /// Issue #221: This is used to advance past complex cell data while returning
7341    /// placeholder values. Future work can add full cell value parsing here.
7342    fn skip_complex_cell(
7343        &self,
7344        data: &[u8],
7345        mut offset: usize,
7346        column_name: &str,
7347        cell_index: u64,
7348    ) -> Result<usize> {
7349        log::debug!(
7350            "V5CompressedLegacy: skip_complex_cell '{}' cell {} starting at offset {}, bytes: {:02x?}",
7351            column_name,
7352            cell_index,
7353            offset,
7354            &data[offset..std::cmp::min(offset + 20, data.len())]
7355        );
7356
7357        // Complex cell format per Cassandra source (UnfilteredSerializer.java):
7358        // [flags: u8]
7359        // [timestamp: VInt if not USE_ROW_TIMESTAMP_MASK]
7360        // [local_deletion_time: VInt if (deleted || expiring) && not USE_ROW_TTL_MASK]
7361        // [ttl: VInt if expiring && not USE_ROW_TTL_MASK]
7362        // [cell_path: VInt length + bytes] <-- AFTER flags/timestamp/etc, NOT before!
7363        // [value: VInt length + bytes if not HAS_EMPTY_VALUE_MASK]
7364
7365        // Step 1: Cell flags (standard 0x00-0x1F range)
7366        if offset >= data.len() {
7367            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7368                "Complex cell {}.{}: unexpected end at flags (offset {})",
7369                column_name, cell_index, offset
7370            )));
7371        }
7372        let flags = data[offset];
7373        offset += 1;
7374
7375        // Validate flags are in valid range
7376        if flags > 0x1F {
7377            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7378                "Complex cell {}.{}: invalid flags 0x{:02x} at offset {} (expected 0x00-0x1F)",
7379                column_name,
7380                cell_index,
7381                flags,
7382                offset - 1
7383            )));
7384        }
7385
7386        let is_deleted = (flags & 0x01) != 0;
7387        let is_expiring = (flags & 0x02) != 0;
7388        let has_empty_value = (flags & 0x04) != 0;
7389        let use_row_timestamp = (flags & 0x08) != 0;
7390        let use_row_ttl = (flags & 0x10) != 0;
7391
7392        log::debug!(
7393            "V5CompressedLegacy: skip_complex_cell '{}' cell {} flags=0x{:02x} (deleted={}, expiring={}, empty_value={}, use_row_ts={}, use_row_ttl={})",
7394            column_name,
7395            cell_index,
7396            flags,
7397            is_deleted,
7398            is_expiring,
7399            has_empty_value,
7400            use_row_timestamp,
7401            use_row_ttl
7402        );
7403
7404        // Step 2: Timestamp (if not using row timestamp)
7405        // Skip-only: byte advancement is identical for vint/vuint, but use the
7406        // UNSIGNED variant to match the writer encoding and the decoding sites
7407        // (roborev #863).
7408        if !use_row_timestamp {
7409            let (remaining, _ts) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
7410                Error::corruption(format!(
7411                    "Complex cell {}.{}: failed to parse timestamp at offset {}: {:?}",
7412                    column_name, cell_index, offset, e
7413                ))
7414            })?;
7415            let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
7416            offset += bytes_consumed;
7417        }
7418
7419        // Step 3: Local deletion time (if deleted/expiring and not using row TTL)
7420        if !use_row_ttl && (is_deleted || is_expiring) {
7421            let (remaining, _ldt) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
7422                Error::corruption(format!(
7423                    "Complex cell {}.{}: failed to parse localDeletionTime at offset {}: {:?}",
7424                    column_name, cell_index, offset, e
7425                ))
7426            })?;
7427            let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
7428            offset += bytes_consumed;
7429        }
7430
7431        // Step 4: TTL (if expiring and not using row TTL)
7432        if !use_row_ttl && is_expiring {
7433            let (remaining, _ttl) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
7434                Error::corruption(format!(
7435                    "Complex cell {}.{}: failed to parse TTL at offset {}: {:?}",
7436                    column_name, cell_index, offset, e
7437                ))
7438            })?;
7439            let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
7440            offset += bytes_consumed;
7441        }
7442
7443        // Step 5: Cell path (VInt length + bytes) - comes AFTER flags/timestamp/ttl
7444        let (remaining, path_len) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
7445            Error::corruption(format!(
7446                "Complex cell {}.{}: failed to parse path length at offset {}: {:?}",
7447                column_name, cell_index, offset, e
7448            ))
7449        })?;
7450        let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
7451        log::debug!(
7452            "V5CompressedLegacy: skip_complex_cell '{}' cell {} path_len={} at offset {}",
7453            column_name,
7454            cell_index,
7455            path_len,
7456            offset
7457        );
7458        offset += bytes_consumed;
7459
7460        // Issue #225: Safe conversion to prevent overflow on large values
7461        let path_len_usize: usize = path_len.try_into().map_err(|_| {
7462            Error::corruption(format!(
7463                "Complex cell {}.{}: path length {} exceeds platform limit",
7464                column_name, cell_index, path_len
7465            ))
7466        })?;
7467        if path_len > MAX_CELL_VALUE_LENGTH {
7468            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7469                "Complex cell {}.{}: path length {} exceeds maximum {}",
7470                column_name, cell_index, path_len, MAX_CELL_VALUE_LENGTH
7471            )));
7472        }
7473
7474        // Bounds check before advancing by path_len
7475        if offset + path_len_usize > data.len() {
7476            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7477                "Complex cell {}.{}: cell path requires {} bytes but only {} available at offset {}",
7478                column_name,
7479                cell_index,
7480                path_len,
7481                data.len().saturating_sub(offset),
7482                offset
7483            )));
7484        }
7485        offset += path_len_usize;
7486
7487        // Step 6: Value (if not empty)
7488        if !has_empty_value {
7489            let (remaining, value_len) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
7490                Error::corruption(format!(
7491                    "Complex cell {}.{}: failed to parse value length at offset {}: {:?}",
7492                    column_name, cell_index, offset, e
7493                ))
7494            })?;
7495            let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
7496            offset += bytes_consumed;
7497
7498            // Issue #225: Safe conversion to prevent overflow on large values
7499            let value_len_usize: usize = value_len.try_into().map_err(|_| {
7500                Error::corruption(format!(
7501                    "Complex cell {}.{}: value length {} exceeds platform limit",
7502                    column_name, cell_index, value_len
7503                ))
7504            })?;
7505            if value_len > MAX_CELL_VALUE_LENGTH {
7506                return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7507                    "Complex cell {}.{}: value length {} exceeds maximum {}",
7508                    column_name, cell_index, value_len, MAX_CELL_VALUE_LENGTH
7509                )));
7510            }
7511
7512            // Bounds check before advancing by value_len
7513            if offset + value_len_usize > data.len() {
7514                return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7515                    "Complex cell {}.{}: value requires {} bytes but only {} available at offset {}",
7516                    column_name,
7517                    cell_index,
7518                    value_len,
7519                    data.len().saturating_sub(offset),
7520                    offset
7521                )));
7522            }
7523            offset += value_len_usize;
7524        }
7525
7526        log::debug!(
7527            "V5CompressedLegacy: skip_complex_cell '{}' cell {} complete, final offset {}",
7528            column_name,
7529            cell_index,
7530            offset
7531        );
7532
7533        Ok(offset)
7534    }
7535
7536    /// Extract element type from list<T> or set<T> type string (CQL or Cassandra internal format)
7537    fn extract_collection_element_type(&self, type_str: &str, collection: &str) -> Result<String> {
7538        let type_lower = type_str.to_lowercase();
7539
7540        // Check for Cassandra internal format first: org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.ListType(...)
7541        let internal_prefix_lower = format!("org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.{}type(", collection);
7542        if type_lower.starts_with(&internal_prefix_lower) && type_lower.ends_with(')') {
7543            // Use the lowercase prefix length to extract from the original string
7544            let inner = &type_str[internal_prefix_lower.len()..type_str.len() - 1];
7545            if inner.is_empty() {
7546                return Err(Error::schema(format!(
7547                    "Empty {} element type: {}",
7548                    collection, type_str
7549                )));
7550            }
7551            return Ok(inner.to_string());
7552        }
7553
7554        // Check for CQL format: list<T>, set<T>
7555        let prefix_lower = format!("{}<", collection);
7556        if type_lower.starts_with(&prefix_lower) && type_lower.ends_with('>') {
7557            // Use the lowercase prefix length to extract from the original string
7558            let inner = &type_str[prefix_lower.len()..type_str.len() - 1];
7559            if inner.is_empty() {
7560                return Err(Error::schema(format!(
7561                    "Empty {} element type: {}",
7562                    collection, type_str
7563                )));
7564            }
7565            return Ok(inner.to_string());
7566        }
7567
7568        Err(Error::schema(format!(
7569            "Invalid {} type format: {}",
7570            collection, type_str
7571        )))
7572    }
7573
7574    /// Extract key and value types from map<K,V> type string (CQL or Cassandra internal format)
7575    fn extract_map_types(&self, type_str: &str) -> Result<(String, String)> {
7576        let type_lower = type_str.to_lowercase();
7577
7578        // Determine the inner content based on format
7579        let inner = if type_lower.starts_with("org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.maptype(")
7580            && type_str.ends_with(')')
7581        {
7582            // Cassandra internal format: org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.MapType(K,V)
7583            let prefix = "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.MapType(";
7584            &type_str[prefix.len()..type_str.len() - 1]
7585        } else if type_lower.starts_with("map<") && type_str.ends_with('>') {
7586            // CQL format: map<K,V>
7587            &type_str[4..type_str.len() - 1]
7588        } else {
7589            return Err(Error::schema(format!(
7590                "Invalid map type format: {}",
7591                type_str
7592            )));
7593        };
7594
7595        if inner.is_empty() {
7596            return Err(Error::schema(format!("Empty map types: {}", type_str)));
7597        }
7598
7599        // Split by comma, handling nested angle brackets and parentheses
7600        let mut depth = 0;
7601        let mut split_pos = None;
7602
7603        for (i, ch) in inner.chars().enumerate() {
7604            match ch {
7605                '<' | '(' => depth += 1,
7606                '>' | ')' => depth -= 1,
7607                ',' if depth == 0 => {
7608                    split_pos = Some(i);
7609                    break;
7610                }
7611                _ => {}
7612            }
7613        }
7614
7615        let split_pos = split_pos.ok_or_else(|| {
7616            Error::schema(format!(
7617                "Invalid map type format (no comma separator): {}",
7618                type_str
7619            ))
7620        })?;
7621
7622        let key_type = inner[..split_pos].trim().to_string();
7623        let value_type = inner[split_pos + 1..].trim().to_string();
7624
7625        if key_type.is_empty() || value_type.is_empty() {
7626            return Err(Error::schema(format!(
7627                "Empty key or value type in map: {}",
7628                type_str
7629            )));
7630        }
7631
7632        Ok((key_type, value_type))
7633    }
7634
7635    /// Parse a value from a complete, bounded byte slice.
7636    ///
7637    /// This is used when the outer Cassandra collection format already provides
7638    /// explicit `[i32 BE len][raw bytes]` boundaries and we have extracted exactly
7639    /// the bytes that constitute the value. The entire `data` slice IS the value.
7640    ///
7641    /// - Variable-width types (text, blob, varint, decimal, inet): consume the full slice
7642    /// - Fixed-width types (int, bigint, uuid, etc.): read from offset 0
7643    /// - Nested collections: use the bounded sub-format `[i32 BE count][i32 BE len][bytes]...`
7644    fn parse_value_from_raw_bytes(
7645        &self,
7646        data: &[u8],
7647        type_str: &str,
7648        column_name: &str,
7649        depth: usize,
7650    ) -> Result<Value> {
7651        if depth > MAX_TYPE_NESTING_DEPTH {
7652            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7653                "Frozen element '{}': recursion depth {} exceeds maximum {}",
7654                column_name, depth, MAX_TYPE_NESTING_DEPTH
7655            )));
7656        }
7657        let normalized_type = type_str.to_lowercase();
7658        match normalized_type.as_str() {
7659            "text"
7660            | "varchar"
7661            | "ascii"
7662            | "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.utf8type"
7663            | "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.asciitype"
7664            | "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.varchartype" => {
7665                let text = String::from_utf8(data.to_vec()).map_err(|e| {
7666                    Error::corruption(format!(
7667                        "Frozen element '{}': invalid UTF-8 in text value: {}",
7668                        column_name, e
7669                    ))
7670                })?;
7671                Ok(Value::Text(text))
7672            }
7673            "blob" | "bytes" => Ok(Value::Blob(data.to_vec())),
7674            "int" => {
7675                if data.len() < 4 {
7676                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7677                        "Frozen element '{}': need 4 bytes for int, got {}",
7678                        column_name,
7679                        data.len()
7680                    )));
7681                }
7682                Ok(Value::Integer(i32::from_be_bytes([
7683                    data[0], data[1], data[2], data[3],
7684                ])))
7685            }
7686            "bigint" | "counter" => {
7687                if data.len() < 8 {
7688                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7689                        "Frozen element '{}': need 8 bytes for bigint, got {}",
7690                        column_name,
7691                        data.len()
7692                    )));
7693                }
7694                Ok(Value::BigInt(i64::from_be_bytes([
7695                    data[0], data[1], data[2], data[3], data[4], data[5], data[6], data[7],
7696                ])))
7697            }
7698            "boolean" => {
7699                if data.is_empty() {
7700                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7701                        "Frozen element '{}': need 1 byte for boolean",
7702                        column_name
7703                    )));
7704                }
7705                Ok(Value::Boolean(data[0] != 0))
7706            }
7707            "uuid" | "timeuuid" => {
7708                if data.len() < 16 {
7709                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7710                        "Frozen element '{}': need 16 bytes for UUID, got {}",
7711                        column_name,
7712                        data.len()
7713                    )));
7714                }
7715                let uuid: [u8; 16] = data[..16]
7716                    .try_into()
7717                    .map_err(|_| Error::corruption("UUID byte conversion failed"))?;
7718                Ok(Value::Uuid(uuid))
7719            }
7720            "float" => {
7721                if data.len() < 4 {
7722                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7723                        "Frozen element '{}': need 4 bytes for float, got {}",
7724                        column_name,
7725                        data.len()
7726                    )));
7727                }
7728                let f = f32::from_be_bytes([data[0], data[1], data[2], data[3]]);
7729                Ok(Value::Float(f as f64))
7730            }
7731            "double" => {
7732                if data.len() < 8 {
7733                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7734                        "Frozen element '{}': need 8 bytes for double, got {}",
7735                        column_name,
7736                        data.len()
7737                    )));
7738                }
7739                Ok(Value::Float(f64::from_be_bytes([
7740                    data[0], data[1], data[2], data[3], data[4], data[5], data[6], data[7],
7741                ])))
7742            }
7743            "smallint" | "short" => {
7744                if data.len() < 2 {
7745                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7746                        "Frozen element '{}': need 2 bytes for smallint, got {}",
7747                        column_name,
7748                        data.len()
7749                    )));
7750                }
7751                Ok(Value::SmallInt(i16::from_be_bytes([data[0], data[1]])))
7752            }
7753            "tinyint" | "byte" => {
7754                if data.is_empty() {
7755                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7756                        "Frozen element '{}': need 1 byte for tinyint",
7757                        column_name
7758                    )));
7759                }
7760                Ok(Value::TinyInt(data[0] as i8))
7761            }
7762            "timestamp" => {
7763                if data.len() < 8 {
7764                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7765                        "Frozen element '{}': need 8 bytes for timestamp, got {}",
7766                        column_name,
7767                        data.len()
7768                    )));
7769                }
7770                Ok(Value::Timestamp(i64::from_be_bytes([
7771                    data[0], data[1], data[2], data[3], data[4], data[5], data[6], data[7],
7772                ])))
7773            }
7774            "date" => {
7775                if data.len() < 4 {
7776                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7777                        "Frozen element '{}': need 4 bytes for date, got {}",
7778                        column_name,
7779                        data.len()
7780                    )));
7781                }
7782                let stored = u32::from_be_bytes([data[0], data[1], data[2], data[3]]);
7783                let days_since_epoch = stored.wrapping_add(i32::MIN as u32) as i32;
7784                Ok(Value::Date(days_since_epoch))
7785            }
7786            "time" => {
7787                if data.len() < 8 {
7788                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7789                        "Frozen element '{}': need 8 bytes for time, got {}",
7790                        column_name,
7791                        data.len()
7792                    )));
7793                }
7794                Ok(Value::Time(i64::from_be_bytes([
7795                    data[0], data[1], data[2], data[3], data[4], data[5], data[6], data[7],
7796                ])))
7797            }
7798            "varint" => Ok(Value::Varint(data.to_vec())),
7799            "decimal" => {
7800                if data.len() < 4 {
7801                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7802                        "Frozen element '{}': decimal too short ({} bytes)",
7803                        column_name,
7804                        data.len()
7805                    )));
7806                }
7807                let scale = i32::from_be_bytes([data[0], data[1], data[2], data[3]]);
7808                let unscaled = data[4..].to_vec();
7809                Ok(Value::Decimal { scale, unscaled })
7810            }
7811            "inet" => Ok(Value::Inet(data.to_vec())),
7812            // Nested list/set/map inside a bounded element (e.g. map<text, list<int>>)
7813            type_str if type_str.starts_with("list<") => {
7814                let element_type = self.extract_collection_element_type(type_str, "list")?;
7815                let (val, _) = self.parse_frozen_list_value_raw(
7816                    data,
7817                    0,
7818                    &element_type,
7819                    column_name,
7820                    depth + 1,
7821                )?;
7822                Ok(val)
7823            }
7824            type_str if type_str.starts_with("set<") => {
7825                let element_type = self.extract_collection_element_type(type_str, "set")?;
7826                let (val, _) = self.parse_frozen_set_value_raw(
7827                    data,
7828                    0,
7829                    &element_type,
7830                    column_name,
7831                    depth + 1,
7832                )?;
7833                Ok(val)
7834            }
7835            type_str if type_str.starts_with("map<") => {
7836                let (key_type, value_type) = self.extract_map_types(type_str)?;
7837                let (val, _) = self.parse_frozen_map_value_raw(
7838                    data,
7839                    0,
7840                    &key_type,
7841                    &value_type,
7842                    column_name,
7843                    depth + 1,
7844                )?;
7845                Ok(val)
7846            }
7847            // Nested tuple inside a frozen collection element.
7848            // The caller (read_frozen_element) has already extracted the raw element bytes
7849            // into `data`, so there is no outer VUInt length here — just the sequence of
7850            // [i32 BE len][bytes] fields as written by serialize_value for Value::Tuple.
7851            type_str if type_str.starts_with("tuple<") => {
7852                let element_types = self.extract_tuple_element_types(type_str)?;
7853                if element_types.is_empty() {
7854                    return Err(Error::schema(format!(
7855                        "Nested tuple element '{}': empty tuple type",
7856                        column_name
7857                    )));
7858                }
7859                let mut off = 0usize;
7860                let blob_end = data.len();
7861                let elements = self.parse_tuple_elements_raw(
7862                    data,
7863                    &mut off,
7864                    blob_end,
7865                    &element_types,
7866                    column_name,
7867                    depth + 1,
7868                )?;
7869                Ok(Value::Tuple(elements))
7870            }
7871            type_str if type_str.starts_with("frozen<") => {
7872                let inner_type = self.extract_frozen_inner_type(type_str)?;
7873                let inner =
7874                    self.parse_value_from_raw_bytes(data, &inner_type, column_name, depth + 1)?;
7875                Ok(Value::Frozen(Box::new(inner)))
7876            }
7877            // UDT (User-Defined Type): delegate to parse_raw_type_value which has the full
7878            // UDT parsing logic including field count validation and nested type resolution.
7879            // The raw bytes representation is identical between the two function conventions.
7880            other if Self::is_udt_type(other) => {
7881                let (val, _offset) =
7882                    self.parse_raw_type_value(data, 0, type_str, column_name, depth)?;
7883                Ok(val)
7884            }
7885            other => {
7886                // Check if it's a short UDT name in the registry (e.g., "address_type").
7887                // This handles the case where parse_value_from_raw_bytes is called recursively
7888                // from the frozen<> arm with the stripped inner type (e.g., frozen<address_type>
7889                // → "address_type"). Since parse_raw_type_value already has a registry-lookup
7890                // fallback that correctly handles bare UDT names, we delegate there.
7891                // The byte-level encoding is identical: UDT fields use 4-byte i32 length prefixes
7892                // with no overall cell-level length prefix, so parse_raw_type_value offset=0 is
7893                // correct for already-extracted cell value bytes.
7894                // See Issue #481 regression fix.
7895                if let Some(ref registry) = self.udt_registry {
7896                    if registry.get_udt(&self.keyspace, other).is_some() {
7897                        log::debug!(
7898                            "parse_value_from_raw_bytes: type '{}' for '{}' resolved as UDT via registry, delegating to parse_raw_type_value",
7899                            other,
7900                            column_name,
7901                        );
7902                        let (val, _offset) =
7903                            self.parse_raw_type_value(data, 0, type_str, column_name, depth)?;
7904                        return Ok(val);
7905                    }
7906                }
7907                // Truly unknown type: fall back to blob.
7908                log::debug!(
7909                    "parse_value_from_raw_bytes: unknown type '{}' for '{}', treating as blob ({} bytes)",
7910                    other,
7911                    column_name,
7912                    data.len()
7913                );
7914                Ok(Value::Blob(data.to_vec()))
7915            }
7916        }
7917    }
7918
7919    /// Parse a raw type value WITHOUT cell flags (for frozen collection elements)
7920    ///
7921    /// Unlike `parse_cell_value_schema_order`, this function does NOT expect cell flags
7922    /// or timestamps at the start of the data. Frozen collection elements are stored
7923    /// as raw type values directly:
7924    /// - Fixed-width types (int, uuid, bigint, float, double): direct bytes, no length prefix
7925    /// - Variable-width types (text, blob): VInt length prefix + bytes
7926    ///
7927    /// This is the correct format for elements inside frozen collections:
7928    /// frozen<list<int>> -> [VInt count][int1][int2]...  (each int is 4 bytes, no flags)
7929    /// frozen<map<text, text>> -> [VInt count][VInt key_len][key][VInt val_len][val]...
7930    fn parse_raw_type_value(
7931        &self,
7932        data: &[u8],
7933        mut offset: usize,
7934        type_str: &str,
7935        column_name: &str,
7936        depth: usize,
7937    ) -> Result<(Value, usize)> {
7938        if depth > MAX_TYPE_NESTING_DEPTH {
7939            return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7940                "Frozen element '{}': recursion depth {} exceeds maximum {}",
7941                column_name, depth, MAX_TYPE_NESTING_DEPTH
7942            )));
7943        }
7944        // Normalize type name for case-insensitive matching
7945        let normalized_type = type_str.to_lowercase();
7946
7947        let value = match normalized_type.as_str() {
7948            // Cassandra internal type names (full package paths)
7949            "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.utf8type"
7950            | "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.asciitype"
7951            | "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.varchartype" => {
7952                // Text: [VInt len][text bytes]
7953                let (remaining, text_len) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
7954                    Error::corruption(format!(
7955                        "Frozen element '{}': failed to parse text length as VInt: {:?}",
7956                        column_name, e
7957                    ))
7958                })?;
7959                let text_len = text_len as usize;
7960                let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
7961                offset += bytes_consumed;
7962
7963                if offset + text_len > data.len() {
7964                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7965                        "Frozen element '{}': need {} bytes for text, only {} available",
7966                        column_name,
7967                        text_len,
7968                        data.len() - offset
7969                    )));
7970                }
7971
7972                let text_bytes = &data[offset..offset + text_len];
7973                let text = String::from_utf8(text_bytes.to_vec())
7974                    .map_err(|e| Error::corruption(format!("Invalid UTF-8 in text: {}", e)))?;
7975                offset += text_len;
7976                Value::Text(text)
7977            }
7978
7979            "boolean" => {
7980                // Boolean: 1 byte
7981                if offset >= data.len() {
7982                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7983                        "Frozen element '{}': unexpected end at boolean value",
7984                        column_name
7985                    )));
7986                }
7987                let bool_byte = data[offset];
7988                offset += 1;
7989                Value::Boolean(bool_byte != 0)
7990            }
7991
7992            "int" => {
7993                // Integer (i32): fixed-width 4 bytes
7994                if offset + 4 > data.len() {
7995                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
7996                        "Frozen element '{}': need 4 bytes for int, only {} available",
7997                        column_name,
7998                        data.len() - offset
7999                    )));
8000                }
8001                let int_val = i32::from_be_bytes([
8002                    data[offset],
8003                    data[offset + 1],
8004                    data[offset + 2],
8005                    data[offset + 3],
8006                ]);
8007                offset += 4;
8008                Value::Integer(int_val)
8009            }
8010
8011            "text" | "varchar" | "ascii" => {
8012                // Text: [VInt len][text bytes]
8013                let (remaining, text_len) = parse_vuint(&data[offset..]).map_err(|e| {
8014                    Error::corruption(format!(
8015                        "Frozen element '{}': failed to parse text length as VInt: {:?}",
8016                        column_name, e
8017                    ))
8018                })?;
8019                let text_len = text_len as usize;
8020                let bytes_consumed = data[offset..].len() - remaining.len();
8021                offset += bytes_consumed;
8022
8023                if offset + text_len > data.len() {
8024                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
8025                        "Frozen element '{}': need {} bytes for text, only {} available",
8026                        column_name,
8027                        text_len,
8028                        data.len() - offset
8029                    )));
8030                }
8031
8032                let text_bytes = &data[offset..offset + text_len];
8033                let text = String::from_utf8(text_bytes.to_vec()).map_err(|e| {
8034                    Error::corruption(format!(
8035                        "Frozen element '{}': invalid UTF-8 in text value: {}",
8036                        column_name, e
8037                    ))
8038                })?;
8039
8040                offset += text_len;
8041                Value::Text(text)
8042            }
8043
8044            "uuid" | "timeuuid" => {
8045                // UUID/TimeUUID: fixed-width 16 bytes
8046                if offset + 16 > data.len() {
8047                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
8048                        "Frozen element '{}': need 16 bytes for UUID, only {} available",
8049                        column_name,
8050                        data.len() - offset
8051                    )));
8052                }
8053
8054                let uuid_bytes: [u8; 16] = data[offset..offset + 16]
8055                    .try_into()
8056                    .map_err(|_| Error::corruption("UUID byte conversion failed"))?;
8057
8058                offset += 16;
8059                Value::Uuid(uuid_bytes)
8060            }
8061
8062            "bigint" | "counter" => {
8063                // BigInt/Counter: fixed-width 8 bytes
8064                if offset + 8 > data.len() {
8065                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
8066                        "Frozen element '{}': need 8 bytes for bigint, only {} available",
8067                        column_name,
8068                        data.len() - offset
8069                    )));
8070                }
8071                let val = i64::from_be_bytes([
8072                    data[offset],
8073                    data[offset + 1],
8074                    data[offset + 2],
8075                    data[offset + 3],
8076                    data[offset + 4],
8077                    data[offset + 5],
8078                    data[offset + 6],
8079                    data[offset + 7],
8080                ]);
8081                offset += 8;
8082                Value::BigInt(val)
8083            }
8084
8085            "float" => {
8086                // Float: 4 bytes
8087                if offset + 4 > data.len() {
8088                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
8089                        "Frozen element '{}': need 4 bytes for float, only {} available",
8090                        column_name,
8091                        data.len() - offset
8092                    )));
8093                }
8094
8095                let val = f32::from_be_bytes([
8096                    data[offset],
8097                    data[offset + 1],
8098                    data[offset + 2],
8099                    data[offset + 3],
8100                ]);
8101                offset += 4;
8102                Value::Float(val as f64)
8103            }
8104
8105            "double" => {
8106                // Double: 8 bytes
8107                if offset + 8 > data.len() {
8108                    return Err(Error::corruption(format!(
8109                        "Frozen element '{}': need 8 bytes for double, only {} available",
8110                        column_name,
8111                        data.len() - offset
8112                    )));
8113                }
8114                let val = f64::from_be_bytes([
8115                    data[offset],
8116                    data[offset + 1],
8117                    data[offset + 2],
8118                    data[offset + 3],
8119                    data[offset + 4],
8120                    data[offset + 5],
8121                    data[offset + 6],
8122                    data[offset + 7],
8123                ]);
8124                offset += 8;
8125                Value::Float(val) // Note: Value::Float holds f64 for both float and double
8126            }
8127
8128            "timestamp" => {
