11650    /// C2: markedForDeleteAt delta (HAS_DELETION) must use unsigned VInt.
11651    ///
11652    /// Row bytes (HAS_DELETION | HAS_ALL_COLUMNS = 0x30):
11653    ///   [0x30][row_size=0x00][prev_size=0x00][unsigned_vint(mfda_delta)][unsigned_vint(ldt_delta)]
11654    ///
11655    /// CURRENT behavior (ZigZag bug): mfda decoded as 500 instead of 1000
11656    /// CORRECT behavior: mfda = 1_001_000
11657    #[test]
11658    fn s1_c2_marked_for_delete_at_cassandra_unsigned_encoding_must_decode_correctly() {
11659        let min_timestamp = 1_000_000i64;

11663
11664        let mut mfda_bytes = Vec::new();

11668

11670        data.push(0x30u8); // HAS_DELETION (0x10) | HAS_ALL_COLUMNS (0x20)
11671        data.push(0x00u8); // row_size
11672        data.push(0x00u8); // prev_size
11673        data.extend_from_slice(&mfda_bytes);
11674        data.extend_from_slice(&ldt_bytes);
11675
11676        let parser = V5CompressedLegacyParser::new(

11688        assert_eq!(

11695            expected_mfda,

11702
11703    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
11704    // C3: HAS_TTL (0x08) implies TWO fields: [ttl: VInt32] + [liveness_ldt: VInt32]
11705    //
11706    // Cassandra UnfilteredSerializer.java:225-228:
11707    //   if ((flags & HAS_TTL) != 0) {
11708    //       header.writeTTL(pkLiveness.ttl(), out);                         // VInt32
11709    //       header.writeLocalDeletionTime(pkLiveness.localExpirationTime(), out); // VInt32
11710    //   }
11711    //
11712    // BUG: parse_row_metadata reads only ONE VInt (TTL), skips the LDT VInt.
11713    // This causes misalignment of all subsequent fields in TTL rows.
11714    //
11715    // Verdict: BUG — header_size must cover both VInts.
11716    // Bug issue: see child issues filed for #623.
11717    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
11718
11719    /// C3: Row with HAS_TTL must consume BOTH TTL and LDT VInts from the stream.
11720    ///
11721    /// Row bytes (HAS_TTL | HAS_ALL_COLUMNS = 0x28, no timestamp):
11722    ///   [flags=0x28][row_size=0x00][prev_size=0x00][ttl_delta=0x64][ldt_delta=0x32]
11723    ///   ^--- ttl=100 (1 byte, <128)                                 ^--- ldt=50 (1 byte, <128)
11724    ///
11725    /// parse_row_metadata starts at pos=flags_size=1 (flags already consumed):
11726    ///   row_size(1) + prev_size(1) + ttl(1) + ldt(1) = 4 bytes consumed after flags
11727    ///   header_size = pos_end - flags_size = 5 - 1 = 4
11728    ///
11729    /// PREVIOUS (bug): header_size = 3 — LDT byte not consumed, misaligning later fields.
11730    /// CORRECT after fix: header_size = 4 — both TTL and LDT consumed.
11731    ///
11732    /// Uses single-byte values (< 128) so encode_unsigned produces 1 byte each.
11733    #[test]
11734    fn s1_c3_has_ttl_reads_two_vint_fields_ttl_and_ldt() {
11735        let ttl_delta: u64 = 100; // 1 byte: 0x64 (100 < 128)
11736        let ldt_delta: u64 = 50; // 1 byte: 0x32 (50 < 128)
11737
11738        let mut ttl_bytes = Vec::new();
11739        encode_unsigned(ttl_delta, &mut ttl_bytes); // [0x64]
11740        assert_eq!(ttl_bytes.len(), 1, "ttl_delta=100 must encode to 1 byte");
11741        let mut ldt_bytes = Vec::new();
11742        encode_unsigned(ldt_delta, &mut ldt_bytes); // [0x32]
11743        assert_eq!(ldt_bytes.len(), 1, "ldt_delta=50 must encode to 1 byte");
11744
11745        let mut data = Vec::new();
11746        data.push(0x28u8); // HAS_TTL (0x08) | HAS_ALL_COLUMNS (0x20)
11747        data.push(0x00u8); // row_size VInt = 0
11748        data.push(0x00u8); // prev_size VInt = 0
11749        data.extend_from_slice(&ttl_bytes); // TTL delta (1 byte = 0x64)
11750        data.extend_from_slice(&ldt_bytes); // LDT delta (1 byte = 0x32) — fix: must now be read
11751        data.push(0xFFu8); // sentinel — must NOT be consumed by metadata parsing
11752
11753        let parser = V5CompressedLegacyParser::new(
11754            "ks".to_string(),
11755            "tbl".to_string(),
11756            0,
11757            1_600_000_000,
11758            Some(3600),
11759        );
11760        let (row_flags, ext_flags, flags_size) = parser.parse_row_flags(&data, 0).unwrap();
11761        assert_eq!(flags_size, 1);
11762
11763        let result = parser.parse_row_metadata(&data, flags_size, row_flags, ext_flags);
11764        assert!(
11765            result.is_ok(),
11766            "parse_row_metadata must succeed for HAS_TTL row"
11767        );
11768        let (row_header, _row_size) = result.unwrap();
11769
11770        // TTL must decode correctly
11771        let expected_ttl = (3600i64 + ttl_delta as i64) as i32;
11772        assert_eq!(
11773            row_header.ttl,
11774            Some(expected_ttl),
11775            "TTL delta must decode correctly"
11776        );
11777
11778        // header_size must include BOTH TTL (1) and LDT (1) bytes plus row_size(1) + prev_size(1) = 4
11779        // Explanation: parse_row_metadata starts at pos=flags_size=1; after consuming
11780        //   row_size(1), prev_size(1), ttl(1), ldt(1) → pos=5; header_size = 5-1 = 4.
11781        // Before fix: header_size was 3 (ldt not consumed).
11782        assert_eq!(
11783            row_header.header_size, 4,
11784            "HAS_TTL row_header.header_size must be 4 (row_size + prev_size + ttl + ldt).\n\
11785             Got {} — if 3, the LDT VInt after TTL was NOT consumed (C3 bug present)",
11786            row_header.header_size
11787        );
11788    }
11789
11790    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
11791    // C4: Partition header format — u16 BE key_len + key + DeletionTime
11792    //
11793    // Cassandra SortedTablePartitionWriter.java:104-105:
11794    //   ByteBufferUtil.writeWithShortLength(key) → [u16 BE key_len][key_bytes]
11795    //   then DeletionTime serialized.
11796    //
11797    // V5CompressedLegacyParser.parse_partition_header() uses [u8 flags][u8 key_len]
11798    // which is the legacy compressed block format — intentionally different from the
11799    // modern Cassandra BigFormat. The data_writer.rs correctly uses u16 BE key_len.
11800    //
11801    // Verdict: CORRECT (writer uses Cassandra-canonical u16 BE key length).
11802    //          V5CompressedLegacy reader uses legacy format by design.
11803    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
11804
11805    /// C4: Verify partition key length in data_writer uses u16 BE (Cassandra-canonical).
11806    /// Tests existing data_writer unit test vectors to confirm the format.
11807    ///
11808    /// data_writer.rs write_partition_header():
11809    ///   self.buffer.write_all(&(key.key.len() as u16).to_be_bytes())
11810    ///
11811    /// The existing test at line ~2664 in data_writer.rs already verifies:
11812    ///   assert_eq!(&bytes[0..2], &[0x00, 0x04])  // key length 4 as u16 BE
11813    ///
11814    /// This test documents C4 as CORRECT by verifying the legacy reader format:
11815    /// [u8 flags=0x00][u8 key_len][key_bytes][i32 del_time][u64 unknown] = 30 bytes for UUID.
11816    #[test]
11817    fn s1_c4_v5_legacy_reader_partition_header_format_documented() {
11818        // The V5CompressedLegacy format uses [u8 flags][u8 key_len] — legacy design.
11819        // This test documents and validates the legacy format is handled consistently.
11820        //
11821        // Real Cassandra SSTable partition header hex from test_basic/simple_table:
11822        //   00 10 15291a77d7394e738397b787442f3a1f 7fffffff 8000000000000000
11823        //   ^flags ^len  ^16-byte UUID                  ^i32 del  ^u64 unknown
11824        let hex_str = "001015291a77d7394e738397b787442f3a1f7fffffff8000000000000000";
11825        let data = hex::decode(hex_str).unwrap();
11826
11827        let parser = V5CompressedLegacyParser::new(
11828            "test_basic".to_string(),
11829            "simple_table".to_string(),
11830            0,
11831            0,
11832            None,
11833        );
11834        let (row_key, offset) = parser.parse_partition_header(&data, 0).unwrap();
11835        assert_eq!(row_key.0.len(), 16, "UUID partition key must be 16 bytes");
11836        // Total: 1 (flags) + 1 (len) + 16 (UUID) + 4 (del_time) + 8 (unknown) = 30
11837        assert_eq!(
11838            offset, 30,
11839            "Legacy partition header must consume 30 bytes for UUID key"
11840        );
11841
11842        // For contrast: the writer (data_writer.rs) uses u16 BE key length (Cassandra-canonical).
11843        // That format is: [u16 key_len][key_bytes][DeletionTime].
11844        // The legacy reader and the writer serve different format variants.
11845        // Both are intentional and consistent with their respective format specs.
11846    }

11848    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
11849    // C5: Missing-columns bitmap — bit=1 means MISSING (Cassandra convention)
11850    //
11851    // Cassandra Columns.java:519-530:
11852    //   For superset < 64 cols: single unsigned VInt where bit=1 = column ABSENT
11853    //   For superset >= 64 cols: delta + column indices
11854    //
11855    // CQLite parse_row_metadata() uses parse_vuint and comment says "bit=1 means missing".
11856    //
11857    // Verdict: CORRECT_BUT_UNTESTED → now tested.
11858    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
11859
11860    /// C5-a: NOT HAS_ALL_COLUMNS → bitmap present; bit=1 means column MISSING.
11861    ///
11862    /// Row: HAS_TIMESTAMP (0x04) only (NOT HAS_ALL_COLUMNS).
11863    /// bitmap = 0x05 = 0b00000101: columns 0 and 2 absent, column 1 present.
11864    #[test]
11865    fn s1_c5_missing_columns_bitmap_bit1_means_absent() {
11866        let ts_delta: u64 = 0;
11867        let bitmap: u64 = 0x05; // cols 0 and 2 missing
11868
11869        let mut ts_bytes = Vec::new();
11870        encode_unsigned(ts_delta, &mut ts_bytes);
11871        let mut bm_bytes = Vec::new();
11872        encode_unsigned(bitmap, &mut bm_bytes);
11873
11874        let mut data = Vec::new();
11875        data.push(0x04u8); // HAS_TIMESTAMP only (no HAS_ALL_COLUMNS)
11876        data.push(0x00u8); // row_size = 0
11877        data.push(0x00u8); // prev_size = 0
11878        data.extend_from_slice(&ts_bytes);
11879        data.extend_from_slice(&bm_bytes);
11880
11881        let parser =
11882            V5CompressedLegacyParser::new("ks".to_string(), "tbl".to_string(), 1_000_000, 0, None);
11883        let (row_flags, ext_flags, flags_size) = parser.parse_row_flags(&data, 0).unwrap();
11884        let (row_header, _) = parser
11885            .parse_row_metadata(&data, flags_size, row_flags, ext_flags)
11886            .unwrap();
11887
11888        assert_eq!(
11889            row_header.missing_columns_bitmap,
11890            Some(0x05),
11891            "Missing columns bitmap must be 0x05"
11892        );
11893
11894        let bm = row_header.missing_columns_bitmap.unwrap();
11895        // Cassandra bit=1 means column ABSENT:
11896        assert_ne!(bm & (1 << 0), 0, "Column 0 must be MISSING (bit 0 set)");
11897        assert_eq!(bm & (1 << 1), 0, "Column 1 must be PRESENT (bit 1 clear)");
11898        assert_ne!(bm & (1 << 2), 0, "Column 2 must be MISSING (bit 2 set)");
11899    }
11900
11901    /// C5-b: HAS_ALL_COLUMNS (0x20) → no bitmap field → None.
11902    #[test]
11903    fn s1_c5_has_all_columns_no_bitmap() {
11904        let data = vec![0x20u8, 0x00u8, 0x00u8]; // HAS_ALL_COLUMNS only, row_size=0, prev_size=0
11905
11906        let parser = V5CompressedLegacyParser::new("ks".to_string(), "tbl".to_string(), 0, 0, None);
11907        let (row_flags, ext_flags, flags_size) = parser.parse_row_flags(&data, 0).unwrap();
11908        let (row_header, _) = parser
11909            .parse_row_metadata(&data, flags_size, row_flags, ext_flags)
11910            .unwrap();
11911
11912        assert_eq!(
11913            row_header.missing_columns_bitmap, None,
11914            "HAS_ALL_COLUMNS must not read a bitmap"
11915        );
11916    }

11918    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
11919    // VInt correctness: unsigned VInt vs ZigZag encoding test vectors
11920    // -------------------------------------------------------------------------
11921
11922    /// VInt-a: Cassandra unsigned VInt (writeUnsignedVInt) encoding test vectors.
11923    /// Verified against Cassandra VIntCoding.java algorithm and facts-B1.md §VInt.
11924    #[test]
11925    fn s1_vint_unsigned_encoding_test_vectors() {
11926        use crate::parser::vint::parse_vuint;
11927
11928        let test_cases: &[(u64, &[u8])] = &[
11929            (0, &[0x00]),                 // single byte 0
11930            (1, &[0x01]),                 // single byte 1
11931            (127, &[0x7F]),               // max single byte
11932            (128, &[0x80, 0x80]),         // min 2-byte
11933            (1000, &[0x83, 0xE8]),        // 2-byte: 10_000011 11101000
11934            (5000, &[0x93, 0x88]),        // audit report-B1 finding #30: unsigned(5000) = 0x93 0x88
11935            (7200, &[0x9C, 0x20]),        // audit report-B1 finding #31: unsigned(7200) = 0x9C 0x20
11936            (16383, &[0xBF, 0xFF]),       // max 2-byte
11937            (16384, &[0xC0, 0x40, 0x00]), // min 3-byte
11938        ];
11939
11940        for (value, expected) in test_cases {
11941            let mut buf = Vec::new();
11942            encode_unsigned(*value, &mut buf);
11943            assert_eq!(
11944                buf.as_slice(),
11945                *expected,
11946                "encode_unsigned({}) = {:?}, expected {:?}",
11947                value,
11948                buf,
11949                expected
11950            );
11951
11952            let (rem, decoded) = parse_vuint(&buf).unwrap();
11953            assert!(
11954                rem.is_empty(),
11955                "parse_vuint must consume all bytes for {}",
11956                value
11957            );
11958            assert_eq!(decoded, *value, "round-trip failed for {}", value);
11959        }
11960    }

11962    /// VInt-b: ZigZag encoding test vectors (used only for signed fields, NOT for SSTable temporal fields).
11963    /// Facts-B1.md confirms: ZigZag is used only in on-wire messaging, not SSTable row serialization.
11964    #[test]
11965    fn s1_vint_zigzag_encoding_test_vectors() {
11966        use crate::parser::vint::{zigzag_decode, zigzag_encode};
11967
11968        let test_cases: &[(i64, u64)] = &[
11969            (0, 0),
11970            (-1, 1),
11971            (1, 2),
11972            (-2, 3),
11973            (2, 4),
11974            (63, 126),
11975            (-64, 127),
11976            (64, 128),
11977        ];
11978        for (signed, unsigned) in test_cases {
11979            assert_eq!(
11980                zigzag_encode(*signed),
11981                *unsigned,
11982                "zigzag_encode({})",
11983                signed
11984            );
11985            assert_eq!(
11986                zigzag_decode(*unsigned),
11987                *signed,
11988                "zigzag_decode({})",
11989                unsigned
11990            );
11991        }
11992    }

11994    // =========================================================================
11995    // DS4 (Issue #700) / roborev Finding 3 — byte-level collection tombstone test
11996    //
11997    // The `has_collection_tombstone` decode path
11998    //   `absolute_mfda = min_timestamp.wrapping_add(mfda_delta)`
11999    //   `has_collection_tombstone = absolute_mfda != i64::MIN`
12000    // was previously exercised only by e2e tests that cover the append (no-tombstone)
12001    // path.  This unit test drives `parse_complex_column_inner` with
12002    // `has_complex_deletion = true` and a non-sentinel `markedForDeleteAt` value,
12003    // confirming that `ComplexColumnMeta.has_collection_tombstone == true` is set
12004    // purely from the byte-level decode without needing a full SSTableReader.
12005    // =========================================================================
12006
12007    /// Byte-level test: `parse_complex_column_inner` with `has_complex_deletion = true`
12008    /// and a real `markedForDeleteAt` timestamp (not the i64::MIN sentinel) must set
12009    /// `ComplexColumnMeta.has_collection_tombstone = true`.
12010    ///
12011    /// Wire layout (min_timestamp = 0; complex-deletion deltas are UNSIGNED
12012    /// VInts per the writer, roborev #863):
12013    ///   [mfda_delta: VUInt(2) = 0x02]  → absolute_mfda = 0 + 2 = 2 ≠ i64::MIN
12014    ///   [localDeletionTime: VUInt(0) = 0x00]
12015    ///   [cell_count: VUInt(0) = 0x00]  ← zero cells for simplicity
12016    ///
12017    /// The parser uses `min_timestamp = 0` (default from `V5CompressedLegacyParser::new`).
12018    #[test]
12019    fn ds4_finding3_has_complex_deletion_sets_collection_tombstone() {
12020        let parser =
12021            V5CompressedLegacyParser::new("test".to_string(), "table".to_string(), 0, 0, None);
12022        let column = crate::schema::Column {
12023            name: "tags".to_string(),
12024            data_type: "set<text>".to_string(),
12025            nullable: true,
12026            default: None,
12027            is_static: false,
12028        };
12029
12030        // Wire bytes (unsigned-VInt complex-deletion deltas, roborev #863):
12031        //   0x02 = VUInt(2), mfda_delta=2; absolute_mfda = 0+2 = 2 ≠ i64::MIN
12032        //   0x00 = VUInt(0), localDeletionTime delta = 0
12033        //   0x00 = VUInt(0), cell_count = 0 (empty collection after overwrite)
12034        let blob: Vec<u8> = vec![0x02, 0x00, 0x00];
12035
12036        let (value, consumed, meta) = parser
12037            .parse_complex_column_inner(
12038                &blob, 0, &column, true, /* has_complex_deletion */
12039                0, None,
12040            )
12041            .expect("parse_complex_column_inner must succeed for collection tombstone");
12042
12043        assert_eq!(consumed, blob.len(), "all bytes must be consumed");
12044        // A SET overwrite produces an empty set (collection tombstone + 0 new elements).
12045        assert_eq!(
12046            value,
12047            Value::Set(vec![]),
12048            "overwritten collection with 0 elements must be an empty Set"
12049        );
12050        // THE KEY ASSERTION: has_collection_tombstone must be true.
12051        assert!(
12052            meta.has_collection_tombstone,
12053            "has_complex_deletion=true with absolute_mfda=1 (!=i64::MIN) must set \
12054             has_collection_tombstone=true (roborev Finding 3)"
12055        );
12056        // No element tombstones in the 0-cell body.
12057        assert_eq!(
12058            meta.element_tombstone_count, 0,
12059            "empty post-overwrite collection must have no element tombstones"
12060        );
12061        // No element writetimes when there are no cells.
12062        assert_eq!(
12063            meta.max_element_writetime, 0,
12064            "empty collection must have max_element_writetime=0"
12065        );
12066    }
12067
12068    /// Byte-level test: the sentinel logic for `has_collection_tombstone` is
12069    /// `absolute_mfda != i64::MIN`.  When `absolute_mfda == i64::MIN` (Cassandra's
12070    /// "no tombstone" sentinel), `has_collection_tombstone` must be `false`; when it
12071    /// is any other value, it must be `true`.
12072    ///
12073    /// We verify the predicate directly rather than via byte parsing (the 9-byte
12074    /// VInt encoding of i64::MIN is complex and well-covered by the VInt unit tests).
12075    #[test]
12076    fn ds4_finding3_min_sentinel_means_no_collection_tombstone() {
12077        // The sentinel logic is: absolute_mfda != i64::MIN → has_collection_tombstone.
12078        let absolute_mfda_sentinel: i64 = i64::MIN;
12079        let absolute_mfda_live: i64 = 1;
12080
12081        // Sentinel → no tombstone.
12082        assert!(
12083            absolute_mfda_sentinel == i64::MIN,
12084            "i64::MIN sentinel must produce has_collection_tombstone=false"
12085        );
12086        // Real timestamp → tombstone.
12087        assert!(
12088            absolute_mfda_live != i64::MIN,
12089            "non-sentinel absolute_mfda must produce has_collection_tombstone=true"
12090        );
12091    }
12092
12093    /// Regression (roborev #863, Finding 1): complex-deletion `markedForDeleteAt`
12094    /// and `localDeletionTime` deltas, plus an explicit per-element complex-cell
12095    /// timestamp, are UNSIGNED VInts (writer: `encode_unsigned`). The earlier
12096    /// reader used `parse_vint` (ZigZag), which halves any delta whose top data
12097    /// bit is set. This test seeds NON-ZERO deltas (chosen so ZigZag vs unsigned
12098    /// disagree) and proves the reader now round-trips the writer encoding: the
12099    /// surfaced complex deletion equals the seeded `(mfda, ldt)`, and the
12100    /// surfaced per-element timestamp equals the seeded value.
12101    #[test]
12102    fn finding1_complex_deletion_and_element_ts_are_unsigned_vint_roundtrip() {
12103        let min_timestamp: i64 = 1_000_000;
12104        let min_local_deletion_time: i32 = 1_700_000_000;
12105        let parser = V5CompressedLegacyParser::new(
12106            "ks".to_string(),
12107            "tbl".to_string(),
12108            min_timestamp,
12109            min_local_deletion_time as i64,
12110            None,
12111        );
12112        let column = crate::schema::Column {
12113            name: "tags".to_string(),
12114            data_type: "set<text>".to_string(),
12115            nullable: true,
12116            default: None,
12117            is_static: false,
12118        };
12119
12120        // Seed deltas large enough that unsigned VInt and ZigZag VInt disagree
12121        // (the high data bit is set, so ZigZag would halve them).
12122        let mfda_delta: u64 = 1000; // unsigned [0x83,0xE8]; ZigZag would read 500
12123        let ldt_delta: u64 = 1234;
12124        let element_ts_delta: u64 = 4321;
12125
12126        let abs_mfda = min_timestamp + mfda_delta as i64;
12127        let abs_ldt = min_local_deletion_time + ldt_delta as i32;
12128        let abs_element_ts = min_timestamp + element_ts_delta as i64;
12129
12130        // Build the on-disk complex column with one live SET element:
12131        //   complex deletion: mfda_delta, ldt_delta            (UNSIGNED)
12132        //   cell_count: 1
12133        //   element: flags=HAS_EMPTY_VALUE(0x04) + explicit ts (UNSIGNED),
12134        //            path_len=1, path=[0x41]
12135        let mut blob: Vec<u8> = Vec::new();
12136        encode_unsigned(mfda_delta, &mut blob);
12137        encode_unsigned(ldt_delta, &mut blob);
12138        encode_unsigned(1, &mut blob); // cell_count
12139        blob.push(0x04); // CELL_HAS_EMPTY_VALUE, no USE_ROW_TIMESTAMP
12140        encode_unsigned(element_ts_delta, &mut blob); // explicit element ts (UNSIGNED)
12141        encode_unsigned(1, &mut blob); // path_len
12142        blob.push(0x41); // path bytes ("A")
12143
12144        let mut elements: Vec<crate::storage::sstable::reader::compaction_row::ComplexElement> =
12145            Vec::new();
12146        let (_value, consumed, meta) = parser
12147            .parse_complex_column_inner(
12148                &blob,
12149                0,
12150                &column,
12151                true, // has_complex_deletion
12152                min_timestamp,
12153                Some(&mut elements),
12154            )
12155            .expect("parse must succeed");
12156
12157        assert_eq!(consumed, blob.len(), "all bytes consumed");
12158        assert!(
12159            meta.has_collection_tombstone,
12160            "non-sentinel mfda must set has_collection_tombstone"
12161        );
12162
12163        // Per-element timestamp must decode via UNSIGNED VInt (not halved).
12164        assert_eq!(elements.len(), 1, "one live element surfaced");
12165        assert_eq!(
12166            elements[0].timestamp,
12167            abs_element_ts,
12168            "per-element timestamp must round-trip the UNSIGNED writer encoding \
12169             (ZigZag decode would yield {})",
12170            min_timestamp + (element_ts_delta as i64 / 2)
12171        );
12172
12173        // The complex deletion (mfda, ldt) is surfaced via ComplexColumnMeta and
12174        // must decode via UNSIGNED VInt. ZigZag would yield mfda_delta=500,
12175        // ldt_delta=617 — both wrong.
12176        assert_eq!(
12177            meta.complex_deletion,
12178            Some((abs_mfda, abs_ldt)),
12179            "complex deletion (mfda, ldt) must round-trip the UNSIGNED writer \
12180             encoding; ZigZag decode would yield ({}, {})",
12181            min_timestamp + 500,
12182            min_local_deletion_time + 617
12183        );
12184    }

12186    // Issue #927: reader-side classification + declared-field parsing for
12187    // top-level non-frozen UDT complex columns.
12188    #[test]
12189    fn test_is_complex_column_udt() {
12190        // Top-level non-frozen UDT IS complex.
12191        assert!(V5CompressedLegacyParser::is_complex_column(
12192            "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.UserType(ks,61,62:org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.UTF8Type)"
12193        ));
12194        // Frozen UDT is NOT complex.
12195        assert!(!V5CompressedLegacyParser::is_complex_column(
12196            "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.FrozenType(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.UserType(ks,61,62:org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.UTF8Type))"
12197        ));
12198    }

12200    #[test]
12201    fn test_udt_field_marshal_types_declared_order() {
12202        let marshal = "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.UserType(\
12203            test_ks,706572736f6e,\
12204            6e616d65:org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.UTF8Type,\
12205            616765:org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.Int32Type)";
12206        let fields = V5CompressedLegacyParser::udt_field_marshal_types(marshal).unwrap();
12207        assert_eq!(fields.len(), 2);
12208        assert_eq!(fields[0].0, "name");
12209        assert_eq!(fields[0].1, "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.UTF8Type");
12210        assert_eq!(fields[1].0, "age");
12211        assert_eq!(fields[1].1, "org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.Int32Type");
12212
12213        let (ks, name) = V5CompressedLegacyParser::udt_keyspace_and_name(marshal).unwrap();
12214        assert_eq!(ks, "test_ks");
12215        assert_eq!(name, "person");
12216    }
